articles.title: National telecoms provider could make $2.7 billion selling recycled copper in AI boom — BT to strip 200,000 tons from legacy network
articles.text:
National telecoms provider could make $2.7 billion selling recycled copper in AI boom — BT to strip 200,000 tons from legacy network
BT's massive network means that it could make a killing out of recycling old cables.
BT, the UK’s largest telecommunications provider, is slowly upgrading its entire network to fiber, with the company looking to move residential endpoints away from copper, and it seems that it will make a killing when it recycles its old cables. According to The Guardian, the company has signed a deal with EMR, one of the largest cable recycling companies in the country, for the recovery of around 200,000 tons of copper over a span of four years. Although the total value of the deal is unclear, the latter has also already paid more than USD 134 million (GBP 99 million) to the telecoms company for a few thousand tons of copper. Aside from the deal with EMR, BT and its subsidiary, Openreach, could also sell the recovered copper directly on the spot market.
More than 22,000 metric tons have already been recovered from the system since BT started its network upgrade, with the metal costing around USD 8,500 per metric ton on the market. If the company sold all that material in the open market, it would have made revenue of USD 187 million. However, the massive AI-driven demand for copper has pushed prices to a record high of more than USD 14,000 per metric ton. The upgrade work is expected to continue well into the 2030s, with Openreach estimating that it could still recover up to 200,000 metric tons of material. That means the company could make an estimated USD 2.7 to 2.8 billion just from the sale of these old network cables.
The AI boom is pushing up demand for several industries — from high-tech products like memory and storage chips and jet engines to “exotic” materials such as rare earth elements and glass cloth fibers. Most people will not equate copper to AI data centers, especially as the PCBs used in their servers often contain so little of the metal, relatively speaking. AI data centers are also switching to optical interconnects and silicon photonics, meaning the internal networks of these data centers will increasingly rely on fiber optics.
However, data centers are forecast to use 194 gigawatts of power by 2035, and all this power can only be transferred via metal cables. While you can also use aluminum wires to transmit power, copper is often the preferred choice for its stability, better electrical conductivity, increased durability, and superior thermal performance. So, as AI hyperscalers expand their operations and build more data centers, the demand for copper wires will also increase accordingly. Utility providers will also need to purchase more cables as they upgrade the grid to deliver the electricity needed by the AI infrastructure.
The AI-powered boom for copper material is a win-win situation for BT, Openreach, and their subscribers. The people will now get end-to-end fiber connections in their homes, hopefully giving them better speed and reliability, while the providers are basically getting a discount on the upgrades that they’re making on their networks.

articles.title: 'It would be really Last of Us' — Asobo Games says it would 'love' to make a potential modern-day sequel to Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy, since Naughty Dog's The Last of Us 'was a big inspiration'
articles.text:
Asobo Games says it would 'love' to make a modern-day entry in the A Plague Tale series, since Naughty Dog's The Last of Us 'was a big inspiration'
That sounds pretty cool
- Asobo Games says it's interested in making a new A Plague Tale game set in the modern day
- The studio says it would be like The Last of Us, since Naughty Dog's game was a "big inspiration"
- Actor Anna Demetriou says a modern-day spin-off would work well since the Macula is "fantastical"
Asobo Games has said it "would love" to make a new A Plague Tale game set in the modern day, since Naughty Dog's The Last of Us influenced the series.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming at Gamescom ahead of the launch of the studio's latest game, Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy, Valérian Robert (lead level designer), Carol Ann Bañuls (lead writer), and actor Anna Demetriou, who played the part of Resonance protagonist Sophia were asked about its next project and confirmed that a modern-day spin-off is something they're asked about frequently.
"Absolutely," Bañuls replied when asked if the setting would be a good pick for Asobo. "Definitely. Personally, I think so. I think it would be great."
Demetriou said, "It's one of the things a lot of people ask me about," with Bañuls adding, "It would be really Last of Us kind of."
Bañuls went on to say that, "Yeah, definitely, because it was a big inspiration. So yeah, if it's in modern days, it would be great."
In the A Plague Tale universe, the Prima Macula is an ancient curse that poisons the blood of certain families and is something that appears in every major A Plague Tale game, including Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy. Demetriou thinks the Macula would work very well in a modern-day setting, because the plague is "fantastical."
"It would be amazing," Demetriou continued, "I would love that to fit into a modern-day setting. Yeah, it would be interesting to see what that would look like. I would love that."

articles.title: Filigran adds attack chaining to OpenAEV for automated penetration testing - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Filigran adds attack chaining to OpenAEV for automated penetration testing
French cybersecurity company Filigran SAS today launched Attack Chaining, a capability in its OpenAEV exposure validation product that links individual attack simulations into a single running path. It ships with OpenAEV v3, out today.
Real intrusions rarely stop at one technique. Reconnaissance finds a target, a credential dump hands over a password and that password opens the next machine, with every step depending on whatever the last one turned up. Single-technique tests and prewritten scenarios catch specific weaknesses well enough. Neither adjusts to what an attacker finds partway through.
Each action feeds the next one. OpenAEV logs what an action turns up as a structured record, whether that is a password, an open port or a set of permissions, and the engine reads it at runtime to work out the next move. A working credential pushes the run deeper into the network. The runs branch where more than one route forward exists, and any control that blocks a step ends the chain there. Teams can assemble that logic themselves out of techniques, payloads or custom actions, then set conditions on each hop.
The run appears on an interactive graph while it happens, tracking pivots and branches from the first action through to the objective. Drilling into a finding shows why an action fired. Filigran said the graph is meant to expose chokepoints, the single step whose removal collapses an entire path, so a team can fix one control instead of triaging the whole chain.
Two modes sit on the same engine. An operator can build the logic and step through execution manually. In agent-led mode the objective and scope are set in plain language, and an artificial intelligence agent builds and adapts the chain itself, generating phishing emails and landing pages for social engineering steps.
“Security validation has to evolve with the way attackers operate,” said co-founder Julien Richard. “The goal is no longer just to prove that we can block individual techniques; it is to understand whether those techniques can be combined into a path that leads to a real compromise.”
Jean-Philippe Salles, vice president of product management at the company, said a validation outcome is “only actionable when security teams can trace the logic that generated it.”
Filigran’s “State of Threat Management” survey of 550 security decision-makers and practitioners found 88% relying on manual processes for offensive attack simulation. The company said 97% also have difficulty working out whether their exposures can be exploited at all.
Four other additions come with v3. A redesigned home dashboard called the Adversarial Exposure Command Center pulls posture, simulation results and detection coverage into a single view. An Adversarial Exposure Score aggregates validation results across exposure sources.
New red-teaming injectors run adversary simulations against chatbots and agents built on large language models, using the same engine that validates endpoint and email defenses. Reporting is now one click to a PDF.
OpenAEV v3 is available to all users today. Attack Chaining is limited to the Enterprise Edition.
Founded in 2022, Filigran has raised more than $100 million in funding, including rounds of $35 million in October 2024 and $58 million in October 2025. Investors in the company include Eurazeo SE, Insight Partners LP, Accel Partners LP and Deutsche Telekom AG.

articles.title: La PS5 nació como consola. Sony está empeñada en que termine siendo también nuestra televisión
articles.text:
La PS5 siempre ha sido una máquina para jugar, pero Sony lleva tiempo intentando que hagamos más cosas con ella. El último paso es Live TV on PS5, un nuevo servicio dentro de la consola que ofrece más de 100 canales gratuitos con publicidad y contenido bajo demanda. De momento está disponible solo en EEUU, aunque Sony ya ha dicho que quiere llevarlo a Canadá y a otros mercados. La idea es sencilla: que la PS5 se convierta en la pantalla de inicio de nuestro entretenimiento, tanto si es gaming como si no.
Televisión gratis... con anuncios. El servicio se puede disfrutar gracias al modelo FAST (Free Ad Supported Streaming Television), es decir, canales emitidos por internet que no requieren pagar una cuota mensual porque se financian con publicidad. Sony incluye contenidos de compañías como Fox, NBCUniversal, Crunchyroll, UFC o Nascar, además de algunos canales propios. No compiten con Netflix, Disney+ o Prime Video de contenidos puramente bajo demanda, sino que recuperan esa "vieja televisión". Es decir: encendemos la tele, elegimos un canal y vemos lo que se está emitiendo en ese momento.
Vuelve el zapping. Parece extraño tras tantos años asumiendo que el streaming nos permitía por fin elegir lo que queríamos ver cuándo y dónde quisiéramos. Aquí Sony confirma una tendencia creciente, porque los canales FAST llevan tiempo teniendo éxito en servicios como Pluto TV, Samsung TV Plus, LG Channels o Tubi. Todos ellos han descubierto que sigue existiendo demanda para este tipo de experiencia de usuario. Una que no te obliga a buscar durante diez minutos una película, sino que hace que disfrutes de la programación ya preestablecida. Y con ese modelo, vuelve probablemente una vieja práctica de los usuarios: el zapping, o cambio frecuente de un canal a otro.
La PS5 como escaparate publicitario. Para Sony el atractivo no está solo en añadir otra función a su consola, porque cada minuto que alguien pasa viendo canales de TV a través de la consola es un minuto que permanece dentro de su ecosistema. Esos canales FAST hacen además crecer el inventario de anuncios que puede mostrar la plataforma gracias a la infraestructura publicitaria de empresas como Publica y PubMatic. Así pues, la idea es monetizar a esa audiencia que puede usar la consola para algo más que jugar o ver contenidos en plataformas de streaming. Es llegar a todos lados, aunque el nicho sea quizá más reducido en este caso.
A Microsoft le salió mal. Es imposible no acordarse de cómo fracasó Microsoft con un intento similar. En 2013 la Xbox One se intentó vender no como una consola de videojuegos, sino como el centro del entretenimiento digital y como una forma perfecta para ver emisiones de televisión gracias a su entrada HDMI. Aquella obsesión de Microsoft hizo que el papel fundamental de la Xbox One como consola de videojuegos se diluyese, algo que aprovechó la PS4 para venderse como rosquillas. Ahora Sony recupera esa idea, pero sin convertirla en protagonista como intentaban en Microsoft: simplemente la añaden como una opción más.
La consola como centro del salón. El objetivo de Sony aquí es el que muchos otros han intentado lograr antes: que un dispositivo se convierta en centro absoluto del entretenimiento en el salón de casa. Las Smart TV han logrado acaparar buena parte de la reproducción de contenidos de streaming y de canales de televisión, y será difícil que alguien encienda la consola "solo para ver TV" cuando podemos hacer lo mismo desde esas Smart TV, pero está claro que en Sony quieren intentarlo.

articles.title: « Dangereux et invisible la nuit » : le nouveau dispositif de cette piste cyclable française tourne au fiasco
articles.text:
L’intention était bonne, l’exécution beaucoup moins. À Strasbourg, un dispositif censé protéger une piste cyclable des deux-roues motorisés a été démonté quelques jours à peine après son installation, tant il s’est révélé dangereux pour les cyclistes eux-mêmes.
Un piège plus qu’une protection
Plutôt qu’une chicane classique avec des barrières, la municipalité avait opté pour un système au sol composé de rails métalliques et d’un potelet central, censé laisser passer les vélos tout en bloquant les deux-roues motorisés. Sur le papier, l’idée pouvait sembler ingénieuse. Dans les faits, le dispositif s’est vite transformé en piège : de nuit, les rails au sol devenaient quasiment invisibles, sans aucune signalétique pour inciter les cyclistes à ralentir suffisamment avant de s’y engager.
Pire encore, l’obstacle censé bloquer les deux-roues motorisés se contournait sans difficulté, à gauche comme à droite. « Tu peux y aller même en voiture », ironisait un internaute sur Facebook, montage à l’appui. « L’idée à la con ! », résumait un autre, dans une avalanche de commentaires moqueurs repérés par nos confrères de Presse-citron.
L’alerte vient d’une association de cyclistes
C’est l’association CADR 67, qui milite pour la promotion du vélo à Strasbourg, qui a le premier signalé le problème, le 19 août, sur sa page Facebook. Elle y pointait un dispositif « totalement invisible de nuit », un franchissement des rails « plus que dangereux », et un potelet installé en plein milieu de la piste qui « risque de faire mal » en cas de chute.
Face à la polémique naissante, la Ville de Strasbourg a fini par confirmer, auprès d’Actu Strasbourg, que l’aménagement visible sur les photos était en réalité incomplet. « Le dispositif n’aurait pas dû être installé en l’état car il est pour l’heure incomplet, dû à des aléas de chantier (retard d’approvisionnement). Les élus ont donc demandé son retrait sans délai », a expliqué la municipalité. La version définitive doit inclure des barrières latérales pour empêcher tout contournement, un système réfléchissant pour la visibilité nocturne, et un panneau invitant les usagers à ralentir.
Une patate chaude que personne ne veut porter
L’affaire a rapidement viré au règlement de comptes politique. Sur Facebook, Landdry Augier de Lajallet, adjoint à la maire chargé des mobilités, a pris la parole pour se démarquer du dispositif : « L’exécutif actuel n’a jamais validé un tel dispositif. Ni l’adjointe de quartier ni moi-même n’avons été informés de cette pose et nous n’avons validé ni son emplacement ni les modalités précises de son installation. »
Une déclaration qui n’a pas manqué de faire réagir Pierre Ozenne, ancien adjoint en charge de ces dossiers sous la précédente municipalité, interrogé par France 3 Grand Est. « C’est fort de café », s’est-il agacé, avant d’ajouter : « Si l’actuel adjoint aux mobilités découvre l’aménagement après cinq mois dans ses fonctions, je m’inquiète pour lui. C’est facile d’accuser l’ancienne municipalité quand un aménagement ne l’arrange pas. » Lui non plus n’assume pas avoir validé ce dispositif, qu’il juge sans « sa place à un tel endroit ». Résultat, impossible à ce jour de savoir qui a réellement donné le feu vert à cet aménagement.
Et maintenant ?
Le dispositif a bel et bien été retiré, ne laissant dans le sol que les trous ayant servi à fixer les rails. La question de fond, elle, reste entière : comment sécuriser cette piste cyclable, régulièrement empruntée par des deux-roues motorisés, sans mettre en danger les cyclistes qu’elle est censée protéger ?
Dès la rentrée, Landdry Augier de Lajallet et Céline Geissmann, élue de quartier, doivent rencontrer les habitants et les associations cyclistes pour reprendre le travail sur un aménagement mieux pensé. CADR 67 confirme avoir déjà été recontactée en vue d’une réunion.

articles.title: GTA 6 en Colombia: esto es lo que podría costar su edición estándar y Ultimate
articles.text:
El lanzamiento de Grand Theft Auto VI se perfila como uno de los hitos más esperados del año en la industria del videojuego, y ya despierta una ola de consultas sobre su precio en Colombia y el contenido de cada edición.
El interés es comprensible: GTA 6 promete una experiencia renovada con una historia profunda, mejoras técnicas y una jugabilidad que apunta a superar todo lo visto en la saga hasta la fecha.
PUBLICIDAD
¿Cuándo sale GTA 6 y en qué consolas estará disponible?
Rockstar Games confirmó que GTA 6 se lanzará mundialmente el 19 de noviembre de 2026 para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S. Los usuarios de estas consolas serán los primeros en acceder al título, mientras que no hay fecha confirmada para PC ni para otras plataformas como Nintendo Switch 2.
La preventa estará habilitada desde el 12 de noviembre, aunque esta opción estará limitada a algunos usuarios exclusivos. Tras la publicación del adelanto extendido y la confirmación oficial de la fecha de estreno, los jugadores buscan anticipar cuánto deberán invertir para experimentar la nueva entrega de Rockstar desde el primer día.
PUBLICIDAD
Precios estimados para Colombia: edición estándar y Ultimate
Aunque Rockstar aún no ha publicado los precios oficiales para el mercado colombiano, la tendencia global y los reportes de la industria apuntan a que la edición estándar de GTA 6 rondará los 79,99 dólares. Al tipo de cambio actual, esto equivaldría a aproximadamente $252.600 COP, aunque la cifra podría variar según el valor del dólar al momento de la compra y las políticas de cada tienda.
Por su parte, la edición Ultimate se estima que costará 99,99 dólares, es decir, cerca de $316.000 COP. Esta versión suele incluir contenido adicional como paquetes de armas, atuendos exclusivos, vehículos especiales y acceso anticipado a ciertas misiones o expansiones, todo pensado para maximizar la experiencia de juego y recompensar a los fans más apasionados.
PUBLICIDAD
¿Qué novedades trae GTA 6 y por qué genera tanta expectativa?
El tráiler de GTA 6, con una duración de poco más de 25 minutos, mostró una Vice City reinventada y los primeros detalles de la aventura que protagonizan Jason y Lucía. Las novedades van más allá de lo visual: el juego incorpora cambios de personaje en tiempo real, mayor profundidad en la relación entre los protagonistas y un sistema de personalización física que incluye alimentación, ejercicio y hábitos que afectan tanto la apariencia como las capacidades de los personajes.
Entre los aspectos destacados del avance:
- Interacciones más realistas con NPC: Portar armas a la vista provoca reacciones inmediatas y una respuesta policial más dinámica.
- Cambios de personaje fluidos: Jason y Lucía pueden alternar roles y tareas a lo largo del mapa y durante las misiones.
- Narrativa romántica y criminal: Es la primera vez que la franquicia explora una historia de pareja con química evidente, inspirada en “Bonnie y Clyde”.
- Personalización avanzada: Los hábitos y el estado físico de los protagonistas afectan la jugabilidad y la percepción de los NPC.
- Crítica social: El juego satiriza la cultura actual, abordando temas como la publicidad invasiva, las redes sociales y la televisión.
¿Por qué los precios pueden variar en Colombia?
El valor final de GTA 6 en Colombia dependerá de varios factores: la cotización del dólar, la política de precios de las tiendas físicas y digitales, los impuestos y la demanda. Además, las ediciones especiales o de coleccionista podrían tener un valor superior y disponibilidad limitada.
PUBLICIDAD
Quienes deseen asegurar su copia desde el primer día deben estar atentos a la apertura de la preventa y considerar los posibles costos extra por reservas anticipadas o contenido exclusivo.
La llegada de GTA 6 promete transformar el panorama del gaming en Colombia y en toda América Latina. El precio de lanzamiento, aunque elevado, refleja la tendencia global de los grandes estrenos y el salto tecnológico que supone esta nueva entrega.
PUBLICIDAD
La decisión entre la edición estándar y la Ultimate dependerá del nivel de interés y las expectativas de cada jugador, pero en ambos casos, la experiencia promete ser una de las más completas y ambiciosas de la década.

articles.title: Le Français Naval Group et la Suède scellent un accord naval express en pleine tension régionale
articles.text:
Naval Group a signé lundi un contrat historique avec la Suède pour quatre frégates de défense et d'intervention. Un accord scellé en un temps record, entre Emmanuel Macron et Ulf Kristersson, pour renforcer la Marine Royale suédoise dès 2030.
Ce depuis Stockholm, le lundi 31 août, qu'Emmanuel Macron et le Premier ministre suédois Ulf Kristersson ont été témoins d'un moment fort de la coopération militaire franco-suédoise. L'industriel français Naval Group, qui fait partie des prochains maîtres d'œuvre du futur porte-avions français, et le ministère suédois de la Défense ont officiellement signé l'acquisition de quatre frégates de défense et d'intervention (FDI), à peine quatre mois après l'annonce de leur sélection. Un timing presque record qui montre à la fois l'urgence stratégique ressentie à Stockholm et la confiance accordée à un navire déjà pris en main par la France et la Grèce.
La Marine Royale suédoise mise sur la technologie française pour ses futures frégates
Le contrat a été paraphé en présence des plus hautes autorités des deux pays, signe de l'importance accordée à cet accord. Côté suédois, Mikael Granholm, le directeur général du FMV, l'agence en charge du matériel militaire, représentait Stockholm. Pierre Éric Pommellet, le PDG de Naval Group, a signé pour la partie française, épaulé par le soutien actif de l'État tout au long des négociations exclusives. Le groupe devient ainsi le partenaire stratégique désigné de la Marine Royale suédoise, chargé de renforcer et de moderniser rapidement sa flotte, dans un contexte opérationnel tendu que tout le monde connaît.
Ce qui frappe surtout, c'est la vitesse d'exécution des échanges. À peine quatre mois séparent l'annonce de ce choix et la signature effective du contrat. Un délai particulièrement court pour ce type de programme militaire, généralement soumis à de longues tractations, et qui confirme encore une fois la volonté commune d'avancer vite
La Marine Royale suédoise ne patientera pas si longtemps, puisque la livraison de la première frégate est programmée pour 2030. C'est long, et court à la fois, pour un tel bâtiment fabriqué sur le Vieux continent. Le calendrier est considéré comme tenable d'ailleurs, puisque la FDI n'est plus un concept depuis longtemps. Deux exemplaires ont déjà rejoint les flottes française et grecque, sur une ligne de production dont l'efficacité est désormais éprouvée.
Une frégate déjà éprouvée par la France et la Grèce
Sur le plan technique, la FDI est un vrai petit bijou. On parle ici d'une frégate de dernière génération, déjà prête au combat et qui embarque des capacités antiaériennes robustes, articulées autour du système de missiles Aster (en grande partie construit par MBDA et Thales, via le consortium Eurosam), un atout de poids, forcément.
La frégate, pensée pour affronter les environnements les plus exigeants, a été conçue pour tenir aussi bien face aux eaux du Grand Nord qu'aux caprices de l'Atlantique Nord ou de la Baltique. De quoi offrir à la Suède des capacités élargies pour soutenir son rôle clé dans les opérations navales interalliées, notamment au sein de l'OTAN.
Au-delà de la vente de navires, Naval Group espère nouer un partenariat industriel durable avec la Suède, en y incluant notamment des transferts de savoir-faire vers ses partenaires suédois, une façon aussi de réaffirmer, aux yeux des partenaires dans la région, la coopération industrielle navale à l'échelle européenne. « C'est un honneur de mettre notre savoir-faire au service de la souveraineté et de la supériorité navale de la Marine Royale suédoise », a résumé Pierre Éric Pommellet. Voilà un nouvel accord qui va dans le bon sens pour la France.

articles.title: "Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations" Devs Hit 17-Hour Days During Crunch Before Layoffs
articles.text:
Monday, August 31st 2026
	
	
	
	
"Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations" Devs Hit 17-Hour Days During Crunch Before Layoffs
Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations is the only story expansion ever launched for The Dark Ages, and it was well-liked by the community, scoring a "Very Positive" review rating on Steam. However, as revealed in a new Insider Gaming interview, the expansion's quality came at a cost to its developers. 
According to former Id Software developer, Andrew Willis, "There were two months where I was working something like at least 12 hours every day. I know I hit 17 a couple of days. It was brutal, and the majority of the game got made in three or four months." He adds that the crunch affected everyone on the team, however, he explained that the crunch wasn't mandated by company policy, but that developers were given a workload that was impossible to complete without the crunch.
It's a really blurry line. You get loaded up with 60 hours of work in a week, and what do you do? You can make a version of that work that would probably be just barely passable, but is that what you want to put your name on? It's almost this thing like, at the level of quality that the players expect and that you expect from yourself, it's kind of like almost pseudo-induced crunch.
The day before the launch of the Revelations expansion, Xbox laid off swathes of staff, during which Id Software was decimated, losing nearly half of its workforce. Willis was among the workers laid off in that Xbox Reset.
You spend so much of your energy and hours of your life, and sacrifice a bunch of things, to get something out the door, and then they lay you off the day before. It's such a wild feeling.
Following the Xbox layoffs in July, another former Id Software worker, Derek Best, posted on LinkedIn that his former team had been reduced to just one artist "with no lead or producer," and corroborating Willis's account of the Doom expansion crunch.

articles.title: The Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam is a fabulously versatile air fryer that surprised me with consistently great results
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer is a wonderfully versatile appliance, producing excellent results no matter the cooking mode you decide to use. The large basket is great for family-sized portions, the steam functionality means you don’t need yet another appliance in your kitchen, while the steamfry mode produces some of the best chicken wings I’ve ever made.
Pros
- +Excellent air fry, steamfry and steam modes
- +Consistently great results across all food types
- +Set of tongs included in the box
Cons
- -You can get big-basket fryers for less
- -The glossy top shows dirt easily
- -Large footprint means you need lots of counter space
Why you can trust TechRadar
Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer: 30-second review
The Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer is an air fryer and then some.
Sure it does a great job at being an air fryer, and so it should for the premium price tag it comes in at. The sizable 9.5L basket offers plenty of space for family-sized portions, while the handy divider allows you to cook two different foods, at differing durations and temperatures, simultaneously. It’s pretty par for the course these days, but the 5000 Series Megabasket is only just getting started.
Things are turned up a notch with the steam functionality Philips has built in. Being able to perfectly steam vegetables, fish and dumplings without the need for a separate appliance saves on counter and cupboard space, and the results here are just as good as the air fryer.
However, the versatility is kicked into overdrive with the streamfry function, allowing you to bring the best of both worlds to your food. The crispy finish of an air fryer combined with the moisture locking abilities of steam. The result? Some of the best chicken wings I’ve ever made.
All this functionality not only comes at a cost to your wallet, but also your counter top. This is a wide, tall air fryer that requires plenty of space — especially when using the steam or steamfry function, as the water vapor vents from the rear.
I’m a big fan of Philips’ controls though. The touch buttons are intuitively laid out, with easily recognizable icons that require little reference to the manual to work out - that can’t be said of all air fryer brands.
The basket, trays and divider are dishwasher safe, and you can also use the steam function to give the appliance its own steam clean. You will need to give the top a wipe every now and then, as the glossy finish attracts grime — but it’s a minor point in what is an overwise excellent appliance.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Whether you’re looking to make cakes, cookies, sausages, chicken wings, fish, vegetables, fries, dumplings or pretty much anything else, the Philips 5000 Series Megabasket delivers consistently great results.
Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer price and availability
- At £259.99 (about $350 / AU$490), it’s at the premium end of the air fryer market
- Available in the UK, but not in the US or Australia
The Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer price is £259.99 (about $350 / AU$490), putting it at the premium end of the market, and pits it against the Ninja Foodi FlexBasket in the larger-basket arena.
There are cheaper, big-basket air fryers on the market that also perform well, with the Philips 1000 Series Dual Basket and Tower Elite 11 Litre Flexi Drawer both coming in at around half the price of the 5000 Series.
This exact model (the NA465) isn’t available in the US and Australia, with these regions instead getting the $349.99 / AU$499 5000 Series Dual-Basket Airfryer with Steam (NA551) with two separate drawers, rather than one large one.
- Value score: 4/5
Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer: specifications
| Review Model | NA465/92 | 
| Number of baskets | 1 | 
| Number of cooking programs | 8 | 
| Cooking programs | Frozen fries, mixed vegetables, chicken drumsticks, tray bakes, fish, dumplings, reheat, favorite | 
| Extra functions | Steam, Steamfry, Shake reminder, SteamClean, Adjustable basket size | 
| Smart control | No | 
| Wattage | 2750W | 
| Capacity | 9.5L | 
| Temperature range | 40-200 degrees C | 
| Time range | 1-180 minutes | 
| Dimensions | 496mm (L) x 329mm (W) x 355mm (H) | 
| Dishwasher-safe | Yes | 
| Weight | 8.2kg | 
Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer: design
- Wide and tall, but for good reason
- Set of tongs included in the box is a nice touch
- Touch controls are easy to understand and well laid out
The Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer is big, it’s almost as if a UFO has landed on your worktop. Wide and tall, it dominates the kitchen counter — but for good reason.
The spacious 9.5L basket provides great flexibility as one large cooking space big enough for 2.5kg of fries, 1.9kg of ribs, or whole chicken, but can easily be split into 3L and 6L baskets with the included divider. This allows you to cook two separate things, at different temperatures and durations, at the same time.
You can even just choose to use one of the sides only, saving on power consumption when cooking smaller portions.
The only small issue with the basket is its handles, which consist of two small protrusions on either side. It means you have to use two hands to open the drawer, and to lift and carry it.
When the basket is fully loaded with food, it’s heavy so you’ll be using two hands anyway, but for times when you want to quickly check on cooking progress, you can’t open it with just one.
The additional height of this air fryer is down to the inclusion of Philips’ clever steam function, giving you more ways to cook from a single machine. You can steam food in this air fryer, as well as 'Steamfry', which combines both cooking methods.
What this means is you’ll need to consider where you want the air fryer to go, and whether you have suitable space for this 496mm x 329mm x 355mm model to fit - especially if you have low-hung wall cabinets over your worktops.
Hot air vents from the rear of the machine, so you need to leave space between it and the wall, and when using the steam function water vapor will also rise from the back of the machine.
The one meter power cable will be long enough for most kitchen setups, and the Philips 5000 Series comes with a clip-on cable tidy for the rear to keep things neat if you like to store your air fryer in a cupboard when not in use. Although, it’ll need to be a sizable cupboard.
A nice inclusion in the box was a set of tongs, a particularly useful addition when cooking with an air fryer, as it makes tossing food and removing it from the basket much easier.
There’s also a paper manual in the box that covers all the basics, mainly via pictorial guides, but for those who want a more detailed breakdown of functionality you’ll need to download the free HomeID app on your phone.
What isn’t made obvious out of the box is the need to run the air fryer empty initially to burn off the protective shipping coating.
Diving into the app deeper, Philips advises to wash the basket and accessories with a soft sponge, water and washing up liquid, dry them, and then run the air fryer empty, a 200C, for the maximum cook time (which for this model is 180 minutes).
That seemed excessive to me. I did an initial four minute cycle at 180C, allowed the basket to cool down, and then washed it, the divider, and the crisp trays, and set the machine at 200C for 50 minutes. The smell did get very strong during this time, but it did the trick.
When I came to cook with the air fryer for the first time, there was a slight smell during cooking, but it didn’t transfer to the food.
The controls here are excellent, just as they are on the Philips 4000 Series Stacked Dual Basket Air Fryer. The illuminated touch buttons on the top of the machine make it really easy to select the basket size you wish to cook with, and to set the temperature and time.
The only slight negative against this design is the glossy black surface quickly gets dirty, and shows up finger smudges. Plus, if your hands aren’t clean it can sometimes struggle to pick up your presses.
There are a number of presets to pick from too (frozen fries, mixed vegetables, chicken drumsticks, tray bakes, fish, dumplings, reheat), if you want to just press and play.
While the presets are useful, I did find during my weeks of testing they sometimes needed to be fine tuned to my preferred cook level. It’s all part of the early trial and error of using a new air fryer to work out the times and temps that work best for the food you’re cooking regularly.
When it comes to cleaning, the good news is the basket, trays and divider are all dishwasher safe. If you don’t have access to one, hand washing also works - although the sheer size of the basket means it can be tricky to clean in smaller sinks.
Another nice feature is the steam cleaning function. Simple to enact - just make sure the water reservoir is full and select the steam clean mode - it does a good job of loosening grease and marks in the basket. It means you can just run a cloth or paper towel round the basket and it’s pretty much clean. No need for hard scrubbing. It’s not going to remove stubborn marks or pieces of food debris, but it’s a handy option when only lightly used.
- Design score: 4.5/5
Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer: performance
Performance
- Steam and SteamFry functions are excellent
- Quiet operation
- Great all-round cooking performance
The Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer is one of the quieter models I’ve tested, making it an excellent cooking companion, especially in smaller kitchens as the noise doesn’t dominate the room.
As well as the presets, there are a couple of other useful features here. First is the shake reminder, where the 5000 Series will work out how many shake intervals are required based on the cook duration you’ve set, and will beep at set times to alert you to the fact you need to shake or turn the food in the basket.
This allows you to ensure an even cook, be it fries, chicken wings, vegetables, or pretty much anything else you’re cooking. If you’re not using a preset, you will need to manually enable the shake reminder by pressing the icon on the control panel.
The second handy feature is sync, allowing you to utilize the dual basket setup, and cook two different foods, at different temperatures, for different lengths of time, but have them finish at the same time.
The air fryer delays the start of the side with the shorter cook time, starting it when its duration matches that left on the other side. It’s simple to set up, and works really nicely.
The 5000 Series Megabasket is certainly well equipped, but how does it actually perform when it comes to cooking food?
As this is a large basket air fryer, and given my penchant for consuming pizza, I decided to kick things off with a simple, store-bought margarita. When I reviewed the Tower Elite 11 Litre Flexi Drawer, I was able to fit a whole round (admittedly small) pizza into the basket.
With the Philips, the basket isn’t as deep, which meant I had to slice my circular pizza in half and lay the two halves at an angle in the basket. It worked fine, but if this pizza was frozen rather than fresh, I would be forced to use the oven.
After warming up the air fryer for a couple of minutes first, I cooked the pizza at 190C for nine minutes. It turned out this was a minute or so too long, as the topping came out a little overdone. It was still fine to eat, but a glass window on the basket would have allowed me to keep a better eye on the progress being made. Alas, there’s no window on the basket.
I returned a few days later however with an oval shaped pizza. This easily sat in the basket, and having learned my lesson I cooked it for seven minutes at 180C.
The final cook was much better, with a crisp base and juicy toppings, although I noticed the part of the pizza towards the back of the basket was slightly more cooked than that at the front.
You don’t always get a completely even cook from this air fryer, but it wasn’t a problem during the weeks of cooking I did.
Fries came out great with this air fryer, whether they were frozen or fresh. Crispy on the outside, fluffy in the middle, and using the frozen fries setting I got automatic reminders to shake the basket a few times during the 24 minute cook at 200C.
For the fresh fries I had to set the temperature (200C) and time (21 minutes) manually, as well as enable the shake reminder. Still, the results were great.
Baking is another highlight when using the Philips 5000 air fryer, with a simple banana bread recipe producing a moist inside, crunchy-topped loaf with an excellent texture. I cooked it at 160C for 25 minutes, and then 20 minutes at 140C.
I also produced delicious, gooey-centered chocolate cookies, with an eight minute bake at 175C doing the job nicely. The chicken breasts, mixed green vegetables and sausages I also cooked using the air fryer mode all came out well.
But air frying is only part of the story. The reservoir atop this device is the signal this device has more tricks up its sleeve. The Steamfry function, that utilizes both the air frying components along with generating steam, aims to lock in moisture and enhance tenderness, creating juicy and golden textures. Basically, the best of air frying and steaming in one.
And it works really well. I used the entire basket to Streamfry large, hand-seasoned chicken wings on the chicken preset (32 minutes at 200C).
During the cook there are periods of air frying and periods of steaming, the latter of which are obvious as you can hear the steam being produced, and see it vent out the rear of the machine. If you have it up close to a wall, or under a kitchen cabinet, expect significant condensation. I’d recommend giving it plenty of breathing room when using a steam function.
The results were superb. Wonderfully crisp skin, and juicy meat made for a delicious dinner, and had me returning the next day for lunch to cook the rest of the wings I didn’t need the night before.
And when it comes to solely steaming, the 5000 Megabasket performs well yet again. Popping a selection of Japanese chicken and vegetable gyoza into the right side of the basket (steam and steamfry are available in the whole basket, or the right side only) and using the preset dumpling mode produced perfectly steamed, silky pillows.
A word of warning on the presets though, they aren’t a sure-fire win every time. When I cooked some green beans, broccoli, sugar snap peas, I split the batch between the two compartments. The veg I put in the smaller side I air fried, while I opted for steam on the larger side.
I selected the vegetables preset for both, which gave me settings of 200C for 30 minutes for the air fried veg, and 100C for 14 minutes for the steamed side. I also selected the sync option, so both sides would finish at the same time. However, at the first shake reminder for the air fried side (after 15 minutes) it was clear my veg was already overcooked.
I completed the full cycle for both sides, and the air fried veg was cremated. Thankfully, the steamed side had cooked very well, with tender broccoli stems, beans and peas.
Put bigger, chunkier pieces of veg in the air fry side (such as roughly chopped carrots and parsnips) and the preset is closer to what you need. It’s a good reminder that you need to spend time with your air fryer in the initial weeks to find out which settings work best for the food you cook - even with premium models such as the 5000 series.
- Performance score: 4.5/5
Should you buy the Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer?
| Report card |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attribute | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | There’s a premium price tag, but you’re getting a premium product. The 5000 Series Megabasket is packed full with features, includes a set of tongs in the box, and is well built. | 4/5 | 
| Design | If you have the space, this is a premium air fryer with excellent controls and plenty of features. The set of tongs included in the box is a nice touch, but the handles on the basket can be a little awkward. | 4.5/5 | 
| Performance | Whether you air fry, steamfry or steam, you’ll get excellent results from the 5000 series. Its easy operation and impressive versatility delivers consistently great cooks. | 4.5/5 | 
Buy it if
You want excellent versatility
The steam and streamfry modes on offer here are excellent, so if you often use steam to cook, want an additional healthy way to cook, or want to reduce the number of appliances in your kitchen, the 5000 Series has you covered. The removable divider provides more flexibility too, with the ability to cook two separate foods simultaneously. You even get a set of tongs included in the box.
You want to feed a family
The large 9.5L ‘Megabasket’ provides plenty of space, allowing you to easily cook family-sized portions. It’s great for a large helping of chips, or a bunch of chicken wings.
You want consistent, delicious results
The Philips 5000 Series Megabasket produces great results in all cooking modes, and you’ll be thoroughly impressed with what it can do. From fluffy cake and gooey cookies, to crispy and moist chicken wings, crunchy fries, and wonderfully steamed veg.
Don’t buy it if
You’re on a budget
If you’re after a large capacity air fryer that still performs well and costs significantly less than this Philips, there are cheaper options available. They won’t look quite as sleek, nor will their controls be so well thought out, but you can pick up a budget, large basket air fryer for around half the price of the 5000 series.
You’re only after air frying capabilities
The steam and streamfry modes are excellent, but if you don’t see yourself ever using them, save yourself some money and go for an air fryer without them.
You’re limited on counter space
The Philips 5000 Series Megabasket is a big airfryer. Wide and tall, it will dominate small kitchens with limited counter space. It also needs to be positioned away from wall-mounted units and walls, to allow the hot air and the steam to properly vent from the rear.
Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer: also consider
Ninja Foodi FlexBasket Dual Air Fryer
An immense air fryer with one of the largest capacities on the market and the flexibility to cook in either two independent zones or convert the drawer into one tray for larger meals.
For more information, check out our full Ninja Foodi FlexBasket Dual Air Fryer review
Tower Elite 11 Litre Flexi Drawer
If you’re after a big-basket air fryer on a budget, the Tower Elite 11 Litre Flexi Drawer has a larger basket than the Philips and is almost half the price. There’s no steam function here though.
For more information, check out our full Tower Elite 11 Litre Flexi Drawer review
How I tested the Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer
- I used the Philips 5000 Series air fryer for multiple weeks in my kitchen
- I cooked a wide variety of food with it, including fries, cakes, vegetables, pizza and meat
- I tested the various cooking functions, and the cleaning process
I spent multiple weeks using the Philips 5000 Series Megabasket with Steam Air Fryer in my kitchen. During that time I cooked using the air fry, steamfry and steam settings, and used the various preset modes, along with manual setting.
I cooked a wide variety of food, including baking cakes and cookies, air frying chips, pizzas, sausages and chicken, steaming vegetables and dumplings, and steam frying chicken wings.
I also tested the steam cleaning function, and cleaned the basket, trays and divider both by hand, and with the dishwasher.

articles.title: Google TV Streamer : +50% de prix aux États-Unis, c’est le moment (ou jamais) d’acheter en France
articles.text:
C’est désormais une petite rengaine en 2026 que l’on répète à l’envi à ses proches et à nos lecteurs : si un produit tech vous intéresse maintenant et que son prix vous paraît correct, n’attendez pas trop, car le tarif va très certainement augmenter.
Loin de nous l’idée de pousser à la consommation, mais après tout, si vous êtes certain-e-s de votre choix, autant payer le moins cher possible.
Ce qui nous amène à l’augmentation du jour. Le Google Streamer TV est une excellente box TV Android, une des façons les plus haut de gamme d’apporter Google TV sur un téléviseur en 2026 et sans doute ma seule alternative crédible à l’Apple TV 4K et la vieillissante (mais néanmoins excellente) Nvidia Shield TV.
Mais qui dit haut de gamme dit un prix à sa sortie qui pouvait, à juste titre, faire grincer des dents. De quoi en motiver plus d’un à attendre une promo en somme.
Une hausse de 50 %
Mais comme nous sommes en 2026 en pleine RAMpocalyspe, c’est plutôt l’inverse qui se produit. Le prix de l’appareil outre-Atlantique a connu une hausse de 50 % de son tarif, passant de 99,99 dollars à 149,99 dollars.
La firme de Mountain View a partagé un commentaire auprès du média américain 9to5Google :
« En raison de la hausse des coûts des composants, nous ajustons le prix aux États-Unis de certaines caméras Google Nest, de certaines sonnettes et du streamer Google TV 4K, à compter du 31 août. Nous restons déterminés à fournir à nos clients une sécurité domestique intelligente de pointe et des mises à jour continues des fonctionnalités. »
En France le prix n’a pas encore bougé
Nous avons toutefois un peu de chance dans notre malchance. Si tout a tendance à augmenter en ce moment, comme le prix de la configuration de base des Pixel 11, par exemple, dans le cadre d’une hausse de prix sur un produit dont le cycle de vie est déjà bien entamé, la hausse a souvent lieu d’abord dans son marché domestique avant d’être répercutée dans le reste du monde. Parfois (touchons du bois), la hausse n’a même pas lieu ailleurs, mais ne rêvons pas trop.
Le Google Streamer TV intégrant 4 Go de RAM et 32 Go de stockage, il subit ici comme n’importe quel produit intégrant de la mémoire la hausse faramineuse des prix de la RAM.
En Europe et a fortiori en Europe, cette hausse de 50 dollars devrait se traduire à minima par une hausse de 50 euros, ce qui se traduirait par un tarif de 170 euros, bien trop élevé pour ce type d’appareil, qui possède des alternatives bons marchés, comme la Xiaomi TV Box S (3d Gen).

articles.title: DataAgent raises $10M to let AI fix production faults inside Kubernetes clusters - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
DataAgent raises $10M to let AI fix production faults inside Kubernetes clusters
Israeli startup DataAgent Ltd. formally launched today with $10 million in pre-seed funding and a platform that repairs production faults inside a customer’s own Kubernetes clusters.
DataAgent plans to spend the money to accelerate customer adoption in North America. Ishay Yaari and Nati Shalom started the company in January as chief executive and chief technology officer. Both formerly worked at open-source cloud orchestration platform company Cloudify Platform Ltd. Dell Technologies Inc. acquired the business in 2023 for a reported $100 million.
Conventional observability tools detect a fault and hand it to an engineer to investigate. That model requires a paid second copy of the customer’s logs and metrics shipped to a vendor’s cloud, and the bill grows along with the system it watches. Grafana Labs Inc. said in its 2025 observability survey that such spending averages 17% of total compute infrastructure spending. The most common answer was 10%.
DataAgent reverses the sequence. Its agents read live system state, topology and configuration drift where the data already sits, work out what caused an incident and apply a fix the customer has pre-approved through guardrails it defines itself. The deeper root-cause analysis runs afterward, offline, after service is restored. The company said that ordering is what shortens mean time to resolution.
The software runs inside cloud-native control planes and sits above whatever monitoring stack a customer already has, rather than replacing it. Data goes outward only when a fault needs deeper inspection. The agent itself is open source and can be run standalone at no cost, with a paid software-as-a-service tier for fleet management and orchestration. DataAgent said that design answers enterprise resistance to running closed software in production.
“In 10 years, no one has ever heard an engineering leader say their organization’s observability costs went down and that is no accident,” Yaari said. “When a vendor’s revenue is your data ingest, it cannot cut your bill without cutting its own.”
Shalom said the industry has spent 15 years “building better ways to watch production and charging more for it every year,” and that adding artificial intelligence copilots to that model has not changed the outcome. He described autonomy as an architectural shift rather than a feature layered onto observability.
The platform earns its independence in stages. During onboarding, a discovery phase shows customers which classes of failure the software can already fix on its own. A timeline covers the rest. Faults the software has not been proven correct on are routed to a human. Approved fixes deploy through a customer’s existing change management process or a single command-line instruction.
MizMaa Ventures Ltd. and Alicorn Venture Partners led the pre-seed round. MizMaa also backed Tenet Security Inc., which launched in June with $6 million in seed funding to police rogue AI agents at runtime. DataAgent said customers who run its platform alongside their existing tools can cut up to 90% of their observability bill.

articles.title: Chinese court freezes $318 million in Nexperia assets as Wingtech presses to regain control — Dutch chipmaker says seizures won't affect day-to-day operations
articles.text:
Chinese court freezes $318 million in Nexperia assets as Wingtech presses to regain control — Dutch chipmaker says seizures won't affect day-to-day operations
Wingtech's 8 billion yuan lawsuit awaits trial.
A court in Dongguan, China, has frozen 2.14 billion yuan (roughly $318 million) in assets held by Dutch chipmaker Nexperia and its equipment arm, ITEC, according to a filing that Chinese parent company Wingtech Technology submitted to the Shanghai Stock Exchange today. The order covers Nexperia's equity in five Chinese subsidiaries and runs until August 2029, handing Wingtech fresh leverage in its year-long fight to regain control of Nexperia that Dutch authorities stripped from it in 2025.
The Dongguan Intermediate People's Court civil ruling, which Wingtech said it received on August 28, freezes Nexperia B.V.'s 100% stakes in Nexperia Semiconductor (China), Nexperia Semiconductor (Wuxi), and Nexperia Semiconductor (Shanghai), plus its 99% holding in Nexperia Semiconductor Technology (Shanghai). A fifth order covers ITEC B.V.'s full stake in its equipment subsidiary, ITEC Technology (Wuxi). The underlying case, an 8 billion yuan (roughly $1.19 billion) damages claim that Wingtech filed in May against Nexperia, its holding company, ITEC, and three executives, hasn't gone to trial.
Those five entities are the same Chinese operations that stopped following instructions from Nexperia's Nijmegen headquarters in October last year, when Nexperia accused them of refusing payment for delivered wafers and opening unauthorized bank accounts. Nexperia says it has no control over those businesses today, and the court order now bars any sale, transfer, or restructuring of their equity for three years. Any settlement of the wider ownership dispute that involves carving up Nexperia's China assets can't close before August 2029 unless the Dongguan court first suspends the asset freeze.
In that May complaint, Wingtech named chief legal officer Ruben Lichtenberg, chief operating officer Achim Kempe, and Stefan Tilger, the CFO who has led Nexperia as interim chief executive since a Dutch court suspended founder Zhang Xuezheng last October. It alleges that the trio implemented or helped enforce discriminatory restrictive measures imposed by the Netherlands, whose government briefly seized control of Nexperia before suspending its intervention last November.
The total value of the frozen assets exceeds Wingtech’s entire first-half revenue, with the company reporting 1.51 billion yuan in H1 2026 sales, down more than 90% year-over-year, alongside a 406 million yuan net loss. Its shares trade under Shanghai's *ST delisting-risk designation after auditor RSM couldn't verify 57% of its assets, most of which are inside Nexperia entities that Wingtech can't access. Nexperia China, meanwhile, has been qualifying domestic wafer suppliers and producing chips on 12-inch wafers.
In a statement to Bloomberg, Nexperia said that the measures relate "solely to entities in China that have been operating outside Nexperia BV's governance structures" and don't affect its day-to-day operations, management, or business continuity.

articles.title: Arsenal vs Aston Villa por la Premier League en Fútbol Libre: una búsqueda que esconde malware
articles.text:
Seguir partidos en vivo de la Premier League como Arsenal vs Aston Villa en aplicaciones piratas como fútbol Libre puede exponer a los dispositivos a una amplia gama de amenazas digitales, como malware, robo de datos y fraudes.
Para prevenir riesgos es clave seguir los partidos u otros eventos deportivos desde aplicaciones legales y que cuenten con derechos de transmisión para evitar infringir la ley de propiedad intelectual y exponer los dispositivos a amenazas.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué malware pueden instalarse en el dispositivo al usar aplicaciones ilegales
Al descargar o usar aplicaciones no verificadas o ilegales como Fútbol Libre, el usuario puede infectar su dispositivo con varias clases de malware. Uno de los más graves es el ransomware, que bloquea el acceso a archivos importantes y exige un pago para restaurarlos.
Según el Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad de España (INCIBE), otra amenaza frecuente es el adware, que introduce anuncios no solicitados y ralentiza el dispositivo.
Además, existen aplicaciones capaces de redirigir al usuario a páginas web con fines de recopilación de datos personales, exponiendo información sensible sin consentimiento.
Cómo puede una app pirata robar datos personales al buscar fútbol en vivo
El INCIBE advierte que algunas aplicaciones fraudulentas pueden registrar las pulsaciones del usuario mediante técnicas de keylogging. De esa forma, capturan contraseñas, mensajes y datos bancarios sin que el usuario lo note. Este tipo de software opera en segundo plano y registra toda la actividad realizada desde el dispositivo.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, las apps maliciosas pueden solicitar permisos para acceder a los SMS, facilitando la interceptación de códigos de verificación empleados en operaciones bancarias o compras online. Así, un ciberdelincuente puede completar transacciones o acceder a cuentas protegidas por autenticación en dos pasos.
Por qué es muy difícil identificar una app peligrosa antes de instalarla
Reconocer una aplicación maliciosa no siempre resulta sencillo, sobre todo cuando imitan la apariencia y funcionalidad de plataformas legítimas.
El INCIBE sugiere verificar siempre la fuente de descarga, privilegiando tiendas oficiales como Google Play o App Store, donde existen filtros y controles de seguridad. Las tiendas alternativas, los enlaces compartidos en foros y las descargas directas representan un riesgo mucho mayor.
PUBLICIDAD
Es clave revisar los permisos que solicita la aplicación. Una app para ver fútbol no necesita acceder a la cámara, ubicación o lista de contactos. Si se detectan solicitudes de permisos injustificadas, se sugiere denegar el acceso o eliminar la aplicación.
Las valoraciones y comentarios de otros usuarios son otros indicadores que pueden ofrecer pistas sobre comportamientos anómalos o antecedentes de seguridad cuestionable.
Qué medidas se sugieren para prevenir infecciones al ver partidos online
El INCIBE destaca la importancia de descargar aplicaciones únicamente desde plataformas oficiales. Tanto Google Play como App Store retiran rápidamente aquellas apps que resultan dañinas, minimizando así el riesgo de infección.
PUBLICIDAD
A su vez, es necesario mantener el sistema operativo y las aplicaciones actualizadas, porque ayuda a corregir vulnerabilidades que pueden ser explotadas por ciberdelincuentes.
Otra medida preventiva consiste en instalar una solución de seguridad o antivirus de confianza. Estos programas detectan y eliminan amenazas antes de que causen daños. Realizar copias de seguridad periódicas de los datos permite recuperar la información en caso de secuestro, robo o daño del dispositivo.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo actuar si se sospecha que el dispositivo ha sido infectado tras buscar partidos
Ante síntomas como lentitud inusual, aparición de anuncios no deseados o mensajes de rescate, el INCIBE sugiere actuar de inmediato. Se debe desconectar el dispositivo de la red, eliminar las aplicaciones sospechosas y realizar un análisis completo con un antivirus actualizado.
Si los archivos han sido cifrados por ransomware, no se aconseja pagar el rescate, porque no garantiza la recuperación de los datos. Se sugiere cambiar las contraseñas de todas las cuentas asociadas al dispositivo y activar la verificación en dos pasos en servicios claves.

articles.title: This gaming headset was designed for audiophiles... but I'm not convinced
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The FiiO FG3 has some audiophile-designed hardware and software, and so there's a lot of potential. However, the rumbly sound profile and slightly uncomfortable fit mean they're a little hard to recommend.
Pros
- +Relatively affordable
- +Web-based control app
- +Removeable, flexible mic
Cons
- -Not the comfiest fit
- -Rough-and-ready design
- -Struggles with low-end
Why you can trust TechRadar
FiiO FG3: one-minute review
As an audio journalist, I’ve covered FiiO plenty of times; the brand is known for beloved digital audio players like the JM21 and digital-audio converters like the FA15. But I was surprised to see the brand enter a totally different market, trying its hand at a gaming headset.
The FiiO FG3 is the resulting device, and it clearly bears some of the audiophile DNA that FiiO is known for. It offers a coaxial dual-driver set-up, which is uncommon in games-focused headphones, and also totes a lightweight DAC control module to jump between audio presets.
So it should be a gaming gem, right? Right? Well, I think something was lost in translation.
FiiO’s hardware is fantastic for music, and the FG3 is the same, with the dual-driver set-up and handy EQ modes working well. However, it’s not quite as good for gaming, which isn’t ideal for a 'gaming' headset.
Audio is often too muddy and rumbly to do justice to the layered sound design of an immersive environment or frantic battlefield. It’s largely the low-end which lets the side down, with higher-pitched sounds cutting through pretty effectively. This won’t affect all games, and dialogue-heavy or rhythm ones will benefit massively from the tuning.
The fit of the headphones isn’t perfect either. While the cups are incredibly soft, the headphones squeeze and the headband is too firm. I had to take breaks from long gaming sessions to avoid my head hurting.
That all may sound like a series of criticisms, but there’s a lot to like here too. The cans are easily portable, and the control app being online-only is a breath of fresh air in this bloatware-riddled world (even if it rules out EQ control when you’ve got no internet).

The FG3 is also, crucially, pretty affordable, and I can see a discount or two making it an absolute bargain. If you’re reading this when they’re even $10 / £10 off, they’ll be an absolute bargain.
So it’s easy to look past some of the more annoying elements, or rougher edges, of FiiO’s sound tuning and design. But I can’t help but hope that the brand’s second foray into gaming headsets makes some improvements on what we’ve currently got.
FiiO FG3: Price and availability
- List price: $69.99 / £69.99 (around AU$140)
- Available in the US, UK and Europe
- Matches RIG R5 Spear Pro HS, undercuts other rivals
The FiiO FG3 sells for $69.99 / £69.99 (about AU$140, though at the time of writing, it’s not on sale in Australia), and was unveiled in June, 2026.
At that price, it undercuts many of the best wired gaming headsets, though it matches our top-rated pick: the catchily-titled RIG R5 Spear Pro HS. That makes it fairly good value for a gaming headset, with many alternatives going for three-figure sums.
For your money, you get the headset as well as a removable microphone, control cable and USB adaptor (which lets you plug the USB-C control cable into a USB-A port, if that’s what you have available).
FiiO FG3: specs
| Price | $69.99 / £69.99 (around AU$140) | 
| Weight | 0.69lbs / 0.31kg | 
| Drivers | 50mm dynamic + 16mm dynamic | 
| Compatibility | PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X\|S, Xbox One, Switch, PC | 
| Connection type | Wired (3.5mm or USB-C) | 
FiiO FG3: design and features
The FiiO FG3 comes with a non-removable cable, which connects into a 3.5mm jack. It’s not long, but it’ll reach a hand-held controller. However, it’s best to connect it to a control module which comes in the box; this offers you the ability to mute, change EQ or modify volume, and has a much longer cable which connects to a device via USB-C (or USB-A, thanks to an included adaptor).
These cans aren’t particularly unique-looking, although the cups are slightly canted, which helps them fit a head shape better. They rotate a little horizontally and vertically, which also helps with the fit, though some other elements like the thin metal headband or certain cheap-feeling plastic elements discourage any notion of these being premium headphones. There are no on-cup controls either.
While the ear pads are soft and comfortable, I did find that the padded headband wasn’t padded enough. Longer gaming stints ended in growing aches; the FG3 fit isn’t as comfortable as other gaming headsets I’ve used. A slight squeeze offered by the cans didn’t help either.
You can fold the cups in on each other, and remove the microphone, transforming the headset into a compact unit which is easy to transport (though it doesn’t come with any kind of carry case). Combined with a feature we’ll get to later, it’s a great headset for people who game in different venues.
Now onto the feature set. A potentially-divisive feature of the FiiO FG3 is that you don’t need to download a control app to clutter up your PC. Instead, FiiO’s website offers the ability to change EQ and flick between presets.
I loved the fact I didn’t need to download more bloating software onto my rig, and that I could tote the FG3 between different systems and locations and still customize them, but it does mean that you get no control while offline.
The control site lets you choose three presets, which the control module lets you change between: a gaming mode, a cinema one, and a music one. The latter list, which includes the custom mode, is the one I found myself using most.
This module also means you can still jump between your EQ presets when you're on a console or handheld, so your decision to play on a Switch, PlayStation or Xbox doesn't mean you're banned from customizable sound.
Don’t expect any Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) here. I found that the Passive Noise Cancellation (PNC) or natural ear cup blocking, managed to cut out annoying background sounds from my street, as did the closed-back design. But it won’t save you from louder interruptions.
FiiO FG3: performance
True to its audiophile heritage, FiiO has packed the FG3 with two drivers per cup: one 50mm dynamic driver designed to handle mid- and low-end, and a smaller 16mm dynamic driver for higher-end sounds. The benefit of dual drivers, rather than the sole unit found in most gaming headsets, is twofold: firstly, each being dedicated to different frequencies means that they can be better catered to them. Secondly, simultaneous sounds can be delivered with better clarity.
This latter is certainly true of the FiiO FG3, which has a distinct V-shaped sound profile; that means that bass and treble are well-defined and clear, though mids are a little lost. This isn’t a huge issue for gaming, as most sound effects are low or high ones, but it’s audible in music (including game scores).
It’s also clear that the high-end dynamic driver does its job well. Dialogue is easy to make out, even in frantic battles, including in-game audio and friends’ voice chats during gameplay. It’s also easy to make out nearby footsteps or the twinkle of a distant collectible.
However, I’m not as sold on the bass capabilities of the larger driver. In music it’s scooping and well-defined, but while gaming it lacks the power or ‘oomph’ of some other headsets I’ve tested. This means the chatter of your gunfire sounds a little dulled, nearby explosions lose a visceral edge, and roaring monsters sound like they have a sore throat.
Perhaps most importantly, the background rumble of a city or busy landscape which so often defines an alive-feeling open world felt a little too ‘rumbly’ for me. Some of FiiO’s equalization modes go some way to fix its issues, but not the whole way; I never found a way to stop the sound feeling a little muddy, and sometimes even made it worse.
A much-touted selling point of the FG3 is the use of Virtual 7.1, an algorithm which spreads sound to give a feeling of surround sound, without using 8 speakers (which would simply be 7.1 sound). It helps a little in spreading environmental and atmospheric sounds about you, though you’ll never forget that you’re simply getting spread-out headphone sound.
The removable microphone is… fine for purpose, but won’t deliver especially crystalline audio. Even recording onto my PC’s own voice recorder app, speech is a little crackly. However, I appreciate how dexterous the strut holding the microphone is: you can move it to different angles or heights, and there’s far more versatility than in many other headsets I’ve used.
Should I buy the FiiO FG3?
Buy it if...
You need something easily portable
Between the removable microphone, the foldable build, and the fact that you can use the control app anywhere, this is perfect for going to a friend's LAN party.
You like customizing your sound
The online EQ platform offers you loads of presets and plenty of control over your sound. Plus, the DAC control panel lets you jump between them easily.
Don't buy it if...
You need something suited for long gaming stints
After a few hours with the FG3, my head and ears were asking for a break. It's not the ideal headset for day-long binges, or even a full workday.
You want the best video game sound
If all you care about is the sound of your games, then the FiiO will disappoint you. It's not bad, but its muddy sound profile means you're never getting the best audio possible.
FiiO FG3: Also consider
Here are two more gaming headsets that we've given positive reviews to, if you're not sold on the FiiO FG3.
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | FiiO FG3 | RIG R5 Spear Pro HS | Turtle Beach Atlas 200 | 
| Price | $69.99 / £69.99 (around AU$140) | $69.99 / £69.99 (around AU$140) | $59.99 / £49.99 (around AU$100) | 
| Weight | 0.69lbs / 0.31kg | 0.74lbs / 0.34kg | 0.62lbs / 0.28kg | 
| Drivers | 50mm dynamic + 16mm dynamic | 40mm graphene | 50mm Nanoclear | 
| Compatibility | PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X\|S, Xbox One, Switch, PC | PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X\|S, Xbox One, Switch, Switch 2, PC | PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X\|S, Xbox One, Switch, Switch 2, PC | 
| Connection type | Wired (USB-C) | Wired (3.5mm) | Wired (3.5mm) | 
RIG R5 Spear Pro HS
This same-price rival offers great sound and a more comfortable fit. However, there's no way of customizing your sound, and you can't remove the microphone.
Read our full RIG R5 Spear Pro HS review
Turtle Beach Atlas 200
For even less than the FiiO, this Turtle Beach alternative offers a well-designed mesh headband and great mic quality. But its feature set is weighted towards PC gamers.
Read our full Turtle Beach Atlas 200 review
How I tested the FiiO FG3
- Used for three weeks
- Tested for gaming and other tasks
- Mainly connected to gaming PC
I tested the FiiO FG3 for roughly three weeks in order to write the review. Through this time, I used the headset while connected to my gaming PC; I tried to plug it into my Android phone, but the connection was stuttery.
The majority of the testing was done gaming; predominantly Nioh 3 and Total War: Pharaoh, but with time also spent on Old School Runescape, Isonzo, Slay The Spire, Crying Suns and the Mortal Shell 2 beta. I also used the headset to stream music while at work, and watch YouTube videos and TV shows.
Since I review audio products for a living, I have plenty of experience testing gaming headsets (and using other headphones for gaming purposes). I've also tested other FiiO products.
First reviewed August 2026
Tom Bedford is a freelance contributor covering tech, entertainment and gaming. Beyond TechRadar, he has bylines on sites including GamesRadar, Digital Trends, Android Police, TechAdvisor, WhattoWatch and BGR. From 2019 to 2022 he was on the TechRadar team as the staff writer and then deputy editor for the mobile team.

articles.title: TransferNow ou WeTransfer : lequel choisir en 2026 ?
articles.text:
Des plateformes de transfert de fichiers comme TransferNow et WeTransfer disposent de plusieurs formules qui présentent chacune leurs avantages. Voici un comparatif critère par critère pour trancher selon l’usage.
Formule gratuite : des philosophies bien différentes
Les deux plateformes ne partent pas de la même position. TransferNow, le service français lancé en 2013, reste l’outsider face à un concurrent bien plus dominant.
Son offre gratuite le reflète : 5 Go par envoi, sans limite de fréquence ni de volume mensuel, et l’essentiel des fonctions (mot de passe, aperçu des fichiers, liens personnalisables) accessible sans création de compte. Une générosité qui s’explique notamment par une volonté de conquête.
WeTransfer, de son côté, occupe une position de leader, cette notoriété lui permet de resserrer son offre gratuite sans trop risquer de perdre des utilisateurs attachés à la marque.
Dans les deux cas, la stratégie déployée est cohérente. Mais si l’on se place du point de vue de l’utilisateur, c’est bien l’approche de TransferNow qui se montre la plus pertinente.
Le duel en un coup d’œil
|  | TransferNow | WeTransfer | 
| Taille max gratuite | 5 Go | 3 Go | 
| Quota mensuel gratuit | Aucun (transferts illimités) | 10 transferts ou 3 Go cumulés sur 30 jours | 
| Disponibilité des fichiers | 7 jours gratuits ou 365 jours Premium | 3 jours gratuit | 
| Choix de la région | Oui, y compris la France | Non | 
| Mot de passe | Oui | Oui | 
| Antivirus | Oui, dès l'offre gratuite | Non | 
Sécurité et confidentialité : TransferNow va plus loin
Il n’est pas nécessaire de rappeler à quel point la sécurité est essentielle pour un service dont la mission est de transmettre des fichiers, parfois sensibles.
WeTransfer et TransferNow chiffrent les transferts en TLS/SSL et le stockage en AES-256. Sur ce socle commun, aucune différence notable : les fichiers sont protégés de la même manière pendant leur transit ainsi que sur les serveurs.
Les différences apparaissent sur les couches additionnelles, celles qui ne sont pas toujours activées par défaut ni comprises dans toutes les offres :
- Analyse antivirus : dès l’offre gratuite chez TransferNow, elle permet de vérifier les fichiers envoyés afin de détecter et bloquer d’éventuels contenus malveillants.
- Chiffrement avec clé personnelle (SSE-C) : TransferNow propose cette option qui permet à l’utilisateur de conserver la maîtrise de sa propre clé de chiffrement au lieu de dépendre des mécanismes de chiffrement gérés par le prestataire. Cette fonction n’est pas disponible chez WeTransfer.
- Choix de la région d'hébergement : sans compte, TransferNow attribue automatiquement une région continentale selon la localisation de l'utilisateur (Europe pour un utilisateur français). À partir de l'offre Starter, il devient possible de sélectionner un emplacement précis : Paris, Francfort, Singapour, New York… Chez WeTransfer, l'hébergement s'effectue en Europe ou aux États-Unis, sans possibilité de sélection : la région est déterminée par la plateforme.
- Utilisation des données pour l'IA : TransferNow s'engage à ne pas utiliser les fichiers ni les données personnelles de ses utilisateurs pour entraîner des modèles d'intelligence artificielle, ni à les exploiter commercialement ou les revendre. Un engagement qui répond à une préoccupation devenue centrale sur ce marché.
Tarifs : TransferNow vs WeTransfer
Sur les offres individuelles, TransferNow Premium démarre à 6 €/mois selon l’engagement, contre environ 19 €/ mois pour WeTransfer Ultimate. L’écart est donc significatif.
Tarif des offres individuelles
|  | TransferNow Premium | WeTransfer Ultimate | 
| Mensuel | 10€/mois | 23€/mois | 
| Annuel | 8€/mois | 19€/mois | 
| 2 ans | 6€/mois | Non proposé | 
|  | TransferNow Starter | WeTransfer Starter |  | 
| Mensuel | 5€/mois | 8€/mois |  | 
| Annuel | 3€/mois | 7€/mois |  | 
Quel service choisir en fonction de son profil ?
- Utilisateur occasionnel : TransferNow et WeTransfer proposent chacun une offre gratuite adaptée à un usage ponctuel. TransferNow autorise néanmoins jusqu’à 5 Go par transfert sans limite mensuelle, contre 3 Go par transfert chez WeTransfer, plafonnés à 10 transferts ou 3 Go cumulés par mois.
- Créateur professionnel ou amateur (photo, vidéo) : le poids des fichiers peut rapidement dépasser les quotas gratuits des deux services, ce qui implique de basculer sur une offre payante. TransferNow se distingue ici par la personnalisation des liens et de la page de téléchargement (image de marque, message personnalisé), ainsi que par une durée de conservation des fichiers pouvant atteindre 365 jours.
- Professionnel indépendant / TPE : TransferNow propose un tarif plus accessible que les offres payantes de WeTransfer, ainsi qu’une protection par mot de passe disponible sans création de compte.
- PME / Équipe : TransferNow facture ses offres Team sous forme de forfait (par exemple 10 comptes inclus), tandis que WeTransfer facture à la licence par utilisateur. L’écart de coût devient significatif dès que l’équipe dépasse quelques collaborateurs, ce qui rend TransferNow plus avantageux…
L’offre qui pourrait bien faire pencher la balance
Avec le code TNWCLUBIC, profitez de 30 % de réduction pendant un an. De quoi tester tranquillement toutes les fonctionnalités de TransferNow… Et découvrir par vous-même les qualités du service, ainsi que la bonne formule à choisir.
FAQ - Questions fréquentes
Quel service est le plus adapté pour une équipe ?
TransferNow, dont l’offre Team inclut 10 comptes pour un tarif forfaitaire, alors que WeTransfer facture chaque utilisateur individuellement, ce qui creuse l’écart de coût dès que l’équipe s’agrandit
TransferNow ou WeTransfer, lequel est le plus généreux en version gratuite ?
TransferNow, avec 5 Go par envoi sans limite mensuelle, contre 3 Go par transfert et un plafond de 10 transferts par mois chez WeTransfer.
Faut-il un compte pour envoyer un fichier protégé par mot de passe ?
Chez TransferNow, ce n’est pas le cas. Le mot de passe est disponible sans inscription.
