articles.title: How Magron is building ‘Generation 2’ of electric vehicles
articles.text:
How Magron is building ‘Generation 2’ of electric vehicles
Bengaluru-based EV startup Magron is developing three electric motorcycles alongside technologies such as wireless charging and an AI-powered riding assistant.
The Indian electric two-wheeler market has largely been driven by scooters. But Bengaluru-based Mobility Aggregation Global Research Organisation (Magron) is betting on electric motorcycles.
Founded in 2022, the startup is developing three electric motorcycles—H35, C20 and C10—and also working on technologies that it hopes to sell across the wider EV ecosystem.
“We thought that at some point of time, motorcycles are actually going to flourish in the industry,” says Co-founder and CEO Abiram Menon. “Since our team is heavily experienced in motorcycles, we thought to take a bet.”
Menon’s move into electric mobility began at Bounce, where he was the company’s first engineer, working on scooters and the transition towards EVs. He was also the EV lead at Yulu for a brief period. He later worked on vehicle development and consultancy projects for several two-wheeler companies.
“If I can actually do it for all these people, why can't I just do it by myself?” he recalls thinking.
The founding team of Magron also includes Co-founder and Director Jahnavi Jaiswal. The startup has a 26-member team with an average experience of 15 years in relevant areas. Its senior-most consultant has around 55 years of experience.
Betting on motorcycles
Magron initially considered competing in the premium end of the electric motorcycle market. It built its first complete prototype using carbon-fibre composite materials in 85 days.
“But we soon realised that India is still not mature enough for any two-wheeler which actually goes beyond Rs 2.5-3 lakh,” Menon says.
The startup then began working on a broader portfolio.
The H35, Magron’s flagship motorcycle, is expected to cost Rs 3-3.5 lakh. It will be produced in limited batches as a technology-led, hand-built motorcycle.
The C20, priced at Rs 2-2.5 lakh, is aimed at the mainstream motorcycle segment. The C10 will be a stripped-down version of the C20, priced below Rs 2 lakh.
“We need to have a sensible product which can sell by itself,” says Menon.
Magron expects the C10 and C20 to reach the market around the middle of 2027, with the H35 following a few months later.
Building beyond the motorcycle
The motorcycles are one part of Magron’s larger technology strategy. The company says it has identified more than 200 potential areas for development across the EV ecosystem and has worked on more than 50 of them so far.
One of the more developed technologies is a patented wireless charging system that’s more convenient than the wired system. Instead of plugging a cable into the motorcycle, riders can simply park over a charging pad and let the vehicle charge automatically.
“We want to actually flood the market with the wireless charging infrastructure,” says Menon, comparing the approach to the gradual standardisation of wireless charging for smartphones.
Magron says its system is designed to deliver charging speeds comparable to wired charging. It is initially targeting 6.6kW and plans to eventually take the technology to 120kW.
The system uses a self-aligning mechanism to position the charger beneath the vehicle.
Magron is also working on safety systems that can detect disruptions around the charging area and automatically cut off power.
The company does not plan to restrict the technology to its own vehicles.
“We want to democratise this charging infrastructure,” says Menon, adding that Magron eventually wants to sell the technology to two-wheelers, four-wheelers, and commercial vehicles in the market.
An AI assistant for riders
Magron is also developing Magron Intelligent Virtual Assistant (Miva), an AI system designed for the riding environment.
Under development since 2023, Miva is intended to understand riding patterns and detect conditions such as drowsiness or unsafe riding.
“It can converse with riders in multiple languages and slang, while safety layers are designed to stop the system from distracting the rider in critical situations. It's more of an emotional AI, not like the generic responding kind of an AI,” he says.
Miva will be available on the C20, with its more advanced capabilities offered as an additional package. The H35 will get the full system.
Menon says the company sees the software as a product that could eventually move beyond its own motorcycles. Magron is already in discussions with other OEMs about sharing its AI technology.
Tech play
Rather than treating the motorcycle as a single product, Magron has divided the EV into different technology stacks, including data, AI and machine learning, and patented hardware components.
“Each and every individual stack also has revenue potential and opportunities to share across the entire EV ecosystem,” says Menon.
Magron has raised around $1 million so far and plans to raise about $5 million in its next round. The capital will go towards extensive testing, supply chain development, tooling, contract manufacturing, and a pilot batch of around 100 vehicles.
The eclectic two-wheeler market is currently valued at $1.98 billion and is expected to reach $5.48 billion by 2032. Prospects for EV companies like Magron are only expected to get better.
For now, the startup is focused on improving existing EV technology rather than trying to reinvent the electric motorcycle from scratch.
“We are only going to bring improvements from whatever is existing in the industry and a few things which are not available in the industry,” says Menon.
Magron is betting on development of “Generation 2” of electric vehicles—making electric motorcycles more practical and turning individual vehicle technologies into products for the broader EV ecosystem. This is what, Menon says, separates Magron from competitors like Bengaluru-based Ultraviolette Automotive.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword's phenomenal combat and epic cinematics make it the best entry in the series, even if it's slow at times
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Onimusha: Way of the Sword is easily the best entry in the samurai demon-hunting franchise, delivering an immersive, cinematic, and epic experience in both its highly detailed cutscenes and combat encounters. It has a few tedious and repetitive segments, particularly due to the low difficulty of many enemy encounters and repeated boss fights; however, those downsides fail to overshadow any stronger aspects of the game.
Pros
- +Addictive combat
- +Exceptional parry and sword-clash animations
- +Most story cutscenes are beautiful, but...
- +Fantastic sound design
- +Good enemy variety
- +Hard mode difficulty for New Game Plus
- +Strong character development
Cons
- -Many enemy encounters are too easy
- -Too many repeated boss battles
- -... switching back to in-game dialogue moments is jarring
- -Only one primary weapon
Why you can trust TechRadar
Onimusha: Way of the Sword has blown me away after 30 hours with its engaging, emotional, and immersive narrative, filled with epic combat encounters. Capcom nailed the sword-fighting in almost all areas, further aided by some of the best boss battles I've ever played in the action-adventure genre.
Platform reviewed: PC
Available on: PS5, Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, PC, Nintendo Switch 2
Release date: September 4, 2026
The enemy variety in Way of the Sword appears a little weak initially, but fortunately, there is surprisingly a decent number of diverse enemy types to tackle, some of which will put players' skills to the test, and enemies that tie directly to some of the darker and morbid aspects of the story — giving me every bit of motivation to defeat those responsible.
Much like previous games in the Onimusha series, upgrades and enhancements work by collecting red souls from defeating enemies or by finding other necessary resources to stay well-equipped for more difficult encounters or boss fights (because there are many of them).
Capcom has blended elements from the beloved franchise with modern elements (notably thanks to the RE Engine, used in Resident Evil Requiem), creating a sword-fighting, narrative-driven experience that successfully revitalizes the franchise for future entries — and yet again, it proves that it's in the best form it's ever been in.
What it takes to be the strongest
In Onimusha: Way of the Sword, we follow Miyamoto Musashi, a confident young samurai looking to climb to the very top to be the best swordsman there is, battling rivals and those with the same goal. When an encounter with a fierce rival, Sasaki Ganryu, goes wrong, both Musashi and Ganryu are thrust into lives and roles neither could ever expect.
Genma (demons) are seeping into Kyoto, Japan, from the depths of hell, and chaos is unfolding, with the lives of innocents taken brutally, and formidable Genma tormenting those who are vulnerable.
Musashi and Ganryu seek the same goal: master the blade and become the ultimate swordsman. However, both will eventually learn that far more important matters are at stake: humanity's attempt to repel Genma is in dire need of attention, and with Ganryu led astray, it's up to Musashi to forge the right path to heroism.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Equipped with Oni gauntlets, Musashi and Ganryu possess strengths far above the ordinary human, with plenty of abilities to challenge and defeat Genma. However, as expected, with that power comes plenty of responsibility.
Do strength and power derive from one's own efforts? Is it honorable to seek absolute power with the sacrifice of innocents? These are questions Musashi is left to answer throughout his journey, learning through victory but also through trial and error, ultimately creating an engaging rollercoaster that kept me on the edge of my seat.
Musashi is far from perfect in his use of Oni powers, but the character's development throughout the Way of the Sword and his bravado (significantly amped by the face model of the late and legendary Toshiro Mifune) are the strongest aspects of the game, keeping you coming back for more after each main story mission.
Miyamoto Musashi shines in every single cutscene, with a level of charisma that accurately represents the legendary Japanese figure, Musashi himself, and Toshiro Mifune's prowess. (Video Credit: Capcom)
As much as Onimusha: Way of the Sword maintains a strong focus on sword combat, it's very much a strong cinematic experience, with cutscenes that are absolutely phenomenal. The level of detail in every character's facial expressions and speech makes it feel like you're watching a movie at times.
Unfortunately, that makes the switch back to gameplay and dialogue sequences quite jarring. It's not that the visuals aren't great during gameplay; it just doesn't match up to those cinematic sequences, and I found myself constantly wishing gameplay looked as great as those important cutscenes — but ultimately, those beautiful visuals are designed for what's most important: the story.
Exceptional, addictive sword combat
Unsurprisingly, the combat in Onimusha: Way of the Sword is fantastic, taking fundamentals from what series veterans are accustomed to, alongside new and exciting skills, making every encounter entertaining.
As mentioned in my preview, the Issen technique makes its return, allowing players to viciously strike enemies right before being hit, and it makes for an incredible spectacle.
More importantly, parrying and deflecting are pivotal to overcoming foes in Way of the Sword. Just like Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice by FromSoftware, both defence options significantly deplete enemy stamina or 'posture', leaving them open to attacks for huge damage.
Way of the Sword treats Sekiro's 'deathblows' slightly differently; instead of one central area to attack, players have several options for areas to strike against bosses.
In scenarios where Musashi runs out of Hozuki (used for quick healing), most bosses will have a limb or part of a weapon (notably with the Byakue boss) highlighted in purple that is filled with red, yellow, blue, and purple souls, but does less damage to the enemy compared to the traditional main attack.
It's an aspect of combat that creates a dynamic back-and-forth between Musashi and various bosses, especially if you need more yellow souls for health from dealing too much damage earlier on.
Patience is key when attempting to execute Issen or Chain Issen, as the timing window is very narrow, more so than those for parries and deflects. When mastered, though, you'll overcome most enemies with ease. (Video Credit: Capcom)
Capcom did promise that enemies further into the game's story would be more difficult, after players voiced concerns that the demo was too easy. While I can say that endgame enemies are certainly more formidable and aggressive, some even making me sweat when in larger numbers, most basic enemy encounters are still easy.
This is directly due to Capcom's design for Way of the Sword's combat, which is very obviously focused on replicating samurai-like fights, taking after historical samurai duels that often ended in a single strike. Enemies won't attack Musashi in groups, making clashes with enemies easy, but I can see what director Satoru Nihei was aiming for with slower, more deliberate, and steadily paced sword clashes.
Fortunately, once you beat the game, you'll unlock the hard mode, Carnage, which is encouraged for use in New Game Plus. This raises the stakes to a new level, as a single hit could result in death, similar to Sucker Punch's Ghost of Tsushima and its Lethal difficulty.
While that doesn't directly address the fundamental aspect of enemies not attacking Musashi all at once, it will keep players on their toes to remain efficient in combat.
Onimusha: Way of the Sword genuinely has some of the best animations I've ever seen in any video game, particularly when parrying. Musashi oozes so much swagger in every single fight, making his confident and cocky attitude shine through combat, not just dialogue and cutscenes.
At the same time, I was slightly disappointed to see that Musashi's katana is the only primary weapon to use throughout the game. Yes, you'll find Oni Armaments on the journey, which effectively act as secondary weapons, but they require blue souls to pull off special attacks. It's a step away from a series tradition, where characters like Samonsuke or Jean Reno had a wide arsenal of weapons to use on the fly.
The game excels at its parry and deflect animations, but is surprisingly lacking in the number of animations for enemy finishers — and I couldn't help but feel like another primary weapon besides the katana would instantly fix that.
Nonetheless, Onimusha: Way of the Sword's boss fights make up for it, as they are easily the standout in an already immersive and addictive game experience. While some of the boss encounters are repeated too often, particularly during the game's climax, they are easily among some of the most epic boss battles I've played in games.
Besides the final boss battle, Dohatsu-ten is a strong favourite of mine, putting my reflexes to parry fast attacks to the test, and its design reminds me of Capcom's very own familiar and beloved half-demon, half-human demon hunter, Dante. (Video Credit: Capcom)
Onimusha: Way of the Sword has several breathtaking boss encounters from start to finish, but the very final boss fight is perhaps now among the best I've ever played in gaming. Without diving into spoiler territory, it was a battle that gave me the true sword fighting back-and-forth I was yearning for throughout the game. Capcom nailed this boss encounter, as it quite literally pushes you utilize every single skill and maneuver Musashi has learned, to overcome an incredibly ferocious and fast foe — and I can only imagine how challenging it will be on the hard mode difficulty.
If difficulty is a major concern, fear not, because not only are the boss fights a fantastic spectacle, but they're also very challenging. Bosses will often launch attacks (where swords have a purple glow) that can't be dodged or blocked, so players must parry or deflect them or lose plenty of souls in the process.
Losing souls from being hit by an enemy's unblockable attack is very risky, as they'll be collected and used to make them even stronger mid-fight — and this is the last thing you'll want to happen during the final boss fight, which I won't spoil.
Players will also have to look out for bosses attempting to grab Musashi by hitting the dodge button just before it lands, as mistiming this results in serious damage and can single-handedly decide a fight. Pulling off well-timed dodges, parries, deflects, and counters to grabs makes the entire combat experience addictive, and once you unlock the Oni transformation, the game takes a new leap to greater heights.
What about performance?
I played Onimusha: Way of the Sword on my main desktop gaming PC, equipped with an RTX 4080 Super and an AMD Ryzen 7 5700X3D processor, and performance was the least of my concerns. Through most of my 30-hour playthrough, I played at maximum graphics settings at the 3440x1440 display resolution, with DLSS Quality enabled, and consistently stayed above the 100 fps mark.
When testing the game on my Lenovo Legion Go S Z1 Extreme handheld gaming PC, I could easily hit around 40fps with graphics settings preset to medium, with FSR set to balanced, at around 24W (power consumption).
This is another Capcom game that runs very smoothly, which was a worry considering some of its semi-open world hubs. The RE Engine seems to struggle in open-world (open-area) games like Dragon's Dogma 2 and Monster Hunter Wilds, rather than those with linear environments in Capcom's Resident Evil games.
I did experience a few odd moments of heavy frame rate dips during some cutscenes, but these were few and far between, so it didn't break the flow of important narrative development.
There is full ultrawide support in both cutscenes and gameplay, which isn't exactly common for PC ports, as the former is often restricted to the 16:9 aspect ratio.
Should you play Onimusha: Way of the Sword?
Play it if...
You love games that heavily rely on parries and counters
Onimusha: Way of the Sword is a sword-fighting fan's dream, with enough combat and duels that will keep you addicted to rematching the toughest bosses, and frankly, should be enough to encourage a second playthrough.
You love the Onimusha games
Without a doubt, Onimusha: Way of the Sword is the best game in the Onimusha series, with Capcom managing to keep mechanics from the original games while adding new content for a modern audience, thanks to the help of the RE Engine.
Don't play it if...
You're looking for a soulslike challenging experience
Onimusha has never been, and seemingly never will be, the franchise that follows in the footsteps of soulslike experiences. Way of the Sword is challenging, but it doesn't punish players for mistakes in the same way something like Elden Ring or Lies of P would. 
You hate repetitive boss encounters
Boss fights are the highlight of Onimusha: Way of the Sword, but it's clear to see that there are far too many boss battles that are repeated at different segments of the game.
Accessibility features
Onimusha: Way of the Sword has plenty of accessibility options, notably color blindness aids alongside visual and auditory accessibility presets. Within those presets lie options such as subtitles (toggle on or off), subtitle size, subtitle background, menu text size, and HUD size.
There are also numerous options to change the blood color, disable dismemberment, remove action prompts, and motion sickness reduction settings.
Players can also change keybinds for mouse and keyboard play, while there are several different options for sprint control (toggle or hold), deflect control, menu cursor speed, and even one to disable the Windows key's functionality.
The game ships with DLSS 4.5 and FSR 3 frame generation, CPU performance presets, and ray tracing, which doesn't seem heavy to run — at least on a high-end gaming system.
How I reviewed Onimusha: Way of the Sword
Most of my 30-hour playthrough of Onimusha: Way of the Sword was on my main gaming PC, using the LG 45GS95QE OLED ultrawide display, providing exceptional immersion thanks to its 800R curvature.
During my trip to Gamescom, I put Onimusha's performance to the test by lowering my Lenovo Legion Go S handheld's TDP as much as possible, and was quite impressed by how steady it was around 40fps. It's certainly possible to achieve 60fps, but it would require lowering graphics settings further and increasing the TDP.
First reviewed August 2026
Isaiah is a Staff Writer for the Computing channel at TechRadar. He's spent over two years writing about all things tech, specifically games on PC, consoles, and handhelds. He started off at GameRant in 2022 after graduating from Birmingham City University in the same year, before writing at PC Guide which included work on deals articles, reviews, and news on PC products such as GPUs, CPUs, monitors, and more. He spends most of his time finding out about the exciting new features of upcoming GPUs, and is passionate about new game releases on PC, hoping that the ports aren't a complete mess.

articles.title: iPhone Ultra, el nuevo plegable de Apple y todos los rumores de lo que sería este primer lanzamiento
articles.text:
El primer iPhone plegable de Apple, conocido por ahora como iPhone Ultra, está a punto de ser presentado oficialmente y promete marcar un antes y un después en la estrategia de producto de la compañía. Las filtraciones más recientes coinciden en que su debut se producirá en el Apple Event del 9 de septiembre, junto a los esperados iPhone 18 Pro y otros lanzamientos clave.
La presentación de este dispositivo supone la entrada de Apple en el competitivo mercado de los smartphones plegables, dominado hasta ahora por marcas como Samsung y Huawei.
PUBLICIDAD
La expectativa es enorme porque el iPhone Ultra llega tras años de rumores, múltiples prototipos internos y una apuesta técnica que busca diferenciarse tanto en diseño como en funcionalidades frente a la competencia.
¿Cómo será el diseño del iPhone Ultra?
Las filtraciones publicadas en sitios como Applesfera, apuntan a un dispositivo con un factor forma plegable y una pantalla exterior cuadrada de 5,5 pulgadas, algo inédito en la gama iPhone y iPad. Al desplegarse, ofrece un panel interior OLED de 7,8 pulgadas con tecnología ProMotion (120 Hz), pensado para quienes buscan productividad y entretenimiento en un formato compacto.
PUBLICIDAD
Apple habría enfocado gran parte del desarrollo en lograr una “arruga invisible” en la pantalla, uno de los retos principales para los smartphones flexibles.
En cuanto a colores, al menos esta primera generación apostará por tonos clásicos, como blanco y negro, dejando de lado las variantes llamativas vistas en otros modelos recientes.
PUBLICIDAD
El iPhone Ultra montará el chip A20 Pro, fabricado en 2 nanómetros, el mismo que equiparán los iPhone 18 Pro y 18 Pro Max. Este procesador, junto a los 12 GB de memoria RAM, ofrecerá mejoras notables en tareas de inteligencia artificial y permitirá ejecutar funciones avanzadas localmente, potenciando la experiencia con Siri AI y las herramientas de Apple Intelligence.
La batería, dividida en doble celda, tendrá una capacidad cercana a los 5.000 mAh, equiparable al modelo Pro Max actual. Según fuentes industriales, se espera una autonomía sólida a pesar del formato delgado y la exigencia del panel plegable.
PUBLICIDAD
Sistema operativo y funcionalidades exclusivas
El sistema operativo será una versión adaptada de iOS 27, con elementos de iPadOS y funciones optimizadas para el formato flexible. Se espera la incorporación de características como Split View y multitarea avanzada, aunque por ahora no habrá compatibilidad con Apple Pencil ni gestor de ventanas completo.
En el apartado fotográfico, el iPhone Ultra contará con una doble cámara trasera de 48 megapíxeles, posiblemente con sensor de apertura variable, aunque no será el referente absoluto en cámaras dentro de la gama. En cuanto a biometría, se descarta Face ID por las limitaciones del formato y se optará por Touch ID lateral.
PUBLICIDAD
Precio, lanzamiento y disponibilidad internacional
El iPhone Ultra será el modelo más caro de la historia de Apple, con un precio estimado de alrededor de 2.200 euros (aproximadamente a 2.380 dólares). La producción inicial estará limitada a entre 7 y 10 millones de unidades, priorizando el mercado estadounidense.
El lanzamiento internacional será progresivo, repitiendo la estrategia usada con el Apple Vision Pro: primero en Estados Unidos y, en función de la demanda y la capacidad de producción, llegará gradualmente a otros países.
PUBLICIDAD
El stock inicial podría agotarse rápidamente, lo que podría retrasar la disponibilidad en mercados internacionales. Factores como la complejidad de ensamblaje, los costes de componentes y la necesidad de ajustar la producción explican la decisión de Apple de controlar el ritmo de distribución.
El iPhone Ultra supone un salto técnico y estratégico en la gama de productos de Apple. Su presentación busca posicionar a la compañía como un competidor serio en el mercado de teléfonos plegables, pero también enfrenta desafíos de producción, costos y aceptación del nuevo formato. La demanda inicial, la experiencia de usuario y la evolución del ecosistema determinarán si el modelo Ultra consolida una nueva línea de producto o queda como una apuesta experimental.
PUBLICIDAD
El lanzamiento del iPhone Ultra será clave para evaluar la capacidad de Apple de reinventar la experiencia móvil en un mercado que busca innovación real.

articles.title: Golpes online fazem parte da vida de 45 milhões de brasileiros, mostra estudo • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Golpes online fazem parte da vida de 45 milhões de brasileiros, mostra estudo
Levantamento do Cetic.br revela que 32% dos usuários de internet no Brasil foram abordados por criminosos.
Golpes online já atingiram cerca de 45 milhões de brasileiros com 16 anos ou mais, o equivalente a 32% da população que acessa a internet no país. Os dados fazem parte da Pesquisa Privacidade e Proteção de Dados Pessoais, divulgada nesta segunda-feira (31/08) pelo Cetic.br, departamento do Núcleo de Informação e Coordenação do Ponto BR (NIC.br) que cuida de estatísticas e indicadores sobre o uso da internet no Brasil. O NIC.br também é a entidade responsável pela gestão dos domínios .br.
O Tecnoblog teve acesso ao estudo, que detalha os canais usados nessas abordagens. Os aplicativos de mensagem são o principal meio usado pelos criminosos e aparecem em 84% dos casos, mas as ligações telefônicas e o SMS, métodos mais tradicionais, surgem logo depois, com 79% e 71%, respectivamente. Ou seja, mesmo quem navega pouco pela internet está sujeito a golpes que envolvem dados pessoais.
Os criminosos não dependem de um único meio para abordar as vítimas. Aplicativos de mensagem são o canal mais citado, presentes em 84% dos relatos, seguidos por ligações telefônicas (79%). Sites e aplicativos falsos aparecem em 71% dos casos, mesma proporção registrada para mensagens SMS. E-mails e redes sociais foram mencionados por 69% e 67% dos entrevistados, respectivamente.
O dispositivo usado para acessar a internet também parece influenciar o tipo de exposição. Entre quem acessa a rede pelo celular, foram mais frequentes os relatos envolvendo sites e aplicativos falsos. Já um acesso mais limitado à internet pode dificultar a adoção de ferramentas e práticas de segurança, ampliando a vulnerabilidade diante dessas abordagens.
Os golpes que usam dados pessoais já fazem parte da experiência de uma parcela significativa dos entrevistados. Segundo a pesquisa, 32% afirmam ter sido abordados por cibercriminosos, enquanto 20% dizem ter sido efetivamente enganados. Os resultados indicam que a exposição não está restrita a quem faz uso intenso da internet: os criminosos também recorrem a canais tradicionais para alcançar as vítimas.
O fator emocional aparece como uma das principais brechas exploradas pelos golpistas. Segundo o estudo, 58% dos entrevistados se consideram mais vulneráveis a esse tipo de abordagem quando estão passando por situações de mal-estar ou estresse emocional. O impacto dos golpes também é diverso: 48% relatam roubo de dinheiro, 43% perda de acesso às próprias contas, 42% dívidas contraídas em seu nome e outros 42% roubo de dados sensíveis.
A escolaridade também aparece associada à exposição. Pessoas que cursaram até o Ensino Fundamental se mostraram mais suscetíveis aos golpes, segundo o levantamento.
A pesquisa ainda revela que a preocupação dos brasileiros aumenta quando há risco direto de perda financeira, enquanto atividades cotidianas de comunicação e armazenamento parecem gerar uma sensação maior de segurança.
No entanto, 66% dos entrevistados afirmaram se preocupar com o uso de seus dados pessoais por ferramentas de inteligência artificial. O nível de escolaridade também influencia esse resultado: a preocupação chega a 72% entre pessoas com ensino superior, mas cai para 54% entre aquelas que estudaram até o Ensino Fundamental.
Também foram avaliados os hábitos de proteção de dados. Há uma queda em quase todas as práticas em relação a 2021. A exceção foi a configuração de cookies, que ganhou espaço no período. A parcela de pessoas que diz ler políticas de privacidade caiu de 68% para 65%; a que verifica a segurança de páginas, de 70% para 63%; e a que restringe o acesso à localização, de 62% para 57%.
A sensação de segurança varia conforme a atividade. Compras online e acesso a contas bancárias são as situações que mais despertam preocupação: 35% e 32% dos entrevistados, respectivamente, se dizem muito preocupados. Já atividades como usar aplicativos de mensagens e armazenar arquivos na nuvem provocam menos receio: 49% e 43%, respectivamente, afirmam estar pouco ou nada preocupados.
O levantamento foi feito em dezembro de 2025 com 2,5 mil indivíduos espalhados pelo país, em entrevistas online.

articles.title: TP-Link announces its first consumer Wi-Fi 8 routers — Archer 8 Ultra preorder commences September 30, in select regions
articles.text:
TP-Link announces its first consumer Wi-Fi 8 routers — Archer 8 Ultra preorder commences September 30, in select regions
The Archer 8 Ultra launches first, while the Deco 8 Ultra arrives in Q1 2027
Earlier this year, TP-Link announced its intentions to launch the first members of its Wi-Fi 8 (802.11bn) networking family. At the time, the company revealed that it would first launch a standalone Archer 8 consumer router this fall, followed by a Deco 8 mesh router. And right on cue, TP-Link stated today that the Archer 8 Ultra BN19000 tri-band router will launch on September 30.
TP-Link is going light on the details at this time, but this is what we know so far. The Archer 8 Ultra BN19000 will come equipped with 18 internal antennas and deliver up to 19 Gbps aggregate wireless speeds. In addition, it will have 10 Gbps wired connectivity, though we don’t know whether that includes WAN and LAN ports or just the latter.
For users who require broader coverage in larger homes or offices, the Deco 8 Ultra BN22000 tri-band mesh router offers aggregate speeds of up to 22 Gbps and includes 10 Gbps wired connectivity. TP-Link typically sells its mesh systems in two- or three-pack configurations, and the Deco 8 Ultra BN22000 3-pack covers up to 9,800 square feet. Unfortunately, the Wi-Fi 8 mesh system won’t be available until Q1 2027, according to TP-Link.
TP-Link plans to expand its Wi-Fi 8 portfolio by Q2 2027 with a new Roam 8 travel router, along with range extenders and PCIe/USB client adapters. Although we don’t know which specific chipsets will power Archer 8 Ultra, Deco 8 Ultra, and other unannounced Wi-Fi 8 devices, the company says its products will use hardware from Broadcom, MediaTek, and Qualcomm.
Wi-Fi 8 is shaping up to be more of a quality-of-life improvement over Wi-Fi 7 than a substantial theoretical speed improvement. Put simply, Wi-Fi 8 hardware devices should be able to come closer to fulfilling the real-world performance metrics that Wi-Fi 7 devices originally promised.
To this end, TP-Link says that its so-called StabilityEngine leverages core Wi-Fi technologies including Enhanced Long Range (ELR) and Distributed Resource Units (DRU). These features together help improve wireless connectivity, primarily for low-power IoT devices that are typically positioned at the edge of your home’s wireless coverage. There are also additional technologies at play, such as Unequal Modulation (UEQM) and Modulation and Coding Schemes (MCS), to ensure uninterrupted wireless traffic in high-interference situations.
A new design language is also being ushered in with the Archer 8 and Deco 8 products, which was teased during TP-Link’s May 2026 announcement. “We stopped building a piece of networking equipment and started designing for the home,” explained TP-Link industrial design chief Gary Chang. “When a router’s design becomes something people want to display, it ends up exactly where it performs best.”
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
What remains unclear is how or when these new Wi-Fi 8 products will launch in the U.S. As of today, TP-Link has yet to obtain FCC approval to release all-new products in the country. Unlike competitors Amazon and Netgear, which received conditional approval from the FCC Covered List, the U.S. government is still playing hardball with TP-Link. For its part, TP-Link only says that preorders for the Archer 8 Ultra will open in “select regions” on September 30.

Brandon Hill is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware. He has written about PC and Mac tech since the late 1990s with bylines at AnandTech, DailyTech, and Hot Hardware. When he is not consuming copious amounts of tech news, he can be found enjoying the NC mountains or the beach with his wife and two sons.

articles.title: Private AI agents get a deny-by-default runtime from Broadcom - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
As AI agents take on enterprise tasks, companies face a new battle over access and control
Enterprise private AI has moved past the pilot stage, and the shift is exposing an awkward gap. Agents that write code, process claims and run business workflows need models, tools and data to be useful, yet few organizations want autonomous software wandering across their infrastructure unsupervised.
That tension is putting platform teams back at the center of enterprise architecture. The same cloud-native disciplines — orchestration, telemetry, observability and role-based access control — are now being applied to fleets of agents. Because agentic applications are essentially microservices applications, the platform is a natural place to enforce control, according to Purnima Padmanabhan (pictured), general manager of the Tanzu Division at Broadcom Inc.
“Agents have, by definition, agency, which means you just give the intent and resources and then the agent interprets that intent and decides to do something,” Padmanabhan said. “You have to say, ‘OK, I want to be able to build agents fast, I want to be able to build that securely and I want to run them, but I want to run them in a sandboxed way.'”
Padmanabhan spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier at VMware Explore 2026, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed agent runtimes, trusted open source and the data foundations behind production AI. (* Disclosure below.)
Private AI gets a deny-by-default agent runtime
Broadcom’s answer to the challenge of securing autonomous agents is a runtime rather than a toolkit. Tanzu Platform Agent Foundations is now an integral part of VMware Private AI Cloud, giving agents a sandboxed place to run where every model, tool and dataset must be explicitly bound, Padmanabhan explained. Curated data products sit alongside it, handling chunking, vectorization and access control so agents can work with curated data without directly accessing original sources.
“The right way to secure an agent is to put it in a black box and give it nothing, but then you won’t get any intelligence,” Padmanabhan said. “I want to give it on my terms in a curated way with identity, with [role-based access control], with credential management. Being able to connect it to curated data sets all on a single platform means I can move faster.”
Trust in the underlying code matters just as much, since agents build with whatever libraries they are handed. Broadcom is scanning both its commercial repositories and open source with Mythos and expanding its Spring and Java security work into Python and Node.js, with June’s patch release the largest in 23 years of Spring stewardship, Padmanabhan noted.
“We are finding issues. We are finding vulnerabilities,” she said. “These vulnerabilities are not just your low-level vulnerabilities, these are things that can completely bring down an enterprise. We take that job very seriously.”
For business leaders, the calculation is less about technology than timing, as coding agents deliver measurable gains and workflow automation follows close behind. Private AI, in that framing, is infrastructure for a competitive position rather than a science project. Organizations that move quickly can turn AI into a source of revenue and competitive advantage, while those that wait risk falling behind, Padmanabhan noted.
“I think the message to the CIO is this is the chance to shine, right? Because this is a revenue opportunity for business,” Padmanabhan said. “It’s also a competitive advantage, and if you don’t do it, it’s a competitive disadvantage, because everybody else is going to be doing it.”

articles.title: OpenAI révolutionne la facturation de ChatGPT : fini de payer sans résultat
articles.text:
Pour l’instant, les grands fournisseurs d’intelligence artificielle appliquent une facturation par jetons. Ainsi, un client achète un certain nombre de jetons qui lui permettent d’effectuer un certain nombre d’actions. Point important : ce mécanisme n’assure en aucun cas des résultats concluants. Certaines entreprises ont ainsi dépensé des sommes faramineuses en jetons pour pouvoir utiliser des modèles d’intelligence artificielle. Par exemple, Microsoft a annulé la plupart de ses licences Claude Code, quatre mois après avoir fortement incité ses développeurs à utiliser quotidiennement les outils d’IA agentique d’Anthropic. La raison : les jetons proposés par Anthropic ont rapidement coûté cher, et ce sans obtenir les résultats escomptés. OpenAI est conscient de ce problème. L’entreprise vient d’ailleurs d’opérer un important changement dans son système de facturation.
Open AI facture désormais certaines entreprises au résultat
Comme le rapporte le média américain The Information, OpenAI a introduit un système de facturation au résultat. Ainsi, peu importe le nombre de jetons utilisés par un client, c’est le travail effectivement réalisé qui compte pour établir la facturation. Les tentatives infructueuses ne sont pas prises en compte dans la facturation, les frais liés à celles-ci étant directement pris en charge par OpenAI. À l’heure actuelle, ce système de tarification au résultat concerne seulement quelques importants clients d’OpenAI. Nous ne connaissons ni les conditions ni les prix.
Bien entendu, un système de tarification au résultat peut être difficilement transposable à l’échelle du grand public tant le nombre de cas à étudier serait conséquent. Cependant, il s’agit d’un véritable tournant dans le secteur de l’intelligence artificielle. Selon Keith Kirkpatrick, analyste et journaliste spécialisé dans les technologies d’entreprise : « La tarification basée sur les résultats est en train de devenir la norme sur le marché ».
Pourquoi ce changement dans la façon de facturer certains clients ?
Le cas de Microsoft qui a annulé ses licences Claude Code après avoir consommé un nombre conséquent de jetons, sans avoir obtenu de résultats concluants, illustre à lui seul le problème. Certaines entreprises brûlent massivement des jetons sans obtenir de résultats concluants. En parallèle, d’autres entreprises voient le problème et freinent leurs investissements dans l’IA. Une entreprise peut également être dans l’incapacité de prévoir le nombre de jetons dont elle aura besoin pour mener à bien un projet et préférera le repousser par crainte de se retrouver avec une facture démentielle. Une facturation au résultat offre ainsi un cadre plus sûr et une promesse d’un travail terminé.
Il reste toutefois à définir ce qu’est un travail mené à bien et correctement réalisé. Sur une longue durée, un client pourra-t-il estimer que le travail demandé n’est pas effectué comme il l’espérait, alors même que les jetons continuent d’être consommés jour après jour ? Justement, les conditions de ce type de contrat, non divulguées, devraient répondre à cette question.

articles.title: El superNiño está convirtiendo el Pacífico en una auténtica fábrica de ciclones: a finales de semana habrá tres activos a la vez
articles.text:
El principio de la historia nos lo sabemos todos: en enero de 2026, el Pacífico ecuatorial estaba virtualmente en condiciones de La Niña. En junio, la NOAA estaba declarando El Niño. Se trata de una de las transiciones más rápidas del registro moderno: el océano ha tardado apenas ocho meses en pasar de un extremo del péndulo al otro.
De hecho, la situación van tan rápido y tan fuerte que el Climate Prediction Center lo considera un candidato serio a superar a todos los Niños medidos desde 1950.
Y, claro, eso tiene consecuencias.
Una fábrica de huracanes. A 1 de septiembre tenemos al huracán Karina, de categoría 4, al oeste de Baja California. 225 km/h y 950 hPa, pero (a priori) sin peligro de tocar tierra. En aguas del Pacífico central, tenemos a Lowell como tormenta tropical a punto de convertirse en huracán, según el Central Pacific Hurricane Center.
Y, por detrás, llegaba EP95, una perturbación con un un 90% de probabilidad de formación en el Tropical Weather Outlook del NHC. Tantas que, de hecho, ya se llama "Marie".
Es decir, si todo progresa como parece que lo hará, para el viernes 4 tendríamos tres sistemas alineados y maduros sobre el mismo océano.
¿Estamos ante algo histórico? No exactamente. En 2015 ya tuvimos un fenómeno parecido: Kilo, Ignacio y Jimena se organizaron simultáneamente como categoría 4 entre el Pacífico central y oriental. Esa sí que fue la primera vez que veíamos una cosa así con huracanes mayores. Ese año llegamos a tener seis (mayores y menores) bailando a la vez en este océano.
¿Qué fue lo que pasó aquel 2015? Exacto: El Niño.
Y eso es lo que hace esto que vemos más interesante. Porque, a falta de que los expertos lo analicen, el mapa que encabeza este artículo no parece una casualidad.
Un mar cargado hasta arriba. Hay muchas cosas que no sabemos, pero lo que sí tenemos claro es que El Niño apunta a ser histórico (un 69% de que se convierta en el más intenso desde 1950), que hay anomalías subsuperficiales de hasta +10 °C en profundidad esperando a aflorar y que tenemos un acoplamiento completo entre el océano y la atmósfera.
Con la cautela propia de saber también que los modelos dinámicos suelen sobreestimar la intensidad del pico a tan largo plazo, la situación pinta tirando a mal.

articles.title: Rentrée 2026 : le Pack Philips Hue Découverte 2025 chute à 129,99€ chez Boulanger
articles.text:
À l'approche de la rentrée, l'envie de s'initier à la maison connectée revient souvent sur le tapis, sans toujours vouloir se lancer dans une installation complète. Boulanger propose actuellement le Pack Philips Hue Découverte 2025 à 129,99 euros au lieu de 279,99 euros, une occasion de faire le point sur ce que ce format d'entrée de gamme apporte réellement au quotidien.
Le Pack Philips Hue Découverte 2025 s'articule autour de la lampe Hue Go, un modèle portable doté d'une batterie rechargeable et compatible avec la technologie Hue White and Color Ambiance. Boulanger commercialise actuellement ce pack, consultable sur la fiche produit du marchand, à 129,99 euros contre 279,99 euros affichés habituellement. Ce type d'offre s'adresse en priorité à celles et ceux qui souhaitent découvrir l'éclairage connecté sans investir immédiatement dans une installation complète avec pont de connexion. Le produit affiche par ailleurs une note de 4,7/5 auprès des acheteurs Boulanger, un indicateur plutôt rassurant pour un premier achat dans cet univers.
Sans le pont Hue Bridge, vendu séparément, certaines fonctionnalités avancées comme la synchronisation avec l'image ou la musique restent toutefois hors de portée avec ce seul pack. Il s'agit donc d'une porte d'entrée vers l'écosystème Hue, pensée pour tester le concept avant d'éventuellement investir davantage.
Voici le Pack Philips Hue Découverte 2025 à 129,99 € au lieu de 279,99 € chez Boulanger !
Pourquoi choisir le Pack Philips Hue Découverte 2025 ?
- Prix confirmé : 129,99 € au lieu de 279,99 € sur la fiche Boulanger, une réduction vérifiée au moment de la rédaction.
- Lampe nomade : la Hue Go embarque une batterie rechargeable, avec une autonomie annoncée jusqu'à 18 heures en mode Bougie chaleureuse.
- Prise en main simple : pilotage via Bluetooth et l'application Hue, sans obligation d'acheter immédiatement le pont Hue Bridge.
Une lampe pensée pour un usage flexible, du salon à la terrasse
La Hue Go se distingue par sa portabilité : posée sur une table basse, emportée en extérieur pour une soirée d'été, ou installée dans une chambre, elle s'adapte à des usages variés grâce à ses 16 millions de couleurs et à des effets lumineux préréglés comme Bougie chaleureuse, Café du dimanche ou Forêt enchantée. Le contrôle s'effectue via Bluetooth, ce qui permet de piloter jusqu'à 10 éclairages sans passer par un pont de connexion, un fonctionnement que Clubic évoquait déjà dans son comparatif des meilleures ampoules connectées, où la simplicité de prise en main de l'écosystème Hue est régulièrement mise en avant. Cette autonomie de contrôle convient particulièrement à un premier achat, avant d'éventuellement étoffer son installation avec d'autres ampoules ou accessoires. Les profils plus exigeants, qui envisagent d'emblée une automatisation poussée ou une synchronisation avec la télévision, devront en revanche prévoir l'achat du pont Hue Bridge, vendu séparément chez Boulanger.
Un pack d'initiation, pas une installation complète
Contrairement aux packs Hue plus complets, incluant plusieurs ampoules et un pont de connexion dès l'achat, ce pack Découverte 2025 se concentre sur une seule lampe nomade à prix réduit. Il permet de tester l'écosystème Hue sans engager un budget conséquent, mais ne remplace pas une installation domotique complète pour plusieurs pièces.
✅ Les points forts
- Prix réduit de moitié par rapport au tarif habituel affiché par Boulanger
- Lampe portable utilisable aussi bien à l'intérieur qu'à l'extérieur
- Large palette de 16 millions de couleurs et effets lumineux préréglés
- Contrôle Bluetooth possible sans achat immédiat du pont Hue Bridge
- Compatible avec Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant et Apple HomeKit
❌ Les limites
- Fonctionnalités avancées (synchronisation TV, musique, automatisations complexes) réservées au pont Hue Bridge, vendu séparément
- Autonomie limitée à 2,5 heures en mode éclairage intelligent complet
- Pack composé d'une seule lampe, insuffisant pour équiper plusieurs pièces d'un coup
- Nécessite l'application dédiée pour exploiter pleinement ses fonctions
Le Pack Philips Hue Découverte 2025 est toujours disponible à 129,99 € chez Boulanger, sous réserve de stock.
Ce Pack Philips Hue Découverte 2025 s'adresse avant tout à celles et ceux qui veulent tester l'écosystème Hue sans investir dans une installation complète. À 129,99 euros au lieu de 279,99 euros, la lampe Hue Go offre un accès simple et nomade à l'éclairage connecté, avec un contrôle Bluetooth suffisant pour un usage ponctuel dans une pièce ou en extérieur.
Les foyers qui envisagent une domotique plus poussée, avec synchronisation TV ou automatisations avancées, devront prévoir l'achat complémentaire du pont Hue Bridge. Pour un premier pas dans la maison connectée, ce pack reste une option accessible et pertinente, à condition de garder ses limites à l'esprit.

articles.title: Studie zeigt: Chatbots verkaufen dreimal besser als Google-Suche – und du merkst es kaum
articles.text:
Dreifache Klickrate: KI-Bots beeinflussen Käufe stärker als jede Suchmaschine
Dass große Sprachmodelle Menschen gezielt beeinflussen können, sorgt immer wieder für Besorgnis: im politischen Umfeld, wo KI-Content Wahlen beeinflussen könnte, aber auch, weil immer mehr Menschen zunehmend enge persönliche Beziehungen zu ihren Chatbots aufbauen – und so im schlimmsten Fall ihre psychische Gesundheit gefährden. Was oft aus dem Blick gerät , ist der Einsatz von großen Sprachmodellen für kommerzielle Zwecke. Forschende der Princeton University haben jetzt in einer Studie gezeigt, wie stark große Sprachmodelle Verbraucherentscheidungen beeinflussen – oft ohne, dass die Nutzer dies bemerken. Die Studie ist als Preprint auf der Online-Plattform Arxiv veröffentlicht.

articles.title: OpenClaw 2.0 lands with an easier setup and a rebuilt browser app
articles.text:
What just happened? OpenClaw shipped version 2026.8.1 over the weekend and is calling it 2.0 – the largest update since the open-source AI agent launched last November. The numbers support the label: 933 contributors, 569 of them first-timers, and more than 16,000 merged pull requests, roughly half of everything the project has merged in its lifetime.
Community manager Hannes Rudolph's blog post for the release was titled "OpenClaw 2.0, Accidentally," explaining that the team set out to simplify installation and rebuild the browser app, but then discovered it couldn't be done in isolation, and ended up reworking the codebase and the full release at the same time.
You might remember a story from earlier this month about an Australian man who asked his AI assistant to book him into a morning gym class. The agent found a flaw in the booking software, discovered it could reserve slots months beyond what the gym allowed, and then, unprompted, hacked the system and jumped the queue. The software that man was running was OpenClaw.
That said, OpenClaw's cultural moment and hype has been on somewhat of a decline. Not because the tool failed but rather because it worked well: rivals absorbed the blueprint, and now we have ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, or Microsoft's Scout.
The people who stayed use it narrowly. Recurring patterns across forums are unglamorous: inbox monitoring that pings Telegram only when something matters, scheduled network scans that come back as a summary, research and flight comparisons, media library chores. AMD and Nvidia both published guides for running it locally on their own hardware, and the project moved to a nonprofit foundation in July.
Suddenly, OpenClaw stopped being a phenomenon and turned into infrastructure for a smaller, more committed group. Reddit threads now regularly point newcomers to Hermes, a self-hosted alternative, while lighter clones like zeroclaw and goclaw split off the rest. Complaints through July centered on stability, with users reporting the gateway failing to start after updates. On Hacker News, the highest-voted comment under this release just asks who's still using it.
The new version aims to improve things with a new guided install that scans your machine for AI access you already have: Codex, ChatGPT or Claude logins, API keys, or local Ollama and LM Studio models – and confirms the chosen model can answer a request before saving it. Most configuration has been pushed out of the first run entirely, on the theory that you can finish setting up the agent by talking to it.
The browser Control UI is now chat-first. The old overview page is gone, sessions moved to a sidebar, and files, approvals, terminals, git diffs and a dockable browser panel sit alongside the conversation. Underneath, sessions and transcripts moved to SQLite, which makes downgrading messy enough that the project recommends a verified backup before you upgrade.
The biggest addition is shared cloud sessions. An admin can grant read-only, suggest, draft or full-participation access to a live agent session with context, which is how the team says it built 2.0 internally. Sandboxing remains off by default.
Security got big improvements as well. Credential requests masked so secrets never enter chat history or model context, an optional 1Password broker, plugin provenance shown before install, workspace-restricted filesystem access, and one-time approvals that expire when an automation's behavior changes.
So this new better version should be considerably nicer to use, arriving at a moment when most people have moved on to agents that do 80% of this inside an app they already pay for. What OpenClaw still offers to differentiate is ownership: your hardware, your model, your data, no subscription. That was always the pitch, and it's the one thing the competition can't copy.

articles.title: 1MORE Launches Classic HQ36 Wireless On-Ear Headphones With Retro-Inspired Design
articles.text:
Monday, August 31st 2026
	
	
	
	
1MORE Launches Classic HQ36 Wireless On-Ear Headphones With Retro-Inspired Design
Building on its expertise in acoustics and understanding of contemporary design trends, professional audio brand 1MORE introduces the 1MORE Classic Headphones HQ36, a new model combining retro-inspired design with modern audio technology. Inspired by vinyl records, the 1MORE Classic HQ36 pairs a distinctive retro look with Hi-Res Wireless certified audio and active noise cancellation, delivering an immersive listening experience for music lovers while also serving as a stylish everyday accessory.
A Distinctive Retro-Inspired Design
The retro aesthetic is one of the defining elements of the 1MORE Classic Headphones HQ36. Its design incorporates classic vinyl-record textures and retro leather materials, with two color options: Maillard Brown and Jazz Black. Designed for a range of everyday settings, from outdoor photography and commuting to work and study, the HQ36 functions as both a listening device and a fashion accessory.Weighing just 193 g, the headphones feature skin-friendly protein leather ear cushions and an adjustable headband to accommodate different head sizes. The lightweight construction is designed to reduce pressure and heat during extended listening. A foldable design also makes the headphones easier to carry.
High-Resolution Sound with Every Detail
In terms of audio performance, the 1MORE Classic HQ36 continues the brand's focus on acoustic engineering and has received Hi-Res Wireless certification. It features a 40 mm dual-magnetic composite diaphragm driver and supports LDAC lossless decoding technology, delivering three times the transmission efficiency of conventional SBC while preserving more detail and depth in music playback.
The HQ36 also supports dynamic spatial audio tracking, allowing the sound field to respond dynamically to head movements for a more immersive, live-like listening experience. In addition, six professionally tuned preset sound profiles and customizable settings through the 1MORE app accommodate different listening preferences across classical, pop, vocal, and other music genres.
Adaptive Listening for Every Environment
For noisy environments, the HQ36 is equipped with QuietMax hybrid active noise cancellation. Its dual-channel hybrid design provides up to -36dB noise reduction, helping reduce environmental noise in settings such as subways and cafés. Users can switch between Noise Cancellation, Transparency, and Off modes with a single control.
Transparency Mode allows surrounding sounds and conversations to remain audible without removing the headphones, providing greater awareness when listening on the go.
Faster, More Stable Wireless Connectivity
The 1MORE HQ36 also features an upgraded dual-core Bluetooth 6.0 solution for faster connections and more stable signal transmission. A 500mAh battery provides up to 60 hours of playback, while fast charging helps reduce downtime during commuting and travel.
For greater flexibility across different listening scenarios, the HQ36 supports both wired and wireless listening and comes with a cable for compatibility with a variety of playback devices. Physical controls provide direct access to power, noise cancellation and volume adjustment.
Through the 1MORE app, users can also access additional functions including one-tap headphone burn-in and OTA firmware updates, providing further customization of the listening experience.
Pricing and Availability
The 1MORE Classic HQ36 On-Ear Headphones are now officially available through the 1MORE official store on Amazon, with availability on the 1MORE official website coming soon. The 1MORE Classic Headphones HQ36 launch at USD 79.99, with additional launch savings currently available on Amazon:

articles.title: The Bentley Supersports: A stripped-out engineer's indulgence
articles.text: Bentley provided flights from Washington, DC, to Monterey, California, and accommodation so Ars could drive the Supersports, as well as ride in a preproduction Torcal EV, which we wrote about last week. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. MONTEREY, Calif.—Last week, we brought news of the Bentley Torcal, a new electric vehicle that the luxury automaker has been cooking up at its HQ in Crewe, England. The company wants to attract new customers with its first battery EV, part of a plan to make sustainability as much a part of the brand's character as its high-end fit and finish. W12 engines have given way to V8 plug-in hybrid power, and the new Continental GT is all the better for it . But around the same time as Ars got its first experience of that new PHEV two-door on a rather wet Spanish racetrack, some of Bentley's boffins were wondering what might happen if you also built one without the hybrid stuff. Or all-wheel drive—something that has been a characteristic of every new road-going Bentley since the turn of the century. That would certainly cut the curb weight. So, too, would leaving out the rear seats. That sort of idea leads down a well-trodden path for some OEMs, and Porsche in particular is famous for making stripped-out road cars inspired by its race cars and making money from them, too. articles.title: Kingston's NV3 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD drops to $156.99 at Newegg — 27% off brings it down to just 15.7 cents per GB
articles.text:
Kingston's NV3 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD drops to $156.99 at Newegg — 27% off brings it down to just 15.7 cents per GB
Lowest price in last 30 days.
With the ongoing AI boom triggering worldwide memory shortages, getting a good deal on RAM or storage has become increasingly difficult. If you are on the lookout for a snappy SSD, however, we have spotted a solid deal on Newegg that could help you save some money on your next storage upgrade. The Kingston NV3 1TB PCIe Gen 4 SSD is currently selling for $156.99, down from its usual price of $215.99, which is also the lowest price the SSD has seen in the past 30 days.
The Kingston NV3 was introduced back in late 2024 as a budget PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD, with the 1TB model rated for sequential read speeds of up to 6,000 MB/s and sequential write speeds of up to 4,000 MB/s. That makes it more than capable of handling everyday office workloads, gaming, and even demanding file transfers. It is notably a DRAM-less SSD as it uses Host Memory Buffer (HMB) technology instead, meaning that the performance may vary depending on the workload. It also has a slightly lower than recommended rated endurance of 320TBW along with a five-year limited warranty.
The Kingston NV3 is a PCIe Gen 4.0 SSD offering sequential read and write speeds of up to 6,000 MBps and 4,000 MBps, respectively.
The SSD may not be suitable for heavy workloads or as a primary SSD in a high-end workstation, but in our testing we found that it can still be a sensible choice for secondary storage. In 3DMark's Storage Benchmark, the NV3 delivered respectable results, and it performed well in PCMark 10, where it beat the Corsair MP600 Elite and came reasonably close to several more expensive SSDs. If you're primarily looking for a drive to store games, photos, videos or any other important data, it should be perfectly adequate. It also consumes very little power and runs fairly cool during operations, just 48°C, the maximum recorded temperature on one of its sensors during testing.
The 1TB Kingston NV3 at its discounted price of $156.99 is a solid option if you're looking for an affordable way to expand your PC's storage. It might not be the fastest or the most capable SSD on the market, but at that price we can't really complain.

articles.title: Cloud infrastructure becomes security front line for agentic AI - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Agentic AI blows up the attack surface as security moves into the infrastructure layer
The enterprise attack surface is expanding rapidly as agentic AI brings a constantly shifting cloud infrastructure into play.
That pace is pushing security decisions down toward the virtualization layer, where policy can be enforced without slowing traffic. Perimeter defenses alone no longer hold, and enterprises that delay a broader lateral security program risk falling behind increasingly automated attacks, according to Umesh Mahajan (pictured), vice president and general manager of the Application Networking and Security Division at Broadcom Inc.
“This is the time where you can’t put off security any longer,” Mahajan said. “‘Oh, I got a perimeter firewall. I’m good.’ No, no, no – not good. It can be bypassed. Now the security gurus or experts are saying, ‘No, you can’t take two years, three years. You have to deploy lateral security.'”
Mahajan spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier at VMware Explore 2026, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed agentic AI’s effect on the enterprise attack surface, zero-trust enforcement and API protection for Kubernetes workloads. (* Disclosure below.)
Building zero trust into cloud infrastructure
Enterprises have often bought security tools piecemeal over the years, and the seams between them are where attackers operate. Broadcom’s answer is an integrated software stack in which the elements share context, delivered through its vDefend and Avi Load Balancer product lines, Mahajan explained.
“Our customers have bought multiple security products. They can’t put it together,” he said. “It’s like buying Swiss cheese. Yeah, you have pieces of security, but you have plenty of holes which people can drive through.”
Scale is the other constraint, Mahajan noted. AI workloads generate heavy east-west traffic and punish any inspection step that adds delay, which is why the company has pushed enforcement into the hypervisor rather than a separate appliance tier, part of a wider update to VMware’s security portfolio for AI-era threats. That includes firewalling and intrusion detection and prevention, with the company aiming to handle security processing at high throughput while keeping latency low.
“We are doing 75 terabits per vCenter cluster for firewalling. We are doing 17 terabits for IDS IPS, and the other aspect is also latency,” Mahajan said. “Because in AI workloads, latency matters, so our security is done at the hypervisor level.”
In other words, Broadcom is pushing security enforcement into the hypervisor to inspect traffic at scale without introducing the latency of sending it through separate security appliances. But protecting those workloads also requires visibility into what is running, Mahajan noted. Agents and Model Context Protocol services are transient, so administrators need a real-time picture of what is authorized and what is shadow IT before they can quarantine anything, and that visibility work is now landing alongside private cloud modernization programs. Bolting protection on later, once the cloud infrastructure is already carrying production AI traffic, is the failure mode executives are trying to avoid.
“It has to be at the infrastructure level; it has to be at scale,” he said. “Otherwise, when are you going to do it? Two years from now, by that time you’ll be compromised.”

articles.title: Cuánto cuesta la criptomoneda Bitcoin este día
articles.text:
El bitcoin fue la primera criptomoneda que salió al mercado. Ideada por Satoshi Nakamoto en 2008, esta divisa digital promovía un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales luego de la crisis financiera mundial que se vivió ese año.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
PUBLICIDAD
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Valor de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El costo de la criptomoneda de bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 77920.46 dólares por unidad.
Esto quiere decir que la moneda digital anotó un cambio del -1.01% en las últimas 24 horas, así como una variación del 0.0% en los últimos 60 minutos.
PUBLICIDAD
Actualmente, bitcoin se encuentra en el lugar #1 de popularidad en el mercado digital. Cabe mencionar que el máximo histórico que ha alcanzado esta criptodivisa es de 126.198 dólares por unidad.
Bitcoin alcanza un nuevo récord y lidera el auge en el mercado de las criptomonedas
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
PUBLICIDAD
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
PUBLICIDAD
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: ChatGPT volta a funcionar após falha nesta segunda (31) • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
ChatGPT volta a funcionar após falha nesta segunda (31)
Problema técnico impedia assinantes de começarem ou continuarem tarefas no ChatGPT Work.
O ChatGPT enfrentou dificuldades técnicas na tarde desta segunda-feira (31/08). Segundo a página de status da OpenAI, usuários de diversos planos pagos enfrentaram problemas na hora de começar ou continuar tarefas no ChatGPT Work, versão corporativa da inteligência artificial. Outros serviços, como a ferramenta de programação Codex, a plataforma de anúncios e o chatbot pessoal, funcionavam normalmente.
Segundo a empresa, o problema foi corrigido por volta das 17h30 (horário de Brasília), cerca de meia hora após uma correção. Antes disso, a companhia disse ter identificado uma alta latência por volta do meio-dia.
O DownDetector, que monitora falhas na web, confirmou que as queixas sobre a instabilidade no ChatGPT começaram por volta do meio-dia. As reclamações começaram a cair pouco antes das 15 até voltar ao patamar de costume às 18h.

articles.title: If space data centers feel far-fetched, why not interstellar travel? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The founders behind Starcloud, a startup with plans to operate a fleet of GPUs in orbit, have a new pitch for potential investors: A plan to send a tiny spacecraft on an 80,000 year journey to Alpha Centauri.
If they do it, it will be the first human-built object explicitly aimed for another star, and the sixth to leave our solar system.
Dubbed Fermi Explorer, the non-profit behind the mission emerged today to ask for partners, donations and advice. The initial team—Starcloud founders Philip Johnston, Adi Oltean, and Ezra Feilden, along with program manager Garret Jameson—has put together a plan to use proven space technologies to send a vehicle with a 10 cm square payload, weighing 1 kilogram, into interstellar space.
The founders say they are launching this mission in the spirit of human exploration; to achieve a historical first; and to test the limits of the Fermi paradox, which attempts to explain why we have yet to find other intelligent life in the universe, and gives the mission its name.
The mission is intended to cost about $15 million, and to launch in 2029. The non-profit is soliciting vendors to build the vehicle, funding to pay them, and scientific and artistic payloads to send, ala the sensors and Golden Record onboard NASA’s Voyager space probe, the first human spacecraft to leave our solar system.
Most plans for interstellar exploration stumble when dealing with the vast distances involved and the comparatively slow methods we have to cross them. Voyager, launched in 1977, is now about 26 billion km from Earth; Alpha Centauri, the nearest star to our solar system, is 41 trillion km away.
The last time Silicon Valley took on this challenge, a nonprofit called Breakthrough Starshot, founded in 2016 by Yuri Milner and backed by Mark Zuckerberg, envisioned a multi-billion dollar effort to use a novel laser-based propulsion system to reach Alpha Centauri in twenty to thirty years. The effort collapsed in 2025, but the dream apparently remains alive.
Fermi Explorer takes the opposite tack: Rather than pushing the frontier of technology, the goal is to use what we have already to do something.
“I also got excited and then disappointed!” Johnston said of Starshot. “That’s the reason we are doing the mission. We are hell-bent on actually launching something in three years. … the big difference with most other [interstellar] missions and the Fermi Explorer is that the others all try to do it in a human lifetime, which means billion-dollar propulsion R&D programs. We have very deliberately picked 80,000 years as the minimum viable mission.”
The plan is to launch the spacecraft on a rocket rideshare, then use efficient but low-power electric propulsion to slingshot the vehicle into a series of orbits that will eventually leave it bound for Alpha Centauri. The spacecraft is intended to be active for about 12 years before entering a final coast phase toward the other solar system.
“If a dinosaur bone can last 200 million years then a metal box can easily survive the radiation environment we expect for 50,000 years,” Johnston said. “We don’t plan on powering spacecraft up at the end of the 80,000 years. We hope that a future human civilization will intercept it.”

articles.title: NVIDIA Invests $3.5 Billion in MediaTek, Partners on NVLink Fusion
articles.text:
Monday, August 31st 2026
	
									
	
	
	
NVIDIA Invests $3.5 Billion in MediaTek, Partners on NVLink Fusion
NVIDIA announced today that it is investing $3.5 billion in MediaTek and adding new layers of collaboration between the two silicon giants. It's important to note that NVIDIA and MediaTek are already working together, as MediaTek designed an SoC called GB10 that powers NVIDIA's RTX Spark consumer products and DGX Spark mini workstations. Both companies have confirmed that they will be approaching the collaboration through NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion ecosystem. NVLink Fusion serves as an IP and chiplet framework that allows non-NVIDIA processors and accelerators to become key participants in the company's data center fabric.
MediaTek will offer the NVLink Fusion platform to its customers, which include numerous ASIC clients like Google, enabling them to connect their XPUs to the NVLink Fusion scale-up fabric using photonic or classical copper interconnects. This includes the NVLink-C2C high-bandwidth fabric, which can connect multiple nearby XPUs and is also used in the upcoming NVIDIA "Rosa" CPUs. Additionally, MediaTek will offer customers NVIDIA's newly announced NVHBM, which integrates the controller into the 3D HBM stack, significantly enhancing performance and efficiency. Compared to standard HBM4E, NVIDIA claims up to 30% more memory bandwidth, 15% lower HBM power consumption, and up to 25% more usable compute die area on the processing unit.This collaboration is also interesting because customers can hand off the entire ASIC design and manufacturing process to MediaTek, which will use NVIDIA and NVLink technologies for connectivity, memory architecture, packaging, manufacturing, and rack-scale technologies to expedite the accelerator's development. Shorter design cycles will lead to faster prototypes and production runs, and customers can even bring their own XPU designs to MediaTek to integrate with NVLink Fusion technologies. Meanwhile, NVIDIA has purchased $3.5 billion worth of convertible bonds issued by MediaTek, which could later become a significant equity share if converted.

articles.title: Trump admin shelves Cyclospora research despite record-breaking outbreak
articles.text: The Trump administration is halting vital federal research on the foodborne parasite Cyclospora, despite the record-breaking, nationwide outbreak of the diarrheal pathogen, according to Politico . Of the three research programs that represent nearly all of the Cyclospora work at the US Department of Agriculture, two have been defunded, and the third is about to lose every scientist working on it. The Trump administration is shuttering the USDA's Beltsville Agricultural Research Center near Washington, DC, and moving its work to a location in Iowa. That includes relocating the remaining Cyclospora research. Although the research is still funded, insiders told Politico that not one of the scientists working on the project plans to relocate from Maryland to Iowa. Instead, they are either retiring, being reassigned to a different project, or leaving the USDA's research services. Read full article Comments

articles.title: 650 ch, boîte de vitesses virtuelle et mode drift : la Hyundai la plus rapide de tous les temps débarque en France à prix d’or
articles.text:
Si vous regrettez la disparition de la Hyundai Ioniq 6, sachez que la marque a un très beau lot de consolation : la diabolique Ioniq 6 N, qui est officiellement commercialisée en France. Rapide comme l’éclair, cet engin de 650 ch abat le 0 à 100 km/h en 3,2 secondes, faisant de lui le modèle Hyundai le plus véloce jamais créé. Et les équipements ne manquent pas pour garantir un plaisir de conduite optimal.
Cela commence par la fonction N e-shift reproduisant les changements de rapports courts typiques d’une voiture de course. Une sonorité moteur est recrachée via les haut-parleurs pour simuler au mieux les changements de vitesse. Aussi, les reprises sont limitées en sous-régime alors que l’auto se bloque automatiquement au rupteur comme si l’on pilotait un véhicule thermique.
Une bête de circuit bardée de technologies issues du jeu vidéo
Inauguré par le Ioniq 5 N, ce système a été favorablement accueilli par la critique. Nombre de marques concurrentes développent d’ailleurs un dispositif similaire pour leurs modèles. L’ordinateur de bord spécifique permet aussi de suivre ses performances sur circuit, avec un visuel de voiture « fantôme » comme dans les jeux vidéo accompagné d’un mode drift pour faciliter la glisse sur piste.
Pour optimiser la tenue de route, la géométrie de suspension a été revue alors que l’amortissement piloté a été recalibré. Côté aérodynamisme, un travail important a aussi été fait puisque la Ioniq 6 N adopte un aileron arrière bien plus imposant que sur le modèle standard façon queue de canard. L’assise du véhicule est en outre élargie tandis que le coefficient de traînée est fixé à 0,27.
Une gestion thermique de pointe pour enchaîner les tours sans broncher
Notons ensuite que les longues sessions sur piste n’auront pas raison du groupe motopropulseur. Le système de gestion thermique composé de circuits de refroidissement distincts pour la batterie et les deux électromoteurs assure des performances constantes tour après tour. Cela est aussi rendu possible par les jantes de 20 pouces reposant sur des pneus Pirelli P Zero 5 spécialement développés pour ce modèle.
La batterie de 84 kWh autorise d’autre part 487 km d’autonomie sur le cycle WLTP. Bref, la Ioniq 6 N est davantage une sprinteuse qu’une marathonienne. Heureusement que la recharge reste de bon aloi, avec un 10 à 80 % assuré en 18 minutes sur une borne 350 kW. La dotation est XXL avec notamment l’affichage tête haute, la pompe à chaleur, les sièges ventilés, la caméra 360° et le V2L. Vu les 79 000 € réclamés, c’est bien normal ! Même si elle est légèrement plus vive, l’auto demeure en tout cas bien plus chère que la Tesla Model 3 Performance.
