articles.title: Foundry Model Router Expands from Two Regions to 28, Refreshing Its Model Pool
articles.text:
Microsoft recently expanded model router in Foundry Models from two regions to 28 for global standard deployments and 21 for data zone deployments, and refreshed the pool of models it selects from. Until this release, the router ran only in East US 2 and Sweden Central.
The pool gained Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8 and the GPT-5.6 family, and lost gpt-5-chat, gpt-5.2-chat, gpt-5.3-chat, and DeepSeek-V3.1 as those models reached end of life. Teams on the default configuration receive the change without redeploying. Teams that configured a model subset do not.
That split matters, because the announcement and the documentation describe it differently.
Sanjeev Jagtap, announcing the update, presents automatic delivery as the point of the release:
The most important detail is what you don't have to do: these updates occur automatically. The endpoint remains stable as the supported model pool is refreshed, so teams do not need to redeploy the model router to receive the update.
Christos Panagiotidis, an Azure MVP and cloud engineer, draws the distinction the announcement leaves implicit:
API stability and behavioral stability are different things.
A new model in the pool can change answer style, tool-selection behavior, structured-output reliability, latency distribution, token usage, refusal behavior, and failure patterns. As he puts it:
The response schema may remain identical while the application's business outcome changes.
For a default deployment, Jagtap's claim is accurate. Model router deploys in Balanced mode across the full supported set unless told otherwise, so a workload on defaults now has two candidates it has never evaluated, and four it may have been reaching are gone, with no deployment and no version bump.
The documentation describes the escape hatch the announcement omits. Teams can restrict routing to a chosen subset, and in that configuration new models introduced later are excluded by default until explicitly added. A team that constrained its pool is insulated from precisely the refresh the blog post celebrates. The update is opt-out, and the opt-out is a setting most teams will not have touched.
Three routing modes exist, none of them mentioned in the announcement. Balanced optimizes cost while maintaining quality and is the default. Quality targets critical work, with Microsoft naming legal review, medical summaries, and complex reasoning. Cost targets high-volume classification and simple question answering. Changes to mode or subset take up to five minutes.
A constraint published earlier this year deserves more attention than it has received, because a changing pool makes it moving rather than fixed. Microsoft states that the effective context window equals the smallest underlying model's window, and that oversized prompts succeed only if the router happens to select a model that can handle them. Adding a smaller model to a pool therefore lowers the ceiling for every request routed through it.
Two further limits sit in the same guidance. Routing decisions are text-only, so vision inputs are accepted but images do not influence which model is chosen, and audio is unsupported. And the router bills its own input prompt on top of the underlying model's cost, which means any savings claim has a markup inside it.
Anthropic models carry a prerequisite that appears as a footnote in the announcement and a troubleshooting entry in the documentation. Claude models must be deployed separately to the same Foundry account with a matching SKU before the router can select them, and referencing them in a subset without that deployment fails with an InvalidResourceProperties error. Claude Opus 4.8 joining the supported list does not make it reachable.
Microsoft frames the regional expansion in compliance terms, noting that inference requests must stay within specific geographic boundaries for regulatory, governance, or customer-trust reasons. Going from two regions to 28 changes what is practical for teams with residency obligations. What the material does not address is how a data zone constraint interacts with pool selection when a candidate model is unavailable within that boundary.
Model router honors the built-in Azure Policy for Foundry model deployment, enforced at deploy time across the portal, REST API, CLI, and ARM templates, which means the allowed publishers list needs Microsoft plus the publisher of every model in the pool. That is deploy-time governance, and it leaves an open question alongside Microsoft's recent AI Gateway tier for Azure API Management, which fronts models behind runtime policy and controls which a workload may reach. Where both are deployed, the public material does not describe how the two compose.
The announcement contains no measurement: no accuracy figures, no cost comparison against a single-model baseline, no latency overhead for the selection step. Microsoft's guidance is to treat an initial deployment as a starting configuration and benchmark it before sending production traffic, and it has published an open-source evaluation pipeline that measures quality, cost, and latency in one run, including router-aware cost math and reporting on which underlying models the router actually reaches for.
Every response names the selected model in a model field, so decisions are auditable after the fact.
For platform teams, the release makes model selection a runtime decision the platform can make, and the default configuration accepts pool changes as they arrive. Panagiotidis frames the discipline that follows: treat a pool refresh as a managed dependency update, capturing the model selected for every evaluated request, comparing against the previous period, and keeping a path to restrict the pool when an update produces unacceptable outcomes.

articles.title: Jazz brings its agentic DLP investigator to CrowdStrike's Falcon Foundry - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Jazz brings its agentic DLP investigator to CrowdStrike’s Falcon Foundry
Data loss prevention startup Jazz Security Ltd. today made its platform available as an app on CrowdStrike Holdings Inc.’s Falcon Foundry, putting its agentic investigator Melody inside the Falcon console.
Melody is built to judge whether a given data movement was a problem. Four inputs go into that call. Jazz counts the data itself, the systems it traveled between, the people involved and the business process sitting behind it. Findings reach an analyst with the supporting evidence already attached, which Jazz says filters millions of raw signals down to the handful that are genuinely high-risk.
Inside Falcon, Melody applies that business context to data protection signals the platform is already collecting. Conclusions go back into the same workflow analysts use. Installation runs to a few clicks, and customers do not have to deploy a second endpoint agent or rework existing processes.
Ido Livneh, Jazz co-founder and chief executive, said Melody “understands the data, systems, people, and intent behind every data flow, revealing the full story of what happened and why” and that “bringing that intelligence into Falcon makes advanced data-protection investigation more accessible to CrowdStrike customers.”
One early user, Cooper Machinery Services LLC’s information security engineer Ramon Espinosa Jr., said running both sets of context in one console lets analysts “focus on decisions instead of manual, time-consuming investigations.”
The app is listed on the CrowdStrike Marketplace as of today. Jazz is demonstrating the integration this week at CrowdStrike’s Fal.Con Las Vegas event that runs through Sept. 3.
Foundry is CrowdStrike’s low-code development platform for the Falcon ecosystem. The company introduced it at Fal.Con in 2023 and made it generally in October the following year, pitching it at security teams that want to build or install applications that run on Falcon data without standing up separate infrastructure.
Jazz took the top spot in the 2026 CrowdStrike Cybersecurity Startup Accelerator in March, topping a field of finalists that pitched at the RSA Conference in San Francisco. Nearly 1,000 startups applied to the eight-week, equity-free program, which CrowdStrike runs with Amazon Web Services Inc. and Nvidia Corp.’s Inception unit. Thirty-five were accepted.
CrowdStrike Chief Business Officer Daniel Bernard called the move from accelerator program to Foundry app in a single year “the kind of outcome we built it for.”
Founded in 2024 and based in Tel Aviv, Jazz formally launched in March with $61 million in funding in a round led by Glilot Capital Partners and Team8. Other investors included Encoded Ventures, MassMutual Ventures, Merlin Ventures and Ten Eleven Ventures.
Jazz says its platform needs no rule-writing, no regular expressions and no browser extension. A single agent covers generative AI use, shadow IT and personal cloud accounts, according to the company, and runs at under 1% CPU usage.

articles.title: PlayStation is hosting two State of Play presentations this week
articles.text:
PlayStation will air two back-to-back State of Play streams this week.
On Thursday, September 3 at 9 a.m., the company will go live on its YouTube and Twitch channels with a State of Play focused on games from PlayStation Studios and third-party partners, including an extended look at Square Enix’s Final Fantasy VII Revelation at the end. Right after, State of Play Japan will run, focusing on games from Japan and other Asian countries.
PlayStation didn’t mention how long the State of Plays will be, so you’ll likely want to allot a good chunk of time to watch both if interested. The company did clarify, however, that the first State of Play will be in English, while the second will be in Japanese with English subtitles.
Other than Final Fantasy VII Revelation, which is confirmed to release on all platforms sometime in early 2027, it’s unclear what to expect from these State of Plays. In terms of PlayStation Studios, some of the upcoming games include Santa Monica Studio’s God of War Laufey (Feb. 16, 2027), Naughty Dog’s Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet (TBA) and Guerrilla’s Horizon: Hunters Gathering (which was recently reported to have been retooled from a live service title).

articles.title: Berlin’s Auxxo closes Female Catalyst Fund II at €33.3 million and launches founder matchmaking platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Auxxo, a Berlin-based venture capital firm dedicated to backing teams with at least one female founder, has announced the final closing of its Auxxo Female Catalyst Fund II at €33.3 million, surpassing its prior fund by more than 75%.
The VC firm announced the first close of Female Catalyst Fund II at €26 million in July 2025, with the European Investment Fund (EIF) as the anchor investor. Besides the EIF, the fund has seen new investors including Aurum Impact, EnBW New Ventures, Cherry Ventures and Speedinvest, together with a number of family offices, business angels and founders from across Europe. The firm highlights that more than 50% of investors are women.
“We are incredibly proud of the trust placed in us by the EIF and our other LPs, investors who understand that diversity drives returns. Our network is growing not only in size but also in influence and impact. The fact that more than half of our LPs are women shows that the industry is moving towards the future we have always envisioned,” said Bettine Schmitz, co-founder and General Partner at Auxxo.
Founded in 2021 by Schmitz and Dr. Gesa Miczaika, following the earlier founding of Auxxo Beteiligungen GmbH with Fabiola Hochkirchen in 2019, Auxxo co-invests at pre-Seed and Seed stages across Europe in companies with at least one female founder holding a minimum of 20% of founder shares.
The FCF II has backed 11 companies to date. Emidat, a climate data infrastructure provider for the construction industry; Resolutiion, an AI platform that helps identify and reduce losses from commercial disputes; and Stanhope.ai, which builds more adaptable, interpretable autonomous systems for robots and drones using a neuroscience-driven approach, were announced at the first closing.
Since then, the portfolio has grown to include Marble Imaging, a developer of Earth observation satellites and AI-powered analysis tools for defence and infrastructure; Delta Labs, an AI platform that helps companies build market intelligence through synthetic customer simulations; and Radiogenesis, which uses AI to design new radiopharmaceuticals for cancer treatment.
While the fund has closed comfortably ahead of the €19 million raised for Auxxo Female Catalyst Fund I, the high point is the fact that more than half of the fund’s limited partners are women. This comes on the back of a stark reality where female-founded companies receive a disproportionately small share of European venture capital, just 16.5% of deal activity in 2025.
“We are glad to be continuing the drive for greater gender diversity in European venture capital alongside Auxxo. Diversity and financial return can go hand in hand – and we look forward to this new fund making exactly that a reality,” said Marjut Falkstedt, Chief Executive of the European Investment Fund.
Alongside the close, the firm has launched a pan-European Founder Matchmaking Platform designed to help ambitious women find co-founders and build diverse teams from the ground up. This new initiative aims to close the “co-founder gap” for women by connecting solo founders, experienced operators and capital-seeking teams. 
The platform focuses on three user groups of any gender: solo founders looking for a technical or operational “missing piece”, experienced operators ready to take the leap into entrepreneurship, and teams seeking capital, for whom Auxxo provides direct access to pre-Seed and Seed investment expertise.
Dr. Miczaika, co-founder and General Partner at Auxxo, said, “We have always seen ourselves as a bridge. With this platform, we are building the foundation of that bridge. We want to ensure that more women found startups – not someday, but now.”
The platform, now live on Auxxo’s website, is built on Auxxo’s extensive European network, including successful entrepreneurs, business angel networks, and an LP base, of which over 50% are women.

articles.title: ChatGPT and Reddit now face EU's toughest online safety rules
articles.text: OpenAI’s ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher EU rules such as removing illegal content or face potential fines, the European Commission said on Monday, as Brussels grapples with how its existing digital regulation applies to rapidly evolving AI services. The Commission said the chatbot, social media forum Reddit, and gaming platform Roblox would be classified as so-called very large online platforms under the EU Digital Services Act, its landmark online safety regime. The designation means all three services will face additional obligations such as removing illegal content and protecting the privacy and security of minors and could face fines of up to 6 percent of their global revenue if they fail to comply. articles.title: Nvidia and Intel supplier Unimicron under investigation over alleged relabeling of Chinese parts
articles.text:
What just happened? Taiwanese prosecutors are investigating Unimicron Technology over allegations that the company relabeled printed circuit boards made in China as products of Taiwan. The case has put fresh attention on supply-chain compliance at a company whose PCB and advanced packaging materials serve high-performance computing, AI, and smartphone markets.
Investigators from the Taoyuan District Prosecutors Office searched Unimicron's headquarters in Guishan District and a manufacturing plant in Zhongli District on Friday. Fourteen executives and employees were questioned. Prosecutors have not announced charges, and the investigation is continuing.
The case centers on allegations that Unimicron sent China-made PCBs to Taiwan and changed their labels to show Taiwan as the country of origin. Prosecutors said the case involves suspected violations of Criminal Code provisions related to document forgery and false product-origin markings. The office said it would continue gathering evidence.
A PCB department general manager surnamed Wang was released on NT$15 million (about $474,263) bail. A deputy general manager surnamed Wu was released on NT$12 million bail. Three others posted bail ranging from NT$300,000 to NT$5 million, while nine people were released without bail.
Unimicron spokesperson Chung Ming-feng said the company is "fully cooperating with the investigation regarding disputes over product origins."
The case has drawn attention because Unimicron supplies materials used in advanced semiconductor packaging. The company is a major producer of Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) substrates, which are used in high-performance computing, AI, and smartphone chips. It also makes printed circuit boards.
Unimicron counts Nvidia and Intel among its customers. It is not known whether either company is connected to the products being investigated, whether the boards were exported to the United States, or whether the matter involves ABF substrates.
The allegations raise questions for buyers of electronics components that must track where parts are made and how they are documented. Country-of-origin claims can affect customs treatment, trade compliance, and sourcing decisions, particularly for hardware used in AI servers and other advanced computing systems.
The inquiry comes as US officials increase scrutiny of technology supply chains linked to China, especially those involving advanced AI-related hardware. If prosecutors find that China-made goods were moved through Taiwan and relabeled before export, the issue could prompt closer reviews by customers and regulators.
Image credit: Taipei Times

articles.title: Key Nvidia and Intel supplier raided over alleged China origin fraud — Unimicron faces probe over PCB origin washing, risk of 40% U.S. tariff penalty
articles.text:
Key Nvidia and Intel supplier raided over alleged China origin fraud — Unimicron faces probe over PCB origin washing, risk of 40% U.S. tariff penalty
Suspects have been released on bail pending investigation.
Taiwanese prosecutors are investigating Unimicron, one of the world’s largest PCB and chip substrate makers and a key supplier to Nvidia, Intel, Google, and Amazon, over allegations that it shipped China-made PCBs back to Taiwan and relabeled them as Taiwanese products, according to Nikkei Asia. Investigators raided the company’s headquarters in Taoyuan’s Guishan District and a manufacturing plant in Zhongli District on August 28, questioning 14 employees as suspects — including the general and deputy general managers of its PCB business — and four more people as witnesses.
Prosecutors say that the alleged conduct contravened Articles 216, 210, and 255 of Taiwan’s Criminal Code, which cover the use of forged private documents and false labeling of an item’s origin. Wang, the person identified as the PCB department general manager, was released on bail of NT$15 million (roughly $473,000), while a deputy general manager identified as Wu was released on NT$12 million (roughly $378,000).
Three others are said to have posted bail ranging from NT$300,000 to NT$5 million, and the remaining nine were released without bail. "There was strong suspicion that they had violated Taiwan's law covering the use of forged private documents and false labeling of goods," the Taoyuan District Prosecutors Office said in a statement. Unimicron told the Taiwan stock exchange that it’s fully cooperating with the investigation and that it doesn’t expect a material impact on its operations.
Since August last year, U.S. Customs and Border Protection has applied an additional 40% tariff on goods that it determines were transshipped through third countries to evade duties, on top of any other applicable penalties, and the agency has no authority to waive or otherwise mitigate the charge. If any relabeled Unimicron PCBs were to reach the U.S., that penalty would fall on the company’s American customers as importers of record.
The White House has identified 40 countries and territories that it says pose an elevated risk of illegal transshipment, with Taiwan flagged as a key concern. Taipei has been running major crackdowns on “origin washing,” where companies claim goods are made in Taiwan to obtain preferential tariff treatment, a crackdown that’s perhaps perfectly illustrated by the fact that prosecutors published names and bail amounts within 24 hours of raiding one of the country’s most important listed tech companies. After all, the “Made in Taiwan” label is ultimately a trade asset whose value rests on the fact that it’s not “Made in China.” Since its elevated risk designation, Taiwan is understandably keen to show Washington that it polices the difference itself rather than leaving it to U.S. Customs.
The products involved in this crackdown appear to be conventional PCBs, not the high-end ABF substrates used for Intel’s EMIB-T platform or Nvidia’s advanced data center accelerators. Unimicron’s offshore manufacturing remains in China for standard substrates, PCBs, HDI, and flexible boards, while its advanced CoWoS-related substrate capacity is based at its Yangmei factory in Taoyuan.
If the case concerns relabeling on individual products, the fallout will be limited to the Taiwanese prosecution. If, however, it turns out that China-made goods were transshipped through Taiwan to alter their origin before export to the U.S., that’s an entirely different story and could trigger CBP’s 40% transshipment penalty on the affected goods, along with potential retroactive duty reassessments, which would hit Unimicron’s American customers as importers of record.

articles.title: Upcoming Intel Arc G3-powered gaming handhelds are being let down by sky-high price tags
articles.text:
Intel Arc G3 handhelds offer amazing performance, but good luck actually being able to afford them
Faster, smoother, better... and way pricier
It has been a few months since Intel rolled out XeSS 3 with its Multi-Frame Generation to any Arc-supported device. With the unveiling of dedicated handheld gaming PCs using the tech, such as the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, Acer Predator Atlas 8, and OneXPlayer 3, hardware manufacturers are finally cashing in on the promised performance capabilities that were previously only dreamt about: no-compromise playable framerates and high-resolution PC gaming in your pocket.
Multi-Frame Generation and AI-powered upscaling technology like Nvidia DLSS and AMD FSR have become essential for PC gaming in 2026. Even the best graphics cards on the market need a boost from a hand-tuned algorithm that interlaces generated frames with purely rasterized ones. In short, that means a higher-than-native framerate with a (hopefully) minimal impact on image fidelity.
Intel XeSS 3 is Team Blue's latest version of the tech, and its USP for how it works with Arc graphics isn't relegated to the best gaming PCs or the best gaming laptops. Now, as the Intel Arc G3 lineup makes its way to new handhelds, MFG becomes a reality for the form factor. Finally, Full HD (1080p) at playable framerates on a small, portable, handheld gaming device. However, it's not all good news; it comes at a cost, and it could bury the appeal of these devices completely.
The Intel Arc G3 lineup is a geniune generational leap for handheld gaming
The core of the Intel Arc G3 Extreme chips, and the rest of the lineup, can best be summarized in four core pillars: Performance, Integration, Efficiency, and Software.
It's the third generation of the purpose-built SoCs from Team Blue, primarily built for handheld devices. Intel promises AI-based upscaling, MFG, DirectX 12 Ultimate support, and full ray tracing at a low wattage with high performance capabilities. It's claimed that the company's partner devices, such as the aforementioned MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ and Acer Predator Atlas 8, can expect up to 11 hours of gameplay, while being "up to 42% faster than the competition on average".
It's early days for Intel's partner devices, which are yet to properly hit the market; however, the company's internal benchmarks give us a rough idea of how much more capable the G3 Extreme is at 35W when weighed up against the previous-generation Arc graphics found in the Intel Core Ultra 7 258V at 30W. In 1080p in High settings, there's a clear performance gap of anywhere from 18% to 47% when directly compared generation-on-generation.
Intel claims the G3 Extreme is up to 44% faster on average, and this performance gap is most evident when looking at how the newer SoC handles demanding games. The Ultra 7 258V can't quite hit a stable, playable 30 FPS in the likes of Crimson Desert or Assassin's Creed Shadows here, but you can expect a respective 34 FPS and 35 FPS average from the G3 Extreme. Crossing that all-important 1080p at 60 FPS mark is also now possible, particularly in intensive software such as Battlefield 6, Pragmata, Baldur's Gate 3, and Dying Light: The Beast, just to name a few examples.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The numbers are similar when comparing the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ with the Intel Arc G3 Extreme at 35W versus the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X with the AMD Z2 Extreme chip as well. There's a similar 42% performance improvement on average in 1080p in High settings with upscaling enabled by default.
In fact, in some cases, the Intel Arc G3 Extreme nearly doubles the performance potential of the previous fastest chip in a handheld gaming PC to date. This is particularly noticeable with Death Stranding 2: On the Beach and Arc Raiders; Team Blue's SoC achieved average framerates of 56 and 100 in those games (respectively), whereas Team Red's silicon lagged behind with 37 and 67. The Z2 still produces playable figures, at least as much as a stable 30 FPS and above can accommodate from a handheld; however, it's a night-and-day difference with the Xe3 cores here.
XeSS 3 as a package incorporates Super Resolution (AI upscaling) as well as MFG and low-latency responsiveness. The revised silicon has meant that Team Blue has been able to facilitate not only playable framerates at 35W, but also 17W and 12W as well, with some concessions, as you would expect. For transparency, the maximum wattage means it has to be plugged into mains power or be receiving power delivery through USB-C PD, etc.
On battery, the Intel Core G3 Extreme is still 24% faster than the Intel Core Ultra 7 258V at 17W, meaning 1080p at High settings, making 30 FPS and above possible from many of the aforementioned demanding games. It also means 1080p at 60 FPS and beyond for many titles, such as Resident Evil Requiem and Diablo 4, which are pretty intense for their respective genres as well.
Playability at 12W has been a challenge for even the best gaming handhelds, especially when trying to balance the longest battery life and settling for a dimmer display just to get a long play session in. This is where the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ with the Intel Arc G3 Extreme demonstrates the power efficiency of Team Blue's new chip; 1080p in Low settings on a display that small is a necessary compromise, but it means 30 FPS in the likes of Battlefield 6, Clair Obscur Expedition 33, and Dying Light: The Beast, which wasn't previously possible from AMD's Z2 chip, while also managing 60 FPS+ averages in older games, such as Shadow of the Tomb Raider, F1 25, and Grand Theft Auto V.
Eye-watering price tags show the cost of progress
Now that I've outlined just how capable the Intel Arc G3 Extreme chip is, it's time for the stinger. The three confirmed handhelds that utilize Team Blue's new chips are incredibly expensive, nearly double the cost of a Steam Deck OLED (even post-price hike), and a heftier amount than the AMD Z2 Extreme alternatives, like the MSI Claw A8, and the Lenovo Legion Go 2. That's a depressing (although not surprising) reality of the PC gaming market in 2026; your money doesn't go very far for the parts, owing to the ongoing RAM crisis, making components scarce and in higher demand than ever.
The new era of handheld gaming PCs has performance that feels like a dream, but with truly nightmare pricing. Confirmed UK pricing for the Acer Predator Atlas 8 shows you just how much you'll need to splash out. The base model features a standard G3 chip with 16GB RAM and a 512GB SSD for £999.99 (around $1,363 / AU$1,915). However, if you want the G3 Extreme variant, it's available in two RAM configurations: 24GB and 32GB, each with a 1TB SSD for £1,299.99 (about $1,772 / $AU2,490) and £1,499 (approx $2,043 / AU$2,871), respectively.
Pre-orders for the OneXPlayer 3 are also available for a similar rate in the US, with the product expected to ship in "late August". If you hoped that a smaller company would undercut the major players, then you're sadly mistaken. It's being sold exclusively with the Intel Arc G3 Extreme chip inside, with the three variants this side of the launch window confirmed to cost $1,499 (about £1,100 / $AU2,100) for 24GB RAM and 512GB SSD, $1,599 (around £1,170 / $AU2,245) for 24GB RAM and 1TB SSD, and $1,799 (approx £1,319 / $AU2,527) for 32GB RAM and 1TB SSD. That's the early bird pricing, though, as buying after launch will see the rates rise to $1,699 (about £1,245, $1,899 (around £1,392 / AU$2,667), and $2,099 (approx £1,539 /AU$2949), respectively.
Priced out of the next generation
While the early benchmarks are impressive, you just aren't getting good value from a price-to-performance perspective here. We're still talking about 1080p at 60 FPS or above, which is palatable for a device costing around $500 / £500 / AU$1,000, but a real hard sell when it's at least three times that amount at minimum (or more) for less than a 50% generational performance boost. Form factor aside, even with the current price gouging of components, you can pick up a far more capable RTX 5070 laptop for less, such as the Acer Nitro V 16 AI, the MSI Katana 15 HX, or the Gigabyte Gaming A16.
It begs the question of exactly who the next generation of handheld gaming PCs will be for. We know the Intel Arc G3 Extreme chip carries a high asking price at a time when people don't have the cash to burn; if you're already a PC gamer, you have a desktop or a laptop of some description, and shelling out over $1,000 / £1,000 / AU$2,000 for a secondary machine isn't going to be worthwhile for the vast majority of people. If you game on an Xbox Series X, PS5, or Nintendo Switch 2, however, there's even less reason to consider handheld PC gaming: you would potentially be spending double (or even triple) the cost of the console for objectively worse gaming performance.
These high prices betray what made the likes of the Steam Deck so revolutionary back in 2022. The killer handheld was easy to use and powerful enough, but (most importantly), it was competitively priced. The original LCD variant shipped starting at $399 / £349 to $649 / £569, depending if you wanted eMMC storage or a proper NVMe SSD inside. Hardware manufacturers still haven't got the key messaging that made Valve's handheld such a success when it was revealed nearly five years ago: it has to be cheap enough to justify the investment and powerful enough to play your games. Backed by the aging RDNA 2 semi-custom hardware and a respectable 720p screen, it achieves this goal.
So where do we go from here, then? It feels as though we're back to where we started with handheld gaming PCs that made them niche, luxury items from boutique manufacturers rather than viable ways to play PC games on the go. The performance potential of Intel Arc G3 Extreme (and XeSS 3 in general) cannot be understated; however, it's come at too high a cost, which means this incoming next-generation could be the turning point that buries the concept completely.

articles.title: Ocultações lunares de planetas, movimento retrógrado e mais no Calendário Astronômico de setembro
articles.text:
Setembro promete um prato cheio para os amantes da astronomia. Nos próximos dias, a Lua vai ocultar dois planetas no céu, um gigante de gelo entrará em movimento retrógrado e outro chegará à sua melhor posição do ano para ser observado da Terra.
Lembrando que todas as datas e horários fornecidos têm como referência um observador em Brasília (DF) e podem variar ligeiramente de acordo com a localidade. Para acompanhar com precisão, a dica é usar aplicativos como Star Walk, Stellarium ou SkySafari, que mostram a posição exata dos objetos celestes com base em onde você está.
Calendário astronômico de setembro
8 de setembro: Ocultação lunar de Júpiter
A Lua passará na frente de Júpiter em uma espécie de “eclipse” chamada ocultação lunar. O fenômeno será visível em locais como Estados Unidos, Canadá, Groenlândia e leste da Rússia. Como a posição da Lua no céu varia conforme o ponto de observação na Terra, nem todos verão esse evento. No entanto, em outros lugares do mundo, como no Brasil, por exemplo, ainda será possível acompanhar os dois corpos bem próximos no céu, em uma conjunção astronômica.
10 de setembro: Urano entra em “movimento retrógrado”
Neste dia, Urano começa um processo pelo qual seu trânsito normal para o leste através do céu noturno é interrompido, mudando a trajetória para oeste – evento que é popularmente conhecido como “movimento retrógrado”. Para a astronomia, a designação mais adequada, no entanto, é “laço” retrógrado. Isso porque, durante o curso percorrido, o planeta parece formar um laço no céu.
De acordo com o guia de orientação astronômica In-The-Sky.org, a inversão de direção do gigante de gelo começará às 16h28 (pelo horário de Brasília). Ele, então, retoma o sentido habitual em 8 de fevereiro de 2027.
14 de setembro: Ocultação lunar de Vênus
A Lua vai “eclipsar” Vênus no céu em uma ocultação lunar visível em partes da Ásia, África, Europa e oeste da Rússia. O evento é restrito a essas regiões por uma questão de perspectiva geográfica. No Brasil, será possível observar a dupla bem próxima no céu durante a noite, em uma conjunção astronômica.
22 de setembro: Equinócio de setembro.
O equinócio é um fenômeno astronômico que ocorre quando o Sol incide diretamente sobre a Linha do Equador. Com isso, os dois hemisférios recebem a mesma quantidade de luz, fazendo com que o dia e a noite tenham praticamente a mesma duração em todo o planeta.
O fenômeno acontece duas vezes por ano: em março, marcando o início da primavera no Hemisfério Norte e do outono no Hemisfério Sul; e em setembro, com o início do outono no Hemisfério Norte e da primavera no Hemisfério Sul.
25 de setembro: Netuno em oposição
Netuno estará mais brilhante e visível do que em qualquer outro momento do ano. Por estar a bilhões de quilômetros da Terra, ele continua inacessível a olho nu. No entanto, usando um telescópio ou binóculos astronômicos, esta é a melhor época do ano para tentar observá-lo.
Em algum momento de setembro, a sonda Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice), da Agência Espacial Europeia (ESA), fará um sobrevoo da Terra para ajustar sua trajetória e ganhar as condições necessárias para seguir viagem pelo Sistema Solar. A manobra faz parte de uma série de assistências gravitacionais que ajudam a espaçonave a chegar a Júpiter sem precisar gastar tanto combustível.
Depois desse encontro, a Juice ainda voltará a passar perto da Terra, em janeiro de 2029, em um último sobrevoo antes de seguir em direção ao gigante gasoso, onde deve chegar em julho de 2031.
Flávia Correia é jornalista do Olhar Digital, cobrindo Ciência e Espaço.

articles.title: Sony revela por qué ya no impulsa "agresivamente" las ventas de la PS5
articles.text:
Parece ayer que la PS5 llegó al mercado, pero la realidad dicta que ya pasaron casi seis años desde su debut en el mercado. Es cierto que al principio fue prácticamente imposible de conseguir, y tal vez eso todavía influya en sentir que no ha pasado tanto tiempo desde su lanzamiento. Sea como sea, la consola ya se encuentra en la segunda mitad de su ciclo de vida y eso es algo que no solo se refleja en el calendario, sino también en sus cifras de ventas.
La comercialización de la PS5 ha pasado su etapa dorada, habiendo incluso registrado una fuerte caída en el último tiempo. En mayo se conoció que durante el trimestre previo se habían vendido "apenas" 1,5 millones de unidades, lo que marcaba un descenso del 46 % interanual. Sony entiende que esto es parte de un proceso lógico y que no corresponde exclusivamente a las subidas de precio que ha sufrido el producto. Es por ello que tampoco están promocionando el dispositivo con fiereza para que sus ventas repunten.
Hiroki Totoki, CEO de Sony, fue bastante abierto sobre este asunto durante una reciente entrevista con The Wall Street Journal. El empresario japonés reconoció que la etapa de vender "agresivamente" la PS5 ha quedado en el pasado y que hoy el enfoque está puesto en otra parte del negocio. Puntualmente, el directivo habló de generar ingresos recurrentes de los usuarios ya existentes, un punto en el que las suscripciones a PlayStation Plus juegan un papel crucial.
Sony quiere generar más ingresos de los usuarios de PS5 ya existentes
"Estamos en la segunda mitad del ciclo de vida de una consola PlayStation. Eso significa que no necesitamos 'vender agresivamente' la consola hoy. Y en lugar de eso, nos centramos en los ingresos recurrentes de la base de usuarios recurrente. Y PlayStation Plus ya tiene más de 125 millones de usuarios activos mensuales en la actualidad, y cómo monetizar a esos usuarios es muy importante para nosotros", explicó Totoki.
La PS5 ha sido una apuesta realmente exitosa para Sony, y eso está a la vista. Los números de ventas más recientes hablan de más de 95 millones de unidades vendidas en todo el mundo, un número excelente y al que ha llegado quebrando varios récords. Queda claro, entonces, por qué a la compañía japonesa ya no le quita el sueño seguir impulsando las ventas del dispositivo.
Ojo, que eso no significa que a la compañía no le importe seguir vendiendo consolas. Con GTA 6 a la vuelta de la esquina y un vistazo extendido al juego que ha revalidado las cualidades técnicas de la consola, no es ilógico pensar que pueda haber un repunte en ventas hacia finales de año, coincidiendo con el debut del título de Rockstar.
Con casi seis años sobre sus espaldas, la PS5 también está allanando el camino al arribo de su sucesora. Sony todavía no ha dado demasiados detalles sobre la PS6, aunque sí ha reconocido que la escasez y el encarecimiento de componentes claves está complicando sus planes. Sea como sea, una sucesora de la PlayStation 5 no llegaría hasta dentro de dos años, como mínimo.

articles.title: Apply now to host a Side Event at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
We’re getting close to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026! From October 13-15, more than 10,000 innovators, founders, investors, and industry leaders will attend our event in San Francisco’s Moscone West, but the community gathering in the Bay Area stretches beyond those three days.
With our Disrupt Side Events program, you can bring people together anytime from October 10-16 for a custom event that gets promoted to Disrupt’s attendees. But time is running out — our deadline to apply for Side Events is this Friday, September 4, at midnight PT, so the time to apply is now!
What are the benefits of a Side Event?
Hosting a Side Event puts you in control of how your community meets up, placing your brand front and center with the people who matter most. Whether you’re a VC looking to spark conversations, a company ready to showcase breakthrough innovation, or a community builder with something to say, this is your moment to:
- Engage directly with thousands of the sharpest minds in tech.
- Build authentic relationships with potential partners, investors, and collaborators.
- Own your narrative and showcase your expertise on your terms.
- Generate buzz that extends far beyond the event itself.
Approved Side Events are all promoted to Disrupt attendees and the rest of our audiences through the official Side Events calendar and marketing channels.
What Side Events can you host?
Anything that aligns with your vision is likely to be approved. Everything from industry roundtables and VC office hours to deep-dive workshops to intimate dinners and casual networking happy hours have succeeded at past Disrupt events.
The format is yours to design — we just ask that you bring the energy and make sure it’s open to both Disrupt attendees and the broader public. We recommend hosting events that take place in the evenings during Disrupt from October 13-15, as there’s less competition and more post-conference excitement to fuel meaningful conversations with undivided audiences.
How can I apply for a Side Event?
You can look at the application form here, but it’s helpful to have a few things locked in before starting the application process:
- Have a venue selected in the Bay Area — this is all about in-person experiences.
- Have a title, description, and venue prepared for the event.
- Double-check the Side Events Host Guide and the Side Event Host T&Cs.
If you have additional questions, we’re here to help! Just email our Side Events team and we’ll follow up to help.
We prioritize events that provide meaningful value to founders, investors, and the startup community, but aside from that, you know your community and ideal audience the best! There’s zero cost to apply and participate, so let’s hear your ideas.
Apply by September 4 to be a part of Disrupt
Apply now and tell us your vision, goals, and what you need logistically in your application, and we’ll handle the rest to give your team the support and exposure you need to make the most of the community and opportunity Disrupt brings to San Francisco and the Bay Area.

articles.text:
Is Someone Hacking DoD Refrigerators?
The stores confirmed to be affected include Fort Irwin, Calif.; F.E. Warren Air Force Base, Wyo.; Fort Huachuca, Ariz.; Naval Station Newport, R.I.; Columbus Air Force Base, Miss.; and Travis Air Force Base, Calif., according to announcements made online by each installation.
Naval Air Station Lemoore, Calif., also experienced an outage, according to M. Elizabeth, writer of the Substack newsletter Signal and Silence.
Each service declined to answer questions about how many bases are affected by the outages, referring all questions to the Defense Department. Pentagon officials did not respond to questions.
However, a defense official said the department is aware of a “possible refrigeration disruption at some Defense Commissary Agency commissaries.” The official was not authorized to comment publicly and spoke on the condition of anonymity.
All speculation at this point, but it’s hard to come up with another explanation for the coincidence.

articles.title: JBL takes on Sonos with new multi-room Cove speakers
articles.text:
JBL is well known for its portable bluetooth and party speakers, but now it’s also stepping into the world of connected whole-home audio. The JBL Cove series of speakers introduced today can work independently, as a stereo pair, or linked together to form a multi-room sound system, placing the range in competition with Sonos and Bose’s new Lifestyle Ultra speakers.
JBL takes on Sonos with new multi-room Cove speakers
The Cove series includes three speaker models that work alone or within a connected audio system.
There are three models in the JBL Cove series, which come in a choice of black or white color options and will be available starting September 13th. There’s the compact $229.95 Cove M1, which includes three 0.75-inch tweeters and a single 4-inch woofer, but requires a wired power source. The larger $399.95 Cove P1 has Dolby Atmos support and the added convenience of being battery-powered, with up to 14 hours of playtime, according to JBL. The $449.95 Cove X1 is the flagship model, which also needs to be plugged into a power outlet, but features four 1.25-inch tweeters and dual 4-inch woofers alongside Dolby Atmos support.
The Cove speakers connect together through Wi-Fi and can be managed through the JBL One app for controlling music streams and room groupings. Notable features include automatic self-tuning, JBL’s “AI Sound Boost” technology to prevent audio distortion at high volumes, and a “Music Follows Me” feature that transfers audio to the room you’re in without resorting to a phone, by long-pressing the Moment button on the closest speaker.
Supported services include Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect, Qobuz Connect, AirPlay 2, Google Cast, and Roon Ready. US Alexa Plus subscribers can also access the Amazon assistant through Cove speakers, including voice-activated smart home controls. Each speaker also supports Bluetooth for a direct connection with phones and tablets, and can connect with JBL’s Bar Series MK2 soundbars for an expanded home theater experience.

articles.title: Lake Ontario now 'Lake America' on Google Maps in the U.S.
articles.text:
U.S. President Donald Trump signed an order to rename Lake Ontario to “Lake America,” on August 27.
Since then, Google Maps has changed the name of the lake depending on which side of the border you’re on.
The Lake Ontario label changes depending on where you’re based.
- Canadian users will see Lake Ontario
- US users will see Lake America
- Everyone else will see Lake Ontario (Lake America)
This is a similar approach to what Google did when Trump renamed the Gulf of Mexico, the Gulf of America. Google says that its policy is to use the name assigned by the U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS).
How the Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) Lake Ontario/Lake America name change in the US will appear on Google Maps pic.twitter.com/nFw80TwaqH
— News from Google (@NewsFromGoogle) August 30, 2026
Apple Maps, on the other hand, hasn’t yet made any changes. Apple Maps did change Gulf of America, though, so I wouldn’t be surprised if we see a similar update with Lake America, but I’m hoping that Apple stands up against the man.
Le nom du lac Ontario tire son origine du mot wendat « Ontari’io », qui signifie « le lac est beau, le lac est grand ».
Ce nom remonte à plus de 400 ans, bien avant la Confédération canadienne et la Déclaration d’indépendance des États-Unis d’Amérique.
Nous savons que les…
— Mark Carney (@MarkJCarney) August 27, 2026
Of course, we at MobileSyrup would never call it Lake America and will be sticking with Lake Ontario. Most people in the country have made fun of Trump, and thankfully our government continues to support the true Canadian lake title ‘Lake Ontario.’
It’s Lake Ontario, now and always. pic.twitter.com/KNahtPAMeJ
— Doug Ford (@fordnation) August 29, 2026
Source: Google Blog

articles.title: China's CXMT beats Western chipmakers to announcement of LPDDR6 mass production — Xiaomi smartphones to debut industry’s first LPDDR6 chips
articles.text:
China's CXMT beats Western chipmakers to announcement of LPDDR6 mass production — Xiaomi smartphones to debut industry’s first LPDDR6 chips
LPDDR6 arrives in less than a year after CXMT started mass-producing LPDDR5.
ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has announced in a social media post that it has started mass production of LPDDR6 memory for a Xiaomi smartphone, Reuters reports. This is not entirely unexpected given the general LPDDR6 mass-production timeline, but the announcement is still surprising because two China-based companies are ahead of industry announcements. Yet, there are caveats.
LPDDR6 is perhaps the most substantial upgrade to the GDDR-class memory ever. Firstly, it uses PAM3 signaling, which encodes 3 bits of information across two symbols, compared with the NRZ signaling used by LPDDR5/LPDDR5X. Second, the data transfer rate increases to 43.2 GT/s. Third, the reduced I/O width from 32 bits to 24 bits requires rework at both the hardware and software levels.
Given the differences between LPDDR5 and LPDDR6, the most important factor here is not exactly LPDDR6 manufacturing, but a broader view.
On the one hand, CXMT reached mass production of LPDDR6 roughly at the same time as the established DRAM leaders, meaning it is on par with them, if not ahead. This marks a substantial change from earlier generations, when Chinese DRAM technology generally lagged considerably behind Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron.
On the other hand, reaching mass production does not necessarily mean that CXMT has achieved full technological or manufacturing parity with its larger rivals. The official announcement covers only one smartphone maker and one model, meaning CXMT's LPDD6 still has to pass validation for other handsets and other makers.
Still, the significance of CXMT's announcement is hard to understate. CXMT is no longer merely catching up by introducing a new memory generation years after its international competitors. With LPDDR6, CXMT is entering the market during the standard's initial commercialization, which means the technology gap between China's leading DRAM producer and the industry's established players has narrowed considerably.
Which brings us to the question of whether CXMT can maintain this pace. Developing a competitive LPDDR6 device is one thing, producing it at high yields and in sufficient volumes to supply major customers is another. For now, we are talking about a niche smartphone with memory operating at undisclosed performance.

If CXMT can mass-produce LPDDR6 for the whole market and manufacturers, we may well have seen the change of the industry leader. Yet, given one niche device, we certainly cannot say so for now.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (August 31, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (August 31, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, August 31, 2026.
Athletes continue to inspire with super human performance as government readies further investments, YourStory brings you today’s headlines and the latest news across sectors.
Featured stories
How Shashruti Nakade went from a swimmer to a top para triathlete
Shashruti Nakade has gone from winning swimming medals to becoming a para-triathlete ranked World No. 9. After narrowly missing the Paris Paralympics, she is now working towards qualifying for the LA 2028 Games.
Read more
Key developments
NIIF raises Rs 19,000 Cr as first close in second fund
The National Investment and Infrastructure Fund Limited (NIIF), India's sovereign-anchored alternative asset manager has raised Rs 19,000 crore as the first close for its Rs 30,000 crore NIIF Infrastructure Fund II. The first close is anchored by the government of India and also saw participation from sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, insurance companies and leading Indian financial institutions.
Zomato tightens food safety norms, bans imitation cheese and paneer
Food delivery aggregator Zomato on Monday announced a zero-tolerance policy on the sale of analogue dishes including analogue cheese, paneer or other dairy products by restaurants listed on its platform, saying it reserves the right to delist non-compliant restaurants.
Govt notifies Rs 1,27,500-cr Semicon 2.0
The government on Monday notified the Semicon 2.0 scheme, setting in motion the Rs 1,27,500-crore plan that seeks to deepen India's semiconductor ambitions--from chip manufacturing to a full-stack ecosystem encompassing indigenous design and IP, equipment, materials, advanced packaging, R&D and talent development.
Funding news
DocPharma raises $2M led by Equentis
Healthcare quick-commerce supply chain platform DocPharma has raised $2 million in a Pre-Series A funding round led by Equentis. Existing investor 100Unicorns, along with Vinners and a consortium of strategic angel investors, also participated in the round. The company plans to use the fresh capital to build 100 new compliant and licensed dark stores, expand into newer cities and strengthen its infrastructure.
DocPharma has developed a proprietary SaaS platform integrating warehouse management, inventory intelligence, order management and fulfillment into a single operating system for healthcare. The platform offers real-time inventory visibility, routes orders to the nearest compliant fulfilment centre and enables prescription-compliant processing. It serves e-pharmacies, insurers, hospitals, wellness and other platforms, enabling delivery of medicines and healthcare products in under 30 minutes.
YOGa Clean Air raises Rs 20 Cr led by Info Edge Ventures
Cleantech startup YOGa Clean Air has raised Rs 20 crore in a funding round led by Info Edge Ventures, with participation from Zomato/Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal and Three Words Capital. The company plans to use the capital for expansion activities. Founded in 2010, YOGa has developed clean air bubble technology designed to filter incoming air and maintain a slightly higher pressure inside a space, preventing polluted air from entering. The system also manages carbon dioxide levels to keep indoor air fresh.
YOGa’s products have been installed across homes, hospitals, schools, offices and gyms in 11 cities. Co-founder and CEO Sachin Panwar said the funding would help the company take its clean-air technology to more homes, schools and hospitals across the country.
Other news
PhonePe launches UPI 123Pay for feature phone users
PhonePe has launched PhonePe UPI 123Pay, bringing UPI payment capabilities to feature phone users across India without requiring an internet connection. The service will come pre-bundled on devices from Nokia, HMD, Lava International and Itel Mobile, with additional handset manufacturer partnerships expected in the coming months. Built on a proprietary technology stack for feature phones, UPI 123Pay uses an SMS-based architecture designed to enable transactions even in areas with limited 2G connectivity.
Users can make peer-to-peer transfers through mobile numbers or UPI IDs and make peer-to-merchant payments using UPI IDs and QR code scanning. The service also allows users to check account balances and transaction histories. Upcoming features include bill payments, recharges and Aadhaar-based UPI onboarding, supported by an AI-powered voice helpline in English and 12 Indian languages.
MapmyIndia Mappls and ClarityX launch Geo-FI lending intelligence platform
MapmyIndia Mappls, in partnership with AI-driven data analytics and decision intelligence company ClarityX, has launched Geo-FI, a geo-intelligence stack designed for the lending sector. The platform aims to provide BFSI companies with a comprehensive view of borrower risk and opportunity by adding spatial intelligence to existing lending technology. Geo-FI integrates with loan origination systems, loan management systems, CRM and collections platforms without disrupting existing workflows. It can be deployed through APIs, spatial visualisation tools and SDKs, with on-premises, hybrid and cloud options.
The platform supports multiple stages of lending, including market identification, underwriting, location verification and collections. It uses geo-tagged field intelligence, delinquency heatmaps and AI-driven workflows to identify emerging risk clusters, recommend collection priorities and continuously improve location intelligence through customer and field-level data.
Paisabazaar says AI now generates 86% of new code
Financial products marketplace and free credit score platform Paisabazaar is accelerating the use of artificial intelligence across its organisation, with AI now generating around 86% of the new code written on its platform. The company said the shift is transforming how it builds and scales technology, improving development velocity and allowing teams to take on a larger product and technology roadmap.
Despite the increased role of AI, Paisabazaar is also expanding its technology team, indicating that productivity gains are being directed towards building more products and experimenting faster rather than reducing resources. AI-assisted development is being used across the engineering lifecycle, including coding, testing, debugging and documentation. Engineers continue to provide human oversight, while the company is placing greater emphasis on systems thinking, complex problem-solving, architectural decision-making and effective collaboration with AI tools.
Appinventiv launches free workspace programme for early-stage AI startups
IT services and digital transformation company Appinventiv has launched AspireHub, a dedicated workspace initiative offering free office space to early-stage AI startups in Delhi NCR. Startups with teams of one to 15 people located anywhere in Delhi NCR can apply for the programme. Selected companies will receive free workspace, high-speed internet, IT support and access to meeting rooms. Participants will also receive mentorship from Appinventiv’s leadership in areas including product development, branding and scaling.
Applications are open on a rolling basis, with startups evaluated on factors such as the founding team, product, market opportunity and execution capabilities. Appinventiv said a select number of participating startups may eventually move into a more structured incubation track, although details of that programme have not yet been announced.
Dreamtime Learning launches AI platform for schools
Dreamtime Learning has launched Dreamtime AiQ, an artificial intelligence platform designed to integrate classroom activity, student performance and stakeholder communication with existing school systems. The platform addresses the fragmentation of classroom, teaching and student engagement information across different systems by capturing and structuring day-to-day inputs. Designed to work alongside existing ERP systems, Dreamtime AiQ uses AI-led transcription and summarisation to convert classroom information into structured reports and updates. School leaders and founders can access information on classroom activity, teaching delivery and student engagement through a central dashboard, allowing them to review developments during the academic year rather than relying solely on periodic assessments.
Teachers can use the platform for administrative tasks including attendance, documentation, assignment evaluation and parent communication. Voice-enabled attendance and AI-supported assignment checking are designed to reduce routine administrative work.
Tiger Analytics named OpenAI Select Partner
Tiger Analytics has been named an OpenAI Select Partner within the OpenAI Partner Network, a global programme for partners building, selling and delivering AI solutions with OpenAI. The partnership will see Tiger Analytics work with OpenAI to help organisations build, deploy and scale AI solutions responsibly and effectively. The company will focus on accelerating enterprise AI adoption, translating advanced AI capabilities into domain-specific solutions and helping organisations maximise business outcomes. Tiger Analytics will help enterprises use OpenAI’s latest capabilities, including GPT-5.6 and ChatGPT Work, to improve productivity and address complex business challenges.
The OpenAI Partner Network brings together companies with industry expertise, delivery capabilities and customer relationships, while providing resources, enablement and support to help enterprises adopt frontier AI models and products and translate investments into measurable impact.
DashLoc launches AI-powered customer support platform DashDesk
AI-powered MarTech platform DashLoc has launched DashDesk, an AI-powered customer support platform designed to help businesses manage customer conversations, automate support operations and deliver faster, more consistent experiences from a single workspace. DashDesk brings customer support functions together on a unified platform, allowing businesses to manage tickets, streamline workflows, collaborate across teams and gain greater visibility into customer interactions.
Built around AI-led automation, the platform combines omnichannel ticket management with features including AI-assisted ticket routing, workflow automation and SLA management. It also provides knowledge base management, customer self-service portals, real-time analytics and customer satisfaction tracking. DashLoc said these capabilities are designed to help support teams improve efficiency and consistency while managing customer queries across channels through a centralised operating environment.
Salesforce expands Headless 360 for the agentic AI era
Salesforce is expanding Headless 360 as part of its evolution towards an agentic AI platform. The expanded offering includes new Model Context Protocol servers, Data 360 capabilities, Slack integrations, developer tools, reusable Skills and headless experiences across major Salesforce clouds. The company said the architecture enables authorised AI agents to securely discover, understand and take action across enterprise systems. Headless 360 is designed to turn Salesforce from a collection of enterprise applications into reusable business capabilities that AI agents can access securely.
Organisations can reuse existing Salesforce capabilities without rebuilding integrations for every new AI experience, while retaining established identity, permissions, metadata, workflows, governance and business logic. Salesforce said the approach builds on its history of openness, extending its enterprise web API philosophy to make trusted business capabilities available wherever AI agents operate.
ARC partners with Qualcomm to develop next-generation gaming devices
Indian gaming technology company ARC is building a new generation of gaming devices in collaboration with Qualcomm Technologies. The partnership will leverage Qualcomm’s expertise in high-performance computing, graphics, connectivity and gaming technologies to support ARC’s hardware development for India and other emerging markets. ARC aims to create gaming devices combining performance, portability and efficiency for a new generation of gamers. The planned devices are expected to focus on high-performance graphics, responsive gameplay, advanced connectivity and power-efficient operation.
ARC will also leverage Qualcomm Technologies’ capabilities across mobile computing, graphics, artificial intelligence, connectivity and power efficiency as it develops a broader portfolio. The company said the collaboration marks a significant step in its product roadmap, with the aim of delivering premium gaming experiences while keeping devices practical and accessible for everyday use.
PaySprint launches AI-powered multi-payment gateway platform
B2B Banking FinTech and RegTech infrastructure company PaySprint has launched SprintPGx, an intelligent multi-payment gateway platform designed for Indian enterprises. The platform connects businesses to more than 10 payment gateways through a single integration and uses artificial intelligence to route transactions in real time. PaySprint said SprintPGx is designed to address payment failures while improving conversion, reducing costs and supporting near-zero downtime without changing the customer checkout experience.
The platform operates as an intelligence layer between a merchant’s checkout page and multiple payment gateways. It analyses factors including card type, issuing bank, transaction amount, time of day and historical success rates before routing transactions to the gateway most likely to approve them. SprintPGx supports success-rate routing, cost-based routing and load balancing during peak periods such as festive sales and IPL ticketing.
NetApp named Leader in 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for enterprise storage platforms
NetApp has been recognised as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Storage Platforms, continuing its position as a Leader from the inaugural edition of the report in 2025. The evaluation considered the company’s Completeness of Vision and Ability to Execute. In Gartner’s 2026 Critical Capabilities report for Enterprise Storage Platforms, NetApp ranked first in the Hybrid Cloud Storage Use Case and second in the Hybrid Platform Services Use Case. NetApp said the recognition validates its ability to help customers address data challenges while providing more predictable hardware delivery timelines. Its platform provides governed access to data across locations and connects with AI and analytics ecosystems through hybrid multicloud storage.

articles.title: Man uses robot vacuum to catch cheating wife, wins $16,000 affair case, then gets jailed for secretly filming her
articles.text:
WTF?! A man has won a legal battle against his wife by using footage from a robot vacuum to prove she was having an affair, but it was a Pyrrhic victory. Because he secretly filmed her, he was fined around 30% of the roughly $16,000 he won and sentenced to five months in prison.
The man in Taiwan used the robot vacuum to gather evidence of his wife's extramarital affair for a civil lawsuit against her, writes the South China Morning Post.
His suspicions arose in late 2023, when he discovered a used toothbrush at the holiday home. He then checked surveillance footage from a garage and identified an unknown man who had previously driven his wife home.
It seems catching his wife in the act was an accident. Three months later, the man remotely activated their robot vacuum cleaner via its mobile application. He was planning to use it to communicate with her. Instead, his suspicions were confirmed by the vacuum's live video feed, so he decided to record everything.
The video showed the woman changing clothes, embracing the man who appeared in the previous video, and walking around the house naked while he lounged on the sofa.
The husband later used the footage to sue his wife and the man for infringement of spousal rights under Taiwan's civil law, seeking $68,000. The court found in his favor, determining that the wife's relationship with the other man had surpassed the limits of ordinary friendship, though the husband was awarded the much lower sum of around $16,000.
Things were about to get much worse for the husband. His wife countersued him for recording private, intimate footage of her without consent. She added that the sensors and lights on the vacuum weren't sufficient warning that she was being filmed.
He tried to argue that the footage had been accepted by the civil court and his actions were legally justified, but the court didn't agree. It determined that what he did was still illegal, deliberate, and that marital obligations do not supersede an individual's right to privacy.
The court fined the man NT$150,000 (about $4,741) and sentenced him to five months in prison. He actually avoided the worst-case scenario of an NT$300,000 (around $9,500) fine and three years behind bars.
With the fine deducted from his award, the man has been left with just over $11,000 and is facing nearly half a year in jail. Some on social media are angry with the court's decision, while others say there are no excuses for breaking the law.

articles.title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Instagram announced Monday that it’s changing how it labels AI-generated profiles and will start limiting the reach of accounts that feature AI-generated people without saying so.
The platform says it’s renaming its existing “AI creator” label to “AI-generated profile,” which Instagram says should make the disclosure easier to understand. The new label is meant to tell users that the person featured on a profile was generated or substantially created with AI.
Under the new policy, creators who don’t properly label an AI-generated profile could see their reach reduced. Creators who use the new label, on the other hand, won’t be penalized simply for having an AI-generated person as their profile subject.
The label also isn’t meant for every use of AI. Instagram says people who use AI to edit photos, polish captions, create graphics, or make other creative tweaks don’t need to use the AI-generated profile label.
Instagram says the change comes partly in response to users who have stumbled across profiles that looked like they belonged to real people, only to find out later that the person was completely AI-generated.
“As generative AI becomes a bigger part of how people create, we’ve heard that people don’t like seeing a profile that seems human, only to find out later that the person featured is AI-generated,” Instagram wrote. “They want to know when a profile features an AI-generated person.”
The timing is notable. Frustration over AI-generated content has been growing as AI influencers become more common across social media platforms.
For instance, earlier this year, the gay dating app Goose became the subject of a Wired investigation after a network of apparently AI-generated male influencers promoted the app on Instagram. Wired found more than two dozen accounts that appeared to feature AI influencers, some of which reportedly reached out to potential users through direct messages to get them to sign up.
Health and wellness content is another particularly worrying example. The New York Times reported in July it found hundreds of AI-generated doctors, healers, and wellness personalities on social media promoting supplements or making health claims to users.
The announcement comes after Instagram faced backlash over an AI tool that allowed users to generate images using other people’s likenesses. Users objected to having their public Instagram content used without an explicit opt-in. Meta then removed the feature.
Last week, Meta reached an $18 billion settlement with U.S. states over allegations concerning the effects of Facebook and Instagram on children and teenagers. As part of the agreement, Meta will introduce a default two-hour daily usage limit for teens across Facebook and Instagram, a “Night Mode” block, muted notifications during school hours, and other restrictions.

articles.title: Real-time context powers Intuit AI and security - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Knowledge graphs deliver the real-time context enterprises need to make AI explainable
As AI adoption accelerates and language models become commodities, enterprises are discovering that knowledge graphs provide the critical layer for turning scattered data into usable, real-time context for AI agents.
That shift is playing out inside large end-user organizations already running graph technology in production. Intuit Inc., known for its active role in open-source communities, including the Linux Foundation, has built its security data platform around graph technology to solve exactly this problem, according to Chad Cloes (pictured), staff software engineer at Intuit.
“I think graphs already were very relevant from a, ‘How do I make my data valuable? How do I make it useful? How do I monetize and/or democratize that data?'” Cloes said. “We have found at Intuit that the graph layer gives that contextualization — it’s a byproduct. The byproduct of it is you can hand all that context that you’ve built with the graph to your LLM.”
Cloes spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier at the Neo4j GraphTalk event, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how knowledge graphs power security operations, compliance and real-time context at Intuit. (* Disclosure below.)
Knowledge graphs turn security data silos into real-time context
Intuit’s Security Knowledge and Insights Platform team built its system to connect siloed security tools and data lakes without relying on sprawling SQL joins, replacing manual lookups with automated, queryable relationships, Cloes noted.
“One of the main tenets of what we attempt to do is we attempt to drive down MTTR, which is meantime to remediate,” he said. “When we started, it would take days to do analysis on how things were connected. You have to log into seven different things. You had to have three different people with different credentials. Once you start drawing that data in and connecting it in a way that’s relevant, you again democratize the data such that it takes it from days to seconds.”
That foundation has since become the backbone for Intuit’s AI tooling, with the team building a GraphQL API on top of its graph platform to power Model Context Protocol servers that developers query in natural language. The underlying database choice matters less than the discipline of building it, Cloes noted.
“Frankly, I don’t even care who wins because I’m going to be pulling data into a graph, making it relevant and real for me,” Cloes said. “It’s going to be ChatGPT today. It’s going to be Amazon Bedrock tomorrow. It’s going to be whatever. It doesn’t really matter because I’m going to be able to contextualize and use it in the most important way.”

articles.title: Ivory Coast’s Afrikrea relaunches under original name on 10th anniversary - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Ivory Coast’s Afrikrea has announced its relaunch under its original name, marking 10 years since the site was launched, restoring a name closely associated with fashion, art, and craft from independent creators across Africa and the diaspora.
Founded in 2016 by Moulaye Tabouré, Abdoul Kadry Diallo, and Luc Perussault-Diallo on the premise of bridging the gap between independent creators across Africa and the diaspora and global audiences, Afrikrea evolved from a singular e-commerce website into ANKA, a family of commerce products.
The startup raised US$5 million in funding in 2023, and was acquired by US company Global Shop Group in 2025. It has now become Afrikrea again, however, which will be where startups shop, whilst ANKA Pay and ANKA Ship are its B2B software offerings. The relaunch of the consumer platform marks a renewed commitment to its founding mission.
“Fashion is where culture, craft, and commerce meet. Throughout my career, I have seen that the strongest businesses begin with a distinct creative point of view,” said CEO Matilda Ceesay.
“Afrikrea is returning to the name that carries that point of view: a home for African and diaspora creators whose work deserves to be seen, valued, and built into enduring businesses.”

articles.title: South African VC Mamor Capital raises $18.8 million first fund
articles.text:
For South African startups, getting customers is only half the battle. Even after people start paying for their products, raising enough money to grow can remain difficult. That is the funding gap Mamor Capital Ventures wants to target with its first venture capital fund.
The black women-owned and managed firm has raised R300 million ($18.8 million) in the first close of its inaugural fund, with the Public Investment Corporation (PIC), South Africa’s largest asset manager, as its anchor investor.
Mamor is still raising towards its R550 million ($34.375 million) target and says it will invest in South African technology companies that already have paying customers.
Mamor’s fund points to a bigger problem in South Africa’s startup market, where companies can have paying customers and a working business yet still struggle to find investors willing to fund their next stage of growth.
Mamokete Ramathe, founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of Mamor Capital, revealed that the firm spent more than three years raising the fund and found that many traditional investors, including pension funds and banks, remain cautious about venture capital.
Some investors, she said, have mandates or risk limits that make it difficult to invest in early-stage companies. Others still associate venture capital with backing businesses that have not yet proved that their products work.
“The fundraising journey reinforced that institutional appetite for venture capital in South Africa is still developing,” Ramathe told TechCabal in an interview on Monday.
Mamor is trying to reduce some of that risk by investing in companies that have already shown that customers will pay for their products or services. Ramathe said the firm does not require companies to be profitable before investing. Instead, it looks at whether they have paying customers, can retain them, have a market they can grow into, and have a realistic path to becoming profitable.
Southern Africa’s VC market recorded R13.35 billion ($834.4 million) in active investments across 1,325 deals in 2024, but limited exits and follow-on funding remain barriers. That puts Mamor in a market where capital is growing, while some founders still struggle to secure the next round.
She explained that a company may have moved beyond an idea and built a business, but still be too small or risky for a bank loan. At the same time, the market still has gaps in follow-on funding, with limited exits and funding for later-stage companies remaining a challenge
“There is a significant funding gap for early-stage, post-revenue businesses in South Africa,” Ramathe said.
Fuzlin Levy-Hassen, Mamor’s co-founder and chief financial officer (CFO), said the fund will focus on businesses with evidence of genuine demand rather than simply promising future growth.
“We are looking for businesses that have moved beyond proving an idea and can show real commercial demand,” Levy-Hassen said.
The fund will focus on areas including financial access, digital infrastructure and technology that Mamor believes can expand economic participation by helping more people and businesses access financial services and markets.
The PIC’s investment is significant because institutional investors have traditionally been cautious about putting money into venture capital, where returns can take years, and some investments can fail.
Leon Smit, the PIC’s acting chief investment officer, said the backing gives the organisation exposure to South Africa’s growing venture capital market while supporting transformation.
“Mamor Capital brings together an experienced investment team, a clear strategy, and a strong transformation proposition,” Smit said.
The PIC also believes institutional investors can play a bigger role in providing the long-term capital needed to develop South Africa’s venture capital market. There are signs that interest is growing. Ramathe said some institutions that are not yet investing are researching venture capital and looking at ways to participate in parts of the market where the risks are lower.
Ketso Gordhan, CEO of the South African Small and Medium Enterprise Fund, which invested through its High Impact Seed Fund of Funds, an early-stage venture capital investment vehicle, said increasing the number of local fund managers able to back technology businesses is important.
“Our investment is intended to strengthen the pool of local fund managers with the capability to identify and support promising technology businesses,” noted Gordhan.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks.
