articles.title: Google Maps is being criticized for renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America at the White House's request, but Google says it's just sticking to its existing policies
articles.text:
'Beyond ridiculous': if you're seeing Lake Ontario renamed as Lake America on Google Maps, here's why
A significant name change
- Lake Ontario is now Lake America in the US via an executive order
- Google Maps has updated its maps to reflect the change
- Viewing the map from outside the US still shows the original name
Some 18 months on from the controversial renaming of the Gulf of Mexico, another edit has been made to Google Maps at the behest of US President Donald Trump: Lake Ontario, spread across the US-Canadian border, is now Lake America.
Or rather, it is if you're viewing Google Maps from inside the US (via Gizmodo) — the rest of the world will still see the Great Lake labeled as it has been since at least the 17th century. The name Ontario most likely comes from the Iroquoian word Kaniatarí:io or Oniatarí:io meaning "lake of shining waters" or "beautiful lake", as per Wikipedia.
The name change is the result of an executive order from the White House, as President Trump bickers with Canada over trade tariffs. In response, Canadian authorities have installed a large new sign at the lake (via the BBC), reading 'Lake Ontario. Now and Always'.
Reactions on Reddit are calling the switch "beyond ridiculous" and "braindead", though some commenters are pointing out that Google is obliged to follow the lead of the US Board on Geographic Names (part of the United States Geological Survey).
Google responds
For its part, Google has also chimed in to say that it has to follow "official government sources" when it comes to place names, saying that "these updates follow our long-standing policy for bodies of water with names that vary from country to country, and are starting to roll out now".
"People using Maps in the US will see 'Lake America', those in Canada will continue to see 'Lake Ontario', and those outside of the US and Canada will see both names," according to the official blog post from Google Maps on the matter.
However, not everyone is towing the line on this: New York State Governor Kathy Hochul took to social media to declare that "New York won't be calling it [Lake America]", so there are going to be some pockets of resistance regarding the change.

articles.title: Activision posts video showing Call of Duty cheat seller getting served at his home
articles.text:
Winners & losers: Activision doesn't mess around when it comes to fighting Call of Duty cheaters. To show it means business, the company has just posted a video of cease-and-desist papers being served to infamous CoD (and other titles) cheat seller Elocarry.
In the one-minute video, posted to the official Call of Duty account, a legal representative films himself arriving at Elocarry's house in Ohio with the cease-and-desist paperwork.
The whole interaction is very quick, and Elocarry appears to take the news well, though he might lose his calm demeanor once he speaks to Activision's attorneys.
 – Call of Duty (@CallofDuty) August 28, 2026
Elocarry's website lists cheats for games including Rust, ARC Raiders, Marvel Rivals, and Apex Legends, offering the likes of aimbots and ESP (extrasensory perception). He'd reportedly been selling a cheat pack for Black Ops 7 and Warzone, advertised as being safe from detection by the Ricochet anti-cheat system. He'd offered three-month subscriptions priced up to $108.
Activision posted a follow-up message on X that included a screenshot from Elocarry's official Discord channel. It confirmed that sales and availability of Call of Duty products (cheats) had been temporarily paused while the matter was "reviewed internally."
 – Call of Duty (@CallofDuty) August 28, 2026
The gaming giant said it has disrupted more than 375 cheat reseller operations, served more than 80 cease-and-desist demands, and shut down more than 30 vendors. The company added that it's prepared to take cheat developers and sellers to court.
This is far from Activision's first fight against Call of Duty cheaters. In 2020, a legal threat from the company pushed CxCheats to stop developing and selling Call of Duty hacks. The following year, Activision banned 60,000 Warzone accounts in one sweep, bringing the total number of permanent bans at the time to more than 300,000.
Later in 2021, Activision introduced Ricochet and warned that persistent offenders could be permanently banned from every past, current, and future game in the franchise. The anti-cheat system has since used some unusual punishments against suspected hackers, including making legitimate players invisible to suspected cheaters, removing cheaters' weapons, and deploying fake player clones that only flagged accounts can see.
Activision has also shown that its courtroom warnings aren't just empty threats. In 2024, a California judge awarded the publisher $14.5 million in damages from EngineOwning, which sold Call of Duty cheats. The company was also awarded almost $293,000 in attorneys' fees, while EngineOwning was ordered to hand over its website.
All of which means Elocarry might want to take those papers seriously. Pausing his sales could be only the first step if Activision decides to make him its next courtroom example.

articles.title: NASA just used satellites and debris to navigate without GPS
articles.text:
NASA just used satellites and debris to navigate without GPS
- Date:
- August 26, 2026
- Source:
- NASA
- Summary:
- NASA has successfully tested a system that allows satellites to navigate without GPS by using other spacecraft and debris as landmarks in orbit. In just three days, FALCON also improved the known orbits of more than 200 space objects completely autonomously.
- Share:
NASA's Starling mission has reached another milestone in autonomous spaceflight by demonstrating a system that can determine a satellite's orbital position using other objects in space as reference points rather than depending on an external navigation network.
The technology, called FALCON (Fast Autonomous Lost-in-space Catalog-based Optical Navigation), is designed to help spacecraft operate with greater independence. Such capabilities could become increasingly important as NASA pursues missions farther from Earth, including lunar satellite swarms, distributed science missions, and future human exploration.
Navigating Space Without GPS
Satellites near Earth commonly rely on GPS for navigation, but those signals may be weak, unreliable, or unavailable around the Moon and in deep space. FALCON offers an alternative by allowing spacecraft to determine where they are using what they can observe around them.
The FALCON payload is a joint flight experiment developed by NASA and EraDrive, a startup that emerged from Stanford University. The system combines EraDrive's Era-Core flight software and embedded algorithms with Starling's cameras and an onboard catalog of known satellites. Together, these tools enable GPS-independent navigation while also helping the spacecraft track activity and objects in its surroundings.
"FALCON is yet another success for the Starling demonstration mission. The results from FALCON can have far-reaching implications for on-orbit space-traffic monitoring, collision avoidance, and alternative navigation," said Roger Hunter, program manager for NASA's Small Spacecraft and Distributed Systems program at NASA's Ames Research Center in California's Silicon Valley. "The number of 'firsts' from Starling just keeps growing."
Using Satellites and Debris as Reference Points
The FALCON demonstration evaluated two related capabilities using Starling's onboard star tracker cameras. These cameras are standard spacecraft instruments that detect bright objects in space and help determine a spacecraft's orientation and position.
During position, navigation, and timing experiments, FALCON identified objects seen by Starling's cameras, including other spacecraft and orbital debris, and compared them with a publicly available catalog of known space objects maintained by the U.S. Department of War. Once the observed objects were identified and verified, FALCON used them as reference points to calculate Starling's orbit.
A separate set of experiments tested whether the spacecraft could improve orbital estimates for the objects it observed. Mission controllers loaded a catalog containing approximately 20,000 space objects and their predicted orbits onto Starling.
FALCON then compared the catalog information with observations gathered by Starling's cameras. Using those measurements, it calculated Starling's position while also refining the estimated locations of other objects in space. The resulting estimates were even more precise than the existing catalog data.
Over a period of three days, FALCON improved the known orbits of more than 200 objects without any intervention from operators on the ground.
A First for Autonomous Optical Navigation
FALCON's ability to determine its own orbit represents a first for a spacecraft navigating with optical cameras based on its position relative to other objects in space. In separate catalog updating tests, Starling also generated better onboard predictions of object positions than those supplied by ground stations.
These abilities could be especially valuable for future networks of satellites operating without GPS. Coordinated satellite systems may play an important role in supporting human activities on the surfaces of the Moon or Mars.
Precise spacecraft positioning is also essential for distributed science missions, where measurements collected from several locations in space must be accurately aligned. For space traffic management, autonomous navigation and onboard catalog updates could reduce dependence on ground-based tracking networks while improving collision avoidance.
From University Research to Commercial Technology
The FALCON experiment also demonstrates NASA's role in helping university research develop into commercial technology. The work began as a University SmallSat Technology Partnerships project before developing into EraDrive, which is now commercializing its Era-Core software and related hardware for wider use.
Starling gave the technology an opportunity to be tested under real conditions in orbit, demonstrating how advanced flight software can allow satellites to function as increasingly autonomous navigators.
Later this year, Starling, which launched in 2023, will expand the FALCON experiment using Era-Core. The mission's four spacecraft will share tracking information with one another and use those combined observations to refine their positions collectively.
NASA's Ames Research Center in California's Silicon Valley leads the Starling mission. NASA's Small Spacecraft and Distributed Systems program, based at Ames and within the Research and Technology Mission Directorate, funds and manages the Starling mission.

articles.title: Tim Cook dice adiós como CEO de Apple: "Este lugar es la prueba de que la cultura triunfa sobre todo"
articles.text:
El cambio de conducción de Apple está a pocas horas de hacerse realidad. Tim Cook finaliza hoy su mandato como CEO, con John Ternus como el designado para tomar las riendas de la compañía a partir de mañana, 1 de septiembre. Si bien el consejero delegado saliente no va a abandonar la empresa, puesto que asumirá el rol de presidente ejecutivo, sí ha aprovechado para cerrar su ciclo como conductor en el día a día con un mensaje especial destinado a sus empleados.
El portal 9to5Mac ha obtenido una copia del memo que Tim Cook envió hoy a los trabajadores de Apple. En el mismo, el ejecutivo agradeció al personal por todo el trabajo que realizaron en estos años, al que consideró fundamental para su éxito como CEO. Asimismo, valoró la misión de la compañía, a la que catalogó como "extraordinaria", y se mostró muy optimista por el futuro bajo el mando de Ternus.
Tim Cook destacó a Apple como un lugar que demostró que "la cultura triunfa sobre todo" y explicó que, si bien va a extrañar el cargo como CEO, está "completamente tranquilo" con la decisión de dejarlo. Y como no podía ser de otra manera, aprovechó el mensaje para recordar el legado de Steve Jobs.
A continuación puedes leer el mensaje completo de Tim Cook en su despedida como CEO de Apple, traducido al español:
"Equipo,
Hoy es mi último día como CEO de Apple. Siempre supe que este momento llegaría, y aún me cuesta creer que haya llegado y que esté escribiendo estas palabras. Amo esta compañía y al equipo que la conforma, y no podía dejar pasar este día sin escribirles para expresarles mi gratitud por las muestras de cariño que me han brindado, por su dedicación diaria y, sobre todo, por el privilegio de toda una vida de haber sido su líder.
La verdad es que, sea lo que sea que se pueda decir sobre mi éxito, sé que todo se debe a ustedes. Han sacado lo mejor de mí. En toda mi vida, nunca antes había visto ni trabajado con un equipo tan extraordinario, y cada día veo más ejemplos de ello.
Hay algo verdaderamente especial en Apple. Me siento muy orgulloso de algo que un informe anual jamás podría reflejar. Este lugar es la prueba de que la cultura triunfa sobre todo. Compartimos la convicción de que lo que construimos importa, y que tenemos la oportunidad y la responsabilidad de dejar el mundo mejor de como lo encontramos. Ese propósito es parte de lo que hace que este lugar sea extraordinario. Apple ayuda a cultivarlo, pero creo que ya existía en cada uno de ustedes mucho antes de que llegaran aquí. Es lo que los trajo a esta empresa y lo que sigue impulsando el trabajo que realizan cada día. Juntos, hemos creado algo mucho más grande de lo que cualquiera de nosotros podría haber imaginado o logrado individualmente. Y ese es el secreto de nuestro éxito. Sacamos lo mejor de cada uno. Nos apoyamos mutuamente. Hemos hecho posible dejar nuestra ‘huella en el universo’, como Steve la describió una vez, gracias a quienes somos, a lo que creemos, a nuestros valores y a nuestra visión del mundo. Qué afortunados somos. Qué afortunado soy yo.
Como saben, no me voy de Apple. Pero sí me retiro de un puesto que he amado profundamente. Extrañaré este trabajo de maneras que apenas puedo imaginar, aunque estoy completamente tranquilo con mi decisión. Extrañaré liderarlos y acompañarlos en cada paso, aunque me reconforta enormemente ceder el mando a alguien tan brillante, maravilloso y capaz como John. Pocas personas comprenden lo que se necesita para crear productos que cambien el mundo como lo hace John, y me entusiasma enormemente su liderazgo.
Espero que sepan cuánto los aprecio y el honor que ha sido ser su CEO. Sobre todo, espero que sigan sintiéndose orgullosos de formar parte de este extraordinario lugar que llamamos Apple y que siempre den lo mejor de ustedes. Cuando nos entregamos por completo a este trabajo, con respeto mutuo y hacia las personas a las que servimos, no hay límites para el profundo impacto que podemos lograr.
Espero verlos en mi nuevo puesto en el Apple Park y en todo el mundo.
Con todo mi ser y con todo lo que tengo, siempre...
Atentamente,
Tim"
Tim Cook se despide como CEO de Apple tras 15 años
De esta manera, el periplo de Tim Cook como CEO de Apple llega a su fin tras 15 años. Recordemos que el ejecutivo asumió el rol formalmente el 24 de agosto de 2011, tras la renuncia de Steve Jobs. Previo a ello, había cubierto parcialmente el cargo durante las ausencias de Jobs por los problemas de salud derivados de un cáncer pancreático.
Antes de convertirse en el conductor de Apple, Tim Cook tuvo un rol crucial como jefe de operaciones. Su trabajo fue fundamental para establecer las cadenas de suministros y las líneas de producción en China. Ya como CEO, transformó a la firma de Cupertino en una de las empresas más valiosas del mundo.
Cuando Tim Cook tomó las riendas de Apple, su valoración de mercado rondaba los 356.000 millones de dólares. Hoy, la empresa vale 4,58 billones de dólares y se encuentra solamente detrás de NVIDIA entre las de mayor marketcap del mundo.
Impulsada por el iPhone como producto estrella, el ciclo de Tim Cook se cierra con otros puntos altos muy interesantes. El Apple Watch y los AirPods fueron apuestas muy exitosas, mientras que la transición a Apple Silicon fue el otro gran golpe de su gestión. Nada mal para un ejecutivo con un perfil que no estaba orientado a producto.
Por supuesto que el mandato de Tim Cook no ha quedado libre de pasos en falso. El Apple Vision Pro es el más reciente, pero no hay que olvidarse del desastroso debut de Apple Maps en 2012. En años más recientes, el fiasco de la nueva Siri con Apple Intelligence fue un tropiezo bastante duro y que recién ahora se está empezando a resolver gracias a la intervención de Google. El Apple Car también podría estar en este registro, aunque la existencia del proyecto nunca se reconoció públicamente.
Si bien Tim Cook ha sido un ejecutivo bien conceptuado públicamente, algunas decisiones recientes impactaron sobre su imagen. Sus esfuerzos por congraciarse con Donald Trump para evitar un impacto mayúsculo de sus aranceles sobre los productos de Apple han recibido duras críticas. No solo por aportar dinero a su comité de investidura o por entregarle un regalo bañado en oro, sino especialmente por aparecer en el estreno del documental Melania y fotografiarse con el director Brett Ratner, acusado de acoso y agresión sexual.
Con John Ternus asumiendo el rol de CEO desde mañana, 1 de septiembre, Apple inicia una nueva era. La primera prueba para el nuevo jefe llegará muy pronto. El 9 de septiembre se lanzarán los iPhone 18 Pro y el iPhone Ultra, y hay más productos al caer antes de que finalice 2026.
Más allá de su carta de despedida, Tim Cook también ha publicado un mensaje en redes sociales. "Enviando mucho amor a la comunidad de Apple en mi último día como CEO. Mi título cambia mañana, pero el amor que tengo por la comunidad de Apple nunca lo hará. Gracias por ser una fuente constante de inspiración. Mi gratitud es infinita, ¡y estoy emocionado por el próximo capítulo!", compartió en X.

articles.title: Kalshi bans George Santos for life over State of the Union bets | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Kalshi has banned former Republican Rep. George Santos from its platform for life, the first time the prediction market company has taken such an action.
Kalshi also penalized and suspended several political candidates accused of betting on their own races, including Ben Midgley, who ran and lost in the Republican primary for Maine’s gubernatorial race; Laurie Buckhout, a Republican congressional nominee; and former California gubernatorial candidate Stephen Cloobeck.
The Santos ban follows allegations that he bet on whether he would attend President Trump’s State of the Union address, allegedly making $17,839 on the wager. Kalshi’s compliance department said it “established reasonable cause” to believe that Santos had placed bets connected to his own attendance at the event. Kalshi also fined Santos $71,356 over the activity.
“As a person capable of influencing the outcome of the underlying event, Santos was prohibited from trading in this market,” Kalshi wrote, accusing him of making public statements about his attendance to impact the odds.
Santos responded on X: “Hey @Kalshi thanks for the lifetime ban from your gambling platform. Let’s see how much longer you guys are around for.”
The move follows a separate CFTC settlement two months earlier over the same conduct, in which Santos agreed to pay an additional $35,000.
The WSJ was the first to report on the ban.

articles.title: John Ternus is now the CEO of Apple
articles.text:
For the first time since 2011, one of the world’s most valuable companies has a new leader, as today marks John Ternus’ first day as Apple’s CEO. He’s replacing Tim Cook, who will continue on as the executive chairman on Apple’s board and departed with a letter to employees that remarked, “This place is proof that culture triumphs over everything. We share a belief that what we build matters, and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it.”
John Ternus is now the CEO of Apple
 From Jobs to Cook to Ternus.
 From Jobs to Cook to Ternus.
Ternus is taking over a company dealing with the rise of AI, shortages of RAM and other components due to that growth in AI, and a political and economic situation that is only getting more complicated as time passes. He will also do it without many of the executives who worked with Cook and Steve Jobs, like Phil Schiller, who Bloomberg reported will step down from his role leading the App Store.
Here’s a look at Apple’s senior leadership team as it stands today:
With Ternus in charge, Tim Cook has been moved to Executive Chair and Phil Schiller continues as an Apple Fellow, despite handing off his day-to-day tasks of heading up the Apple Store and Apple events. We can also see that Katherine Adams’ position of SVP of government affairs has been fully vacated, with some of that responsibility being handed to Jennifer Newstead and Tim Cook, who’s now Trump’s full-time handler. Apple’s former CFO Luca Maestri is no longer listed on the leadership team after he transitioned to the roll of VP of corporate services in 2024.
The first Apple hardware event of the Ternus era is just around the corner on September 9th, where we expect to see new iPhones including a foldable “Ultra.” It will give us an early glimpse of what to expect, and the new public faces of the company going forward.

articles.title: Ultradünne Solarfolie für Luft- und Raumfahrt
articles.text:
Effizient wie ein Solarmodul: Marktstart für ultradünne Solarfolie von Solarwindow
Flexible Solarfolien sind nichts Neues. Aufgebracht auf E-Autos sollen sie deren Reichweite verlängern. Zudem sollen sie in transparenter Ausführung auf Fensterscheiben geklebt werden können und so zusätzliche Energie für private Haushalte liefern.
Solarwindow startet Verkauf von Solarfolie
Das US-Unternehmen Solarwindow Technologies hat jetzt den Verkaufsstart einer Solarfolie angekündigt, die nicht nur ultradünn und flexibel ist, sondern auch mit einem hohen Wirkungsgrad punkten kann. Einem Bericht von pv-magazine.com zufolge soll die Zelleffizienz der nur 0,85 Millimeter dicken Solarfolie 24,4 Prozent erreichen und sich damit auf dem Niveau moderner Solarmodule bewegen.
Die selbstklebende Folie eignet sich vor allem für flache und gebogene Oberflächen sowie für Anwendungen, bei denen es auf jedes Gramm ankommt und wo herkömmliche Module nicht geeignet sind. Mit Electrolux zielt Solarwindow eigenen Angaben zufolge auf die Bereiche Transportwesen, Luft- und Raumfahrt, Landwirtschaft, Infrastruktur sowie Gebäudearchitektur ab.
Electroflex: Marktstart in den USA
Zunächst liefert Solarwindow die Folie nur an industrielle Hersteller in den USA aus. In den kommenden Quartalen sollen weitere Märkte in Nordamerika und Asien dazukommen. Ob irgendwann auch private Haushalte oder kleinere Firmen die Solarfolie kaufen können, ist nicht bekannt.
Bisher hatte sich Solarwindow auf die Entwicklung einer transparenten, flüssigen Beschichtung für Glas- und Kunststoffoberflächen konzentriert. Liquidelectricity soll auch in Innenräumen und bei schattigen Verhältnissen Strom erzeugen können.
Strategiewechsel euphorisiert die Börse
Mit Electroflex erweitert Solarwindow sein Portfolio jetzt um physische, flexible Solarprodukte. Das Ganze ist Teil eines Mitte August 2026 kommunizierten Strategiewechsels hin zu einer breiter aufgestellten Energieplattform. Neben Electroflex und Liquidelectricity sollen weitere neue Produkte kommen, wie Solarwindow-CEO Amit Singh ankündigte.
An der Börse hatte das für Euphorie gesorgt, wie es bei boerse-express.com heißt. Innerhalb der vergangenen zwei Wochen hatte sich der Kurs der Aktie des Unternehmens mehr als versiebenfacht. Ob die Hochstimmung anhält, hängt laut Beobachter:innen aber davon ab, ob die angekündigten detaillierten Produktinformationen sowie die Updates zur Produktzertifizierung halten, was sie versprechen.

articles.title: Chinese Fire Ant hackers turn Cisco routers into spying platforms
articles.text:
The researchers discovered Fire Ant's new tactic after finding an active GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) tunnel interface on a Cisco IOS XR router that could not be explained by a running configuration or commit history.
According to incident response company Sygnia, the threat actor switched from targeting VMware hypervisors to compromising Cisco routers, TACACS authentication servers, and Linux management hosts.
The researchers discovered Fire Ant's new tactic after finding on a Cisco IOS XR router an active GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) tunnel interface that could not be explained by a running configuration or commit history.
Further analysis revealed that Fire Ant had deployed custom malware on the devices, enabling persistence through a fake system service that ran the implant only during alternating hours.
The malware selectively suppressed syslog messages to hide tunnel-related information from legitimate administrators, established outbound Telnet connections to Fire Ant infrastructure, and supported interactive shell access with no logging.
The attackers also used their administrative access to capture traffic from multiple routers and upload the resulting PCAP files to external FTP servers.
These captures could expose internal topology, administrative connections, authentication flows, routing relationships, and traffic exchanged with connected networks.
“This behavior shifts the router’s role from a transit device to a collection platform,” Sygnia explains.
“Once the actor controlled the router, the device became a vantage point for observing traffic moving through trusted network paths.”
The concealed GRE tunnel connected one compromised router to a legacy Linux server, which Fire Ant used as a staging and reconnaissance system.
From there, the attackers probed systems in connected high-value environments, including systems associated with critical infrastructure, over ports commonly used for SSH, web services, SMB/RPC, and RDP.
Sygnia believes that Fire Ant's operation aimed to compromise trusted infrastructure at an initial victim and use it as a covert bridge to explore access paths into connected high-value networks, a tactic which they dub “target behind the target.”
The researchers also discovered a previously undocumented backdoor called ‘BridgeAgent,’ which Fire Ant disguised as a legitimate Zabbix monitoring agent.
The backdoor persists as a root-level systemd service and supports TLS reverse shells and the execution of additional payloads on the compromised host.
Sygnia says Fire Ant activity strongly overlaps with UNC3886, a Chinese espionage group previously documented by Google. However, the researchers say that there are differences in filenames, paths, and implementation details.
The researchers warned that Fire Ant systematically tampers with system logs and records, even changing file timestamps to obscure evidence that would benefit investigators, noting that logs retrieved from compromised infrastructure should be validated against other data.
Sygnia's report shares an extensive list of indicators of compromise (IoCs), along with hunting and YARA rules to detect Fire Ant activity.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Tiny robots powered by light can hunt down and collect bacteria
articles.text:
Tiny robots powered by light can hunt down and collect bacteria
Light-powered nanorobots can now hunt down, collect, and relocate bacteria like futuristic microscopic cleaning crews.
- Date:
- August 18, 2026
- Source:
- University of Würzburg
- Summary:
- Researchers have built microscopic, light-driven robots that can rapidly navigate through liquid, collect bacteria, and deposit them in chosen locations. These tiny “cleaners” could open new possibilities for manipulating cells and microbes with remarkable precision.
- Share:
Robots small enough to operate in the microbial world could give scientists a new way to directly handle objects that are impossible to manipulate by hand. These tiny machines are around 50 times smaller than the diameter of a human hair, bringing researchers closer to the long-pursued goal of interacting directly with the microscopic world.
That capability could be especially useful for biological materials in water, including individual cells and bacteria. Precisely controlling and moving objects at this scale has been a persistent challenge. The newly developed nanorobots show that it is already possible to collect bacteria, transport them, and release them at selected locations.
Light Powers and Steers the Tiny Robots
One of the biggest obstacles in developing machines this small is finding an effective way to propel and control them. At Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg (JMU), a research team led by Professor Bert Hecht has been developing a solution that uses the recoil produced by individual photons to move microscopic devices known as microdrones.
The devices contain as many as four plasmonic nanoantennas. These antennas absorb light with a particular color and helicity, then emit that light in a specific direction. Redirecting each photon creates a tiny recoil force, similar in principle to the recoil produced when a bullet is fired. Because the microdrones have so little mass, those extremely small forces can generate substantial acceleration and speed.
For the latest work, the researchers reduced the size of their light-powered robots even further, producing devices smaller than one micrometer. Simplifying the steering system was an important part of achieving that size while retaining propulsion based on photon recoil.
The new control method takes advantage of nanoscale antenna wires built into the robot. These wires naturally tend to align with the polarization direction of incoming light. By changing the light's polarization, the researchers can control which direction the nanorobot faces. At the same time, photon recoil continues to propel it forward, creating a steering system that works somewhat like the directional control used in larger vehicles.
Nanorobots Act as "Microscopic Cleaners"
"In essence, we have built a light-driven nanorobot that can track down and collect bacteria," says Jin Qin, lead experimental scientist of the study. "By simplifying the design, we reached a size at which these robots can operate directly in the microbial world - almost like microscopic cleaning devices."
The robots are also highly maneuverable. They can make extremely fast 90° turns, helping them scan broad areas of a sample in an organized and efficient way. They can also selectively capture, carry, and release substantial numbers of bacteria.
Under controlled laboratory conditions, this means the nanorobots can effectively "clean" microscopic environments. They gather bacteria from one area and deposit them at specifically chosen locations.
"This is a striking example of how light can be used not only to observe the microscopic world, but also to actively shape it," adds Bert Hecht. "The idea of tiny robotic cleaners may sound futuristic, but we are already demonstrating the physical principles that make it possible."
The robots remain fully maneuverable even while carrying larger groups of bacteria, although their speed decreases somewhat under the added load. That ability to keep functioning while transporting larger bacterial clusters points to possible future uses in microbiology, biomedical research, and precise manipulation of materials at the microscopic scale.

articles.title: Adiós a las estafas: One UI 9 llevará una de las mejores funciones de los Pixel a más Samsung Galaxy
articles.text:
Una de las mejores funciones de los Google Pixel para acabar con los llamados fraudulentos está cerca de llegar a más Samsung Galaxy. Nos referimos a la detección de estafas, que podría expandirse a un número mayor de modelos de la marca coreana de la mano de One UI 9.
Según reporta Android Authority, la beta de One UI 9 incluye referencias a la expansión de la detección de estafas que Google originalmente lanzó como una característica exclusiva de los Pixel. Dicha herramienta ya se encuentra disponible en los Samsung Galaxy S26 y en los plegables Galaxy Z Fold 8, Fold 8 Ultra y Flip 8, pero en cuestión de meses estaría dando el salto a modelos previos.
Puntualmente, la versión en desarrollo de One UI 9 revela que la detección de estafas se incorporaría a todos los teléfonos que conforman la línea Galaxy S25. De modo que la próxima gran actualización de software de Samsung introduciría esta herramienta tanto en en el modelo estándar como en las variantes Plus, Ultra y Edge.
Asimismo, la característica haría su estreno en los Galaxy Z Fold 7 y Flip 7, además del Galaxy Z Trifold, el plegable triple de la marca coreana. Por ahora no se ha mencionado si la detección de estafas llegará también al Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE, la versión más económica del plegable tipo concha.
La detección de estafas llegará a más Samsung Galaxy con One UI 9
El citado reporte indica que la detección de estafas también estaría disponible en los Galaxy S27 que se lanzarán a principios de próximo año. Esto no sorprendería, considerando que la característica ya forma parte de los S26 y que los próximos buques insignia de Samsung tendrán One UI 9 preinstalado.
La detección de estafas es una de las mejores funciones que Google introdujo en Android en los últimos años. La característica se encarga de monitorear las llamadas entrantes usando un modelo de inteligencia artificial que se ejecuta directamente en el smartphone. Si el contenido de la conversación comienza a tornarse sospechoso, la función envía alertas visuales y auditivas. Además, el móvil comienza a vibrar para que el usuario preste atención y finalice la llamada antes de que el engaño se concrete.
Vale mencionar que la detección de estafas se encuentra integrada en la aplicación Teléfono, pero también funciona con SMS a través de la app Mensajes. En el caso de One UI 9, si la expansión a más modelos realmente se concreta, se trata de una adición muy interesante. Lo que todavía no está claro es si Samsung planea llevar esta herramienta a todos los móviles compatibles con dicho software, o si lo mantendrá limitada a sus buques insignia.

articles.title: Harvard Law dropout raises $6M for Blue Voice to build a 'Harvey for police officers' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
David Lawrence was a Harvard Law student when an on-campus shooting involving a police officer sparked intense controversy over police conduct. Realizing that most policing errors occur when officers lack instant access to department rules, Lawrence dropped out to tackle the problem with AI. He teamed up with co-founders Amit Patankar, a Harvard MBA and former Google engineer, and Michael Gropman, a retired Boston police deputy chief, to launch Blue Voice — a Boston-based AI startup that provides real-time policy guidance to officers in the field.
Three years later, Blue Voice is coming out of stealth with $6 million in funding led by SignalFire and Las Olas VC. Officers at 225 county agencies across 25 states now rely on the tool daily to ensure their actions follow department protocol — a platform Lawrence likens to Harvey, the AI tool widely used by lawyers, or OpenEvidence, which is a similar tool for doctors.
“When an officer makes a decision, they do so from memory or best guess, based on thousands of pages of law, policy, municipal ordinances, and state laws that they’ve internalized and keep in their head,” Lawrence told TechCrunch.
Before Blue Voice, an officer who couldn’t recall a specific protocol — like the exact seventh step required at a crime scene — had few good options: Flip through a 15,000-page manual, wake up a supervisor in the middle of the night, or search generic tools like Google or ChatGPT that lack police-specific training. The problem was that traditional methods took too much time, while consumer AI models delivered incorrect answers up to 30% of the time, Lawrence said.
Blue Voice says it solves this issue because it is trained on department-specific laws, local ordinances, protocols, and guidelines that general-purpose AI tools can’t access on the public internet. The platform also gives officers instant access to detailed school maps on their phones during active-shooter emergencies.
Today, Blue Voice answers a question every minute. Lawrence says that officers feel confident relying on the tool because it always points them directly to original regulations rather than just generating an answer on its own the way ChatGPT would. Rather than dictating actions, the tool simply provides the laws, leaving the final decision to the officers, who combine it with their own field experience.
Over the last year, says Lawrence, Blue Voice grew its customer base elevenfold because police departments see concrete results, including reduced crime and fewer operational controversies.
Blue Voice recently helped prevent a kidnapping after a rookie officer spotted a man pressuring a young girl to enter his vehicle, according to Lawrence. Unsure whether he had legal grounds to intervene, the officer consulted Blue Voice on his phone. The app instantly confirmed that the situation met the legal criteria for “child enticement” — an offense covering attempts to lure a minor for the purpose of committing a crime against them — giving him the immediate authority to act.
In another instance, Blue Voice reminded a department chief that he couldn’t return an officer to active-duty following a shooting without first obtaining a third-party mental health evaluation.
The startup, which competes with PE-backed Lexipol, also recently developed functionality to help detectives solve cold cases.
At a time when police use of AI — such as Flock Safety’s license plate surveillance systems — draws growing criticism, Lawrence hopes Blue Voice proves that properly deployed AI can deliver public safety benefits without sacrificing civil rights.
Lawrence, who previously worked for Connecticut governor Ned Lamont, developed a deep passion for public service and says he has no regrets about leaving law school behind. “This is the best thing I could do with my career and the most impact I could potentially make,” he said.
Above, left to right: Michael Gropman, David Lawrence, and Amit Patankar.

articles.title: Apple processa OpenAI após perder centenas de funcionários; startup rebate
articles.text:
A OpenAI rejeitou as acusações da Apple de que ex-funcionários teriam levado segredos comerciais ao deixar a fabricante. Em documento apresentado à Justiça dos EUA, a empresa diz que a Apple não conseguiu provar que informações confidenciais foram roubadas.
O caso envolve a contratação de profissionais para a divisão de hardware da OpenAI e marca uma nova etapa no desgaste entre as duas empresas, que chegaram a manter uma parceria para ampliar o uso do ChatGPT nos produtos da Apple.
Apple acusa ex-funcionários
A Apple processou a OpenAI e os ex-funcionários Tang Tan e Chang Liu em julho. A fabricante afirma que os dois se apropriaram de informações relacionadas a design de hardware, fabricação e cadeia de suprimentos.
A OpenAI vê a ação de outra forma. Para a empresa, o processo tenta frear a expansão de uma possível concorrente e desencorajar funcionários da Apple a mudar de emprego. Cerca de 400 profissionais da fabricante foram contratados para a iniciativa de hardware da OpenAI, conforme documentos do processo.
“Esta disputa é uma confusão criada pela própria Apple, e ela está tentando culpar todo mundo”, afirmou a OpenAI.
A empresa também argumenta que a legislação da Califórnia permite que funcionários deixem uma companhia para trabalhar em outra, mesmo quando as duas competem entre si.
Arquivos viram ponto central
A Apple sustenta que Tan e Liu acessaram documentos internos depois de deixar a empresa. Para a fabricante, o acesso faria parte de uma estratégia da OpenAI para obter informações confidenciais.
A OpenAI rebateu a acusação citando os próprios procedimentos da Apple para desligamento de funcionários. Segundo a empresa, eles dificultariam a separação entre arquivos pessoais e corporativos.
Entre os pontos levantados estão:
- Funcionários podem usar contas pessoais do iCloud para acessar documentos de trabalho;
- A retirada imediata dos funcionários das instalações reduziria o tempo para devolver dispositivos;
- Arquivos internos poderiam não ser transferidos de volta à empresa antes da saída;
- A passagem de responsabilidades também poderia ser prejudicada.
Liu afirmou que acessou documentos depois de sair para ajudar antigos colegas a localizar arquivos e responder dúvidas sobre seu trabalho anterior. Ele disse que funcionários da Apple continuaram procurando sua ajuda.
Ex-funcionários contestam versão
Tan, que passou 24 anos na Apple, afirmou ter devolvido protótipos antes de deixar a companhia. Disse ainda que só manteve materiais não confidenciais, incluindo uma lista de verificação usada no desligamento de funcionários.
Leia mais:
- Apple diz ter encontrado “evidências chocantes” contra OpenAI em MacBook
- ChatGPT Ads chega a US$ 1 bilhão em receita em menos de 200 dias
- OpenAI corta acesso de empresa comprada por SpaceX e alfineta Musk
“Eles podem deixar uma empresa como a Apple, que teve dificuldades para adotar a IA, e ir para uma startup empolgante que desenvolve produtos inovadores”, escreveu a OpenAI.
A relação entre as duas companhias mudou rapidamente. Há cerca de dois anos, Apple e OpenAI haviam firmado uma parceria para ampliar o alcance do ChatGPT e dar à fabricante uma posição mais forte no mercado de inteligência artificial.
Agora, com a OpenAI avançando em hardware e disputando profissionais da Apple, a parceria deu lugar a uma batalha judicial que coloca segredos comerciais, contratações e procedimentos internos no centro da discussão.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.
Bruno Capozzi é jornalista, mestre em Ciências Sociais e editor executivo do OD.

articles.title: "Comment évoluent mes actions Nvidia ?" : Revolut déploie AIR, un assistant IA financier, pour ses clients français
articles.text:
Plusieurs mois après un premier déploiement au Royaume-Uni, Revolut AIR est dès aujourd’hui disponible pour les clients basés en France et dans toute l’Europe, nous informe la banque en ligne aux 80 millions de clients par communiqué de presse. L’assistant IA financier de Revolut est disponible directement sur l’application. Pour y accéder, il faut se rendre sur sa page Profil, puis dans Discussions, puis AIR, ou simplement faire glisser son doigt vers le bas depuis le centre de l’écran d’accueil de l’application
    À lire aussi : 
    Avis Revolut : en 2026, est-ce la meilleure banque en ligne ?
« Un nouveau niveau d’intelligence financière »
AIR (pour « AI by Revolut ») est l’assistant conversationnel intégré à l’application Revolut. Pour la banque, il sert d’abord à faciliter la navigation sur une application de plus en plus chargée. Ces dernières années, Revolut a en effet multiplié les nouveautés et propose aujourd’hui quasiment autant de services qu’une banque traditionnelle. Surtout, AIR propose plusieurs fonctionnalités autour de la gestion financière.
Nous pensons que l’époque où il fallait naviguer entre une multitude d’onglets et de menus est révolue. Avec AIR, nous proposons un nouveau niveau d’intelligence financière à la fois puissant et intuitif. Qu’il s’agisse de maîtriser ses dépenses quotidiennes ou de planifier des voyages en toute simplicité et sans stress, AIR agit comme un copilote qui facilite la vie au quotidien, rendant la gestion financière aussi simple et naturelle que l’envoi d’un SMS.
Julia Ponomareva, associée et directrice générale des produits CX et IA chez Revolut
Parmi les fonctionnalités mises en avant, Revolut évoque d’abord une gestion plus intelligente de ses dépenses : connaître immédiatement ses dépenses dans telle ou telle catégorie sur le mois, bloquer une carte perdue ou gérer ses abonnements. AIR peut également être utilisé dans le volet investissements pour obtenir un briefing sur un cours en particulier ou un bilan des performances de son portefeuille.
Revolut met enfin en avant une planification plus intelligente de ses voyages avec notamment un usage optimisé de ses RevPoints. On peut également imaginer utiliser AIR pour une simulation de demande de crédit ou une conversion rapide entre devises.
Pour concevoir le modèle IA pour AIR, Revolut explique à Frandroid s’être appuyé sur la combinaison de modèles propriétaires et de modèles open source tandis que l’ensemble de l’architecture IA est conçue et développée en interne. Revolut affirme également imposer à tous ses fournisseurs tiers de LLM des engagements stricts en matière de non-conservation des données.
Bien que le lancement soit officialisé, AIR est actuellement en cours de déploiement à travers toute l’Europe et sera progressivement disponible dans les prochains jours. Il est donc possible que vous n’y ayez pas encore accès.

articles.title: Spiro names Auroasish Choudhuri as West and Central Africa MD
articles.text:
Spiro, one of Africa’s largest electric motorcycle and battery-swapping companies, has appointed Auroasish Choudhuri as its Managing Director for West and Central Africa.
Choudhuri, who has more than two decades of experience leading automotive businesses across Africa, Asia and the Americas, will oversee Spiro’s mobility business in the two regions and report to Kaushik Burman, its chief executive officer of Mobility, the company said in a Monday statement.
The hiring is the latest wave of appointments at Spiro as the company reshapes its leadership following a $270 million fundraising haul in June. The company appointed former Indofast Energy CEO Anant Badjatya as Group CEO and moved former CEO Burman to lead its mobility services business, separating its rider-facing operations from its ambitions in battery swapping, energy infrastructure, logistics and vehicle manufacturing.
“Auroasish brings extensive experience in growing and transforming automotive businesses across some of the world’s most dynamic markets,” said Anant Badjatya, chief executive officer of Spiro. “His deep understanding of the sector, combined with his track record in market expansion and operational leadership, will be a strong asset as we continue to scale Spiro across Africa.”
Choudhuri joins Spiro from DAG Industries, an automotive and industrial company, where he has served as CEO, overseeing its operations in Nigeria and Benin. Before that, he spent more than a decade at Indian two-wheeler manufacturer TVS Motor Company, serving as Regional Business Head for Asia and, later, Latin America.
Earlier in his career, he led international sales and business development at Escorts Limited across the US, Latin America, West Asia, and Sri Lanka. His experience spans sales, business development, and market expansion.
At Spiro, that experience will be deployed alongside the company’s push to expand its mobility business and launch in new markets.
“Africa is entering an exciting new phase in the transformation of mobility,” Choudhuri said. “I am excited to join Spiro and bring together my automotive expertise and experience of West African markets to support the company’s next phase of growth and expand access to affordable, sustainable mobility across the continent.”
The appointment comes as Spiro expands its ambitions beyond selling electric motorcycles. The company has been building an integrated electric mobility ecosystem around its motorcycles through the battery-swapping infrastructure that allows riders to replace depleted batteries with charged ones.
Spiro assembles vehicles in Kenya, Rwanda and Uganda and operates a battery recycling facility in Nigeria. It also operates in Benin, Togo, and Cameroon and has previously identified Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of Congo as markets for expansion.
Spiro has also moved to strengthen control over its supply chain by acquiring UK-based two-wheeler engineering specialist Coexlion in May as it moves into vehicle development and manufacturing. The task for the company’s growing leadership team is to build the local infrastructure and supply chains needed to make its battery-swapping model work at scale. With Choudhuri leading West and Central Africa, the company is adding someone whose career has centred on expanding automotive businesses across markets.

articles.title: Workload-Driven HBF Substrate For Capacity-Scalable LLM Inference (Huawei, ETH Zurich, HUST)
articles.text:
Researchers at Huawei, ETH Zürich, and HUST published a technical paper titled “FLINT: Efficiently Leveraging High Bandwidth Flash for Capacity-Scalable LLM Inference Acceleration.”
Abstract:
“LLM inference is increasingly constrained by accelerator memory capacity rather than compute throughput. This constraint is especially acute in single-accelerator and small-node inference systems, where limited on-package memory capacity restricts the size of deployable models. HBF is an emerging 3D-stacked NAND flash technology that provides multi-terabyte near-accelerator capacity, making it a promising capacity tier for storing LLM weights. However, existing HBF-based proposals face three adoption challenges: they (1) rely on coarse-grained static prefetching for LLM weights aiming to hide the microsecond-level read latency of the NAND flash device while maximizing HBF’s read throughput, (2) expose NAND flash management tasks (e.g., refresh operations) to the accelerator-visible critical inference path, and (3) miss optimization opportunities to specialize and optimize the flash-management mechanisms to the workload behavior.
Our goal is to design an efficient HBF substrate that integrates HBF as a memory-capacity tier alongside HBM while addressing these three challenges. To this end, we propose FLINT, a workload-driven HBF substrate for capacity-scalable LLM inference. FLINT introduces three mechanisms: (1) a hardware burst-buffer controller that dynamically coalesces and pipelines HBF reads aiming to utilize existing NAND flash buffers while sustaining high HBF bandwidth, (2) a phantom-plane refresh mechanism, which removes refresh from the critical inference path by moving refresh-related NAND flash operations outside the read foreground back via low-cost resource duplication, and (3) a read-only FTL, which replaces SSD-class support for arbitrary writes with a compact table that translates logical weight bursts to physical HBF locations.”
Find the technical paper here. August 2026.
Oliveira, Geraldo F., Arash Tavakkol, Xiangyu Zhu, Ahmet Caner Yüzügüler, Vamanan Arulchelvan, Lukas Cavigelli, Renzo Andri et al. “FLINT: Efficiently Leveraging High Bandwidth Flash for Capacity-Scalable LLM Inference Acceleration.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.25062 (2026).

articles.title: Nigeria wants crypto firms to lock up 80% of customer assets offline
articles.text:
This is Follow the Money, our weekly series that unpacks the earnings, business, and scaling strategies of African fintechs, financial institutions, companies, and governments. A new edition drops every Monday.
When you buy cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin or Ether on a local exchange, you are often trusting the platform with one simple task: to keep your funds safe.
But what happens if the exchange is hacked, freezes withdrawals or suddenly shuts down?
Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) wants cryptocurrency companies to have better answers.
Under proposed rules released on August 20, crypto exchanges and other digital asset firms would have to separate customer funds from their own, strengthen how they safeguard cryptocurrencies, and report major losses, cyber incidents, and other material operational failures to the regulator.
The framework, which is open for public comment, brings a rule already familiar in the traditional banking sector to the digital asset industry: when something goes wrong, the regulator expects to know about it quickly. Like banks, crypto firms would have to notify their regulator of certain incident reporting within 24 hours with further updates where necessary; the SEC’s proposal also requires digital asset firms to submit a detailed incident report within 48 hours.
The SEC is also proposing higher financial requirements for digital asset businesses. Digital Asset Exchanges and Digital Asset Custodians (DACs) would each need minimum paid-up capital of ₦2 billion ($1.5 million) while Digital Asset Platform Operators (DAPOs), Digital Asset Offering Platforms (DAOPs), and Real-World Asset Tokenisation Platforms (RATOPs) would require ₦500 million ($371,600). Virtual Asset Service Providers would require ₦200 million ($149,000).
The proposal also requires a current fidelity insurance bond covering at least 25% of the applicable minimum paid-up capital.
The rules are aimed at strengthening investor protection and reducing the risk that customers lose access to their assets when a digital asset company fails. The stakes are high in a market where the collapse or failure of a platform can leave customers unable to access their money, with little clarity on when—or whether—they will be repaid.
VASP Regulatory Money Maze Simulator
Test your virtual asset business model against Nigeria SEC’s capital locks, supervisory levies, and stress traps.
| Minimum Capital Baseline | ₦0 | 
| Multi-Model Buffer Increase (50%) | ₦0 | 
| Locked Fidelity Bond (25%) | ₦0 | 
| Licensing & Processing Fees | ₦0 | 
| Annual SEC Turnover Levy | ₦0 | 
| Cold Storage Vault Lock (80%) | ₦0 | 
| Remaining Free Cash Buffer | ₦0 | 
The proposal also gives retail investors a five-business-day cooling-off period for certain digital asset offerings. During that period, investors can withdraw their subscription and receive a full refund, subject to the conditions set out in the rules. The provision applies to subscriptions to digital asset offerings; it is not a blanket five-day withdrawal right for every cryptocurrency purchase on an exchange.
Nigerians have already seen what can happen when a crypto company fails to protect customer assets. Patricia, a Nigerian crypto startup, suffered a breach in January 2022 that was reported to have cost the company about $2 million. The company later froze withdrawals, leaving customers unable to access their assets for extended periods.
The SEC’s proposed fidelity insurance requirement is intended to provide another layer of protection against losses suffered by clients or investors as a result of operational failure, technology failure, cybersecurity breaches, custody failures, fraud, negligence, misconduct, misappropriation or unauthorised transactions.
The protection would not extend to losses caused by market movements, price volatility or poor investment performance.
Separating client money from company funds
Globally, crypto platforms can hold assets belonging to many customers in the same wallet or account, a structure commonly known as an omnibus account. But those assets are still legally and operationally distinct from the platform’s own property.
The 2022 wave of crypto failures in the United States showed the consequences when that separation breaks down. Firms including Celsius, Voyager, and FTX collapsed after taking on significant risks tied to lending, trading and related activities, leaving customers to navigate lengthy bankruptcy proceedings and uncertainty over the recovery of their assets.
In FTX’s case, the US regulators alleged that customer funds were diverted to Alameda Research, its trading affiliate, and used for expenses and debts. The collapse prompted renewed scrutiny of customer-asset segregation and custody arrangements.
In a post-FTX proposal, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said customer and company funds should be kept separate, with daily reconciliations and records showing who owns the assets. In August 2026, the US SEC also proposed stronger custody requirements for investment advisers holding customer crypto assets.
Nigeria’s SEC is proposing similar safeguards. Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) would have to keep client assets separate from their own, while Digital Asset Custodians would have to legally segregate client assets from proprietary assets and those of affiliated entities. Custodians would also have to maintain separate wallets for each client, or equivalent internal ledgering systems that accurately attribute assets to individual clients.
Custodians would also not be allowed to use client assets for proprietary trading, or lend, pledge, rehypothecate, or otherwise encumber them, unless the arrangement is disclosed, the client gives separate consent and the SEC permits it. They would also have to reconcile client assets, with discrepancies reported to the SEC within 24 hours.
VASPs must keep customer funds separate from their own when users deposit naira or withdraw money from a crypto platform. Digital asset exchanges (DAXs) cannot use customer fiat to fund their own trading, operating expenses, lending, investments, or other obligations.
“Client fiat funds received or held in connection with on-ramp or off-ramp services shall be segregated from the [virtual asset service provider] VASP’s proprietary funds and handled in accordance with the client funds, trust account, safeguarding, and settlement requirements prescribed by the Commission,” the regulator said in the draft.
Keeping client money and assets separate makes it easier to identify ownership and protect customers if a company becomes insolvent.
SEC Token Raise & Retail Limits Calculator
Check your legal token fundraising limit, SEC whitepaper taxes, or retail investment caps under Nigeria’s digital asset offering rules.
The regulator is also setting consumer-protection rules for the emerging crypto-backed lending sector. Custodians would generally be prohibited from lending, pledging, or rehypothecating client crypto assets, unless the arrangement is disclosed, the client explicitly consents, and the SEC permits it.
Digital Asset Exchanges (DAXs), meanwhile, would not be allowed to use client assets for their own benefit or for the benefit of affiliates or third parties. If an exchange wants to provide separate custody services, the proposed rules require the custody entity to be separately incorporated and registered or authorised as a Digital Asset Custodian.
Several Nigerian and Africa-serving crypto companies, including Busha, Bitmonie, and Blockchain.com, have entered the crypto-backed lending market. If the SEC’s proposal is adopted as drafted, exchanges that want to continue offering custody, lending, or related services may need to obtain the relevant registration or restructure those activities through a separately authorised entity.
A Nigerian virtual asset company operating across multiple categories could therefore face multiple registration requirements, fees, and minimum-capital thresholds, depending on the functions it performs.
Keeping crypto assets and their keys secure
Digital asset custodians would have to keep at least 80% of customer assets in cold storage, leaving only what is needed for withdrawals, settlements, and transactions in online wallets.
Cold storage systems are designed to keep crypto stored offline, reducing the risk of hackers accessing customer assets. Such examples include crypto hardware wallets which are a popular cold storage method; companies such as Trezor and Ledger manufacture physical wallets for storing crypto.
Several Nigerian cryptocurrency exchanges operate custodial wallets and storage systems, which allow them to store customer assets themselves, rather than non-custodial wallets, which users control. Requiring custodians—which can also include exchanges—to keep 80% of customer assets in cold storage could increase demand for hardware wallets and other offline storage systems from foreign manufacturers.
Yet, several hardware wallet companies do not heavily prioritise African markets, including Nigeria, due to customs duties and the loss of control over last-mile delivery.
In December 2025, Singapore-based hardware wallet manufacturer Cypherock told TechCabal that it had sold about 15,000 wallets globally, but only about 200 in Africa.
However, the proposed rules could change that. The SEC’s logic is to keep customer assets in offline locations to make them easier to retrieve when needed, such as when the regulator or other authorities need to freeze them during an investigation.
But hardware wallets have shown they are not hack-proof.
In June, hackers exploited a vulnerability in Coldcard, an offline hardware wallet built by Canadian company Coinkite, stealing about 1,779 Bitcoins worth over $113 million, according to US-based research firm Galaxy Research.
With possibly stronger demand for cold storage, however, hot storage wallet providers who primarily serve Nigerian cryptocurrency exchanges may be caught in this regulatory provision, limiting business and adoption. If custodians must keep 80% of customer assets offline, online wallet technology providers could see less demand for their services.
Technical service providers, including wallet infrastructure companies, would fall under the digital asset custody rules if they directly hold customers’ private keys. The regulator also wants multiple people or signatories involved in accessing customers' assets, so no single person can control them, as well as records that can be audited at all times, whether they use custodial or non-custodial wallets.
Stablecoins face new local requirements
Stablecoin issuers, foreign-based or local, would also have to keep enough assets in reserve to cover what they owe holders—retail users and businesses.
Naira-backed stablecoins would need reserves equal to 100% of their outstanding liabilities, in cash or cash equivalents. Foreign-currency stablecoins would need reserves worth at least 120% of what they owe, held in the same currency or equivalent cash instruments.
A USD-backed stablecoin serving the Nigerian market, such as USDT and USDC, can be held in USD instruments, but would require a higher redemption limit.
The SEC also wants stablecoin reserves to be kept separate from customer funds. While foreign issuers would not need to hold those reserves in Nigeria, they must still hire a local representative, show proof that they’re regulated abroad, and regularly disclose their reserves.
Kenya took a different approach with its gazetted rules, requiring stablecoin issuers to keep 30% of their reserves with local banks and the rest in local instruments.
On August 25, Tether opened roles for expansion leads in Nigeria and Côte d'Ivoire, underscoring the El Salvador-based issuer’s immediate focus.
Commodity-backed stablecoins, such as gold-backed tokens like Tether’s XAUt, would need to hold 100% backing, while crypto-backed stablecoins would need to hold at least $150 worth of approved liquid crypto assets for every $100 of stablecoins issued, keeping that level of backing at all times.
The rule would also prevent connected companies from controlling different parts of the same stablecoin business in a way that creates conflicts of interest.
If Company A owns Company B and Company B issues a stablecoin, Company A cannot promote that stablecoin on its platform without meeting the SEC’s restrictions and safeguards.
The SEC Stablecoin Reserve Calculator

The regulator is also tightening who can issue and list digital assets in Nigeria. Like Kenya, Nigeria has also proposed that foreign-issued stablecoins, such as USDT or USDC, must be approved by the SEC before cryptocurrency exchanges can list them on their platforms.
“A foreign-issued stablecoin shall not be listed, admitted for trading, custodied, settled, promoted, or otherwise used by a DAX [digital asset exchange] or other regulated platform in Nigeria unless recognised or authorised by the Commission,” the regulator said.
If more African countries adopt this rule, foreign stablecoin issuers like Tether and Circle must soon set up local entities in different countries to comply with specific local rules, or otherwise be selective about the countries they prioritise, forcing them to price risk.
At scale, it could lead to a scenario where USDT and USDC, popular US dollar-backed stablecoins, would no longer be accessible in certain African markets, as regulators fight to uphold monetary sovereignty.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Riskante Software-Ausfälle: Robotaxis verletzen zunehmend das eigene Testpersonal
articles.text:
Unfallrisiko Robotaxi: Abrupte Manöver führen zu Verletzungen bei Testfahrten
Menschliche Sicherheitsfahrer:innen ziehen sich bei Testfahrten in den autonomen Fahrzeugen von Waymo und Zoox immer wieder Verletzungen zu. Das geht aus Daten der US-Arbeitsschutzbehörde OSHA, wie TechCrunch berichtet.
Demnach erlitten insgesamt mehr als zwei Dutzend Testfahrer:innen in den Jahren 2024 und 2025 Verletzungen, die durch plötzliche und unberechenbare Bremsmanöver der Software ausgelöst wurden. Zu den gemeldeten physischen Schäden gehören unter anderem Schleudertraumata, Verstauchungen und Brüche des Handgelenks, aber auch anhaltende Schmerzen im Bereich der Wirbelsäule.
Systemausfälle bei Robotaxis führen zu abrupten Bremsmanövern und Spurwechseln
Bei dem zu Amazon aus Seattle im US-Bundesstaat Washington gehörenden Entwickler Zoox ereignen sich die Vorfälle vor allem in modifizierten SUV des japanischen Herstellers Toyota. Wie TechCrunch unter Berufung auf anonyme Vertragsmitarbeiter:innen schreibt, kommt es bei diesen Fahrzeugen zu sogenannten „Nogos“, bei denen sich das autonome System unerwartet abschaltet und eine plötzliche Vollbremsung auslöst.
Diese harten Bremsmanöver passieren den Berichten zufolge oft bei Geschwindigkeiten von über 70 Kilometern pro Stunde, wenn das System vermeintliche Hindernisse auf der Fahrbahn fälschlicherweise als Gefahr einstuft. Bei einem dokumentierten Vorfall im Januar 2025 verletzte sich eine Testperson durch einen solchen abrupten Stopp an der Schulter, während eine andere Fachkraft in Las Vegas nach einer unerwarteten Fahrzeugbewegung für mehr als zwei Monate mit Rückenschmerzen ausfiel.
Verletzungen auch bei Waymo-Testfahrten
Auch bei der Alphabet-Tochtergesellschaft Waymo steigen die Unfallzahlen in Verbindung mit unvorhersehbaren Fahrzeugreaktionen. Das Unternehmen vergrößert seine Flotte für den kommerziellen Betrieb dennoch. Die für Waymo tätigen Testfahrer:innen sind meist beim französischen Mobilitätsdienstleister Transdev angestellt, der für die Jahre 2024 und 2025 insgesamt 16 solcher Verletzungen an die zuständigen Behörden meldete.
Die Verletzungen traten hauptsächlich in den Großstädten San Francisco, Los Angeles und Phoenix auf, wo Waymo den Ausbau seiner autonomen Flotte zuletzt vorangetrieben hatte. In einem Fall bremste ein Fahrzeug in Los Angeles derart hart ab, dass die betroffene Testperson 175 Tage lang nicht arbeiten konnte, während ein Kollege durch eine plötzliche Lenkbewegung des Autos einen Bruch des Handgelenks erlitt.
OSHA-Richtlinien verdecken Dunkelziffer bei kleinen Startups
Die tatsächliche Zahl der verletzten Fahrer:innen in der gesamten Branche dürfte noch spürbar höher liegen, da die OSHA-Richtlinien lediglich Unternehmen mit mehr als 100 Angestellten zur öffentlichen Meldung der Verletzungsdaten verpflichten. Startups und kleinere Entwickler autonomer Fahrsysteme, die ihre Software auf öffentlichen Straßen testen, tauchen in dieser behördlichen Statistik aufgrund der gesetzlichen Ausnahmeregelung gar nicht erst auf.
Weil die unerwarteten Stopps bereits mehrfach Auffahrunfälle verursacht haben, steht das Bremsverhalten der Zoox-Fahrzeuge schon länger im Fokus der US-Verkehrssicherheitsbehörde NHTSA. Zwar spielte das Unternehmen ein Software-Update auf, um den Fehler zu beheben. Laut TechCrunch berichten Vertragsfahrer:innen jedoch, dass die Systeme trotz des Updates noch bis in den Juli 2026 hinein abrupte Vollbremsungen hinlegten.
Wie Gizmodo ergänzt, belegen diese Zwischenfälle anschaulich, dass die Softwareentwicklung den Expansionsplänen der Technologieunternehmen hinterherhinkt. Trotz der ungelösten Probleme vergrößern die Betreiber ihre Testgebiete rasant.
Die Systeme lassen sich nach wie vor von harmlosen Objekten auf der Fahrbahn irritieren und reagieren mit abrupten Stopps. Solche Phantombremsungen sind ein handfestes Sicherheitsrisiko: Sie verletzen nicht nur das Personal an Bord, sondern gefährden auch die Insassen nachfolgender Autos. Bevor die Flotten weiter wachsen, müssen die Entwickler ihre Sensorauswertungen zwingend in den Griff bekommen.

articles.title: Bharat Innovates: Building the ecosystem for India’s deeptech future
articles.text:
Bharat Innovates: Building the ecosystem for India’s deeptech future
India’s deeptech ecosystem is moving from promise to global relevance, with 4,000+ startups and growing support from academia, industry, policy, and capital. Bharat Innovates 2026 highlights what the ecosystem needs next: stronger research commercialisation, industry adoption, and patient capital.
India’s deeptech journey is rapidly evolving from early promise to global relevance. Today, the country has over 4,000 active deeptech startups, driven by an enabling policy environment, stronger industry participation, world-class research institutions, a maturing capital architecture, and a new generation of entrepreneurs building IP-led technologies that strengthen resilience in critical sectors from India, for the world.
Bharat Innovates 2026 - the recent national platform accelerating deeptech entrepreneurship, anchored by the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, in partnership with 15+ higher education Institutions, key policy stakeholders including the Department of Science and Technology (DST), the Department of Biotechnology, IN-SPACe, DPIIT and NITI Aayog, MEA, and 175+ investors, industry leaders, and ecosystem stakeholders - offered a clear signal of this growing momentum.
The Core Advisory Committee, chaired by Honourable PSAI, evaluated more than 3,000 applications, ultimately selecting 120 pioneering ventures spanning energy, supply chains, mobility, advanced manufacturing, biotechnology, advanced materials, semiconductors, artificial intelligence, space, healthcare, and climate technologies.
The scientific capability and entrepreneurial ambition demonstrated by the applicants reflected a deeptech ecosystem that has matured well beyond isolated success stories, with founders building globally competitive, differentiated technologies engineered to compete globally on performance, reliability, and cost from the outset.
Bharat Innovates 2026 surfaced three critical themes that will define the continued evolution of India’s deeptech ecosystem.
Turning scientific research into scalable ventures
The first was the vital role of academia in deeptech venture creation. Bharat Innovates reaffirmed the depth of scientific capability and research-led entrepreneurship emerging from India’s academic ecosystem. This transition is propelled by a robust network of 21,400+ scientific research bodies, R&D organisations, and technical institutions - collectively anchoring a talent pool of over one crore STEM students.
Institutions like IIT Madras are increasingly demonstrating how academia can evolve beyond knowledge creation to become a catalyst for translational research and technology commercialisation. Throughout the programme, leading universities like IIT Bombay and IIT Gandhinagar played a critical role in steering the evaluation process and convening pre-summit engagements that brought together stakeholders within the deeptech ecosystem to identify opportunities, challenges and collaborative solutions.
The ventures showcased Agnikul, Ather Energy, BacAlt, Brainsight AI, IdeaForge, and Sarvam AI, each born out of academia, exemplify how scientific breakthroughs can be translated into globally competitive deeptech enterprises across advanced manufacturing, mobility, advanced materials, medtech, defence, and AI. The opportunity now is to further strengthen our research infrastructure to translate scientific discovery into venture-scale enterprises through technology transfer, translational research, founder-friendly IP frameworks, validation infrastructure, and closer collaboration between researchers, entrepreneurs, and industry.
Why industry partnerships matter for deeptech
Second, the program reinforced the critical role of industry participation in accelerating deeptech commercialisation. Across evaluations, pre-summits, and sectoral roundtables, there was strong alignment that structured co-development, paid pilots, lighthouse customers, and long-term procurement pathways provide the technical validation, operational learning, and commercial credibility gained only through real-world deployment.
Many of the ventures showcased through Bharat Innovates illustrated how early industry adoption can accelerate the journey to commercial scale.
AmpereHour Energy, now India’s largest battery energy storage systems (BESS) operator, is deploying grid-scale energy storage in partnership with leading companies like ReNew Power, IndiGrid, and Serentica Renewables.
Tsuyo is commercialising indigenous, rare-earth-free electric powertrain technologies with leading OEMs like Volvo, Mahindra, and the Sonalika Group.
Intello Labs is leveraging Physical AI to transform quality assessment across fresh produce value chains in partnership with Reliance Fresh, Adani, and others market leaders.
Ethereal Machines’ advanced manufacturing platform is supplying high-precision components to marquee aerospace clients like HAL, BEL, and Collins Aerospace.
Lohum is leading India’s lithium-ion battery recycling sector, working with global players like Mercedes-Benz Energy, MG Motor India, and Glencore.
The scale of commercial adoption is already measurable: national data reveals that 300+ large corporations are now actively investing in, acquiring, or partnering with technology startups, driving a 30% year-on-year surge in corporate-startup open innovation pathways.
Both Amperehour and Tsuyo were also selected to represent India at VivaTech 2026 - their recognition at Europe’s largest technology, innovation, and entrepreneurship platform is strong validation of India’s growing ability to build world-class deep tech solutions.
The imperative now is to deepen industry adoption of homegrown innovation, creating the commercial pathways that enable deeptech startups to scale while strengthening strategic capability across India’s critical value chains.
Deeptech needs patient, specialised capital
Finally, Bharat Innovates reflected the need for a purpose-built capital architecture aligned with the longer development cycles of scientific innovation. India’s capital stack is beginning to mature to support this shift. Landmark initiatives such as the Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, and the Rs 10,000 crore Deep Tech Fund of Funds are catalysing the long-term strategic capital architecture required to strengthen India’s deep tech innovation economy.
As more companies progress from discovery to commercialisation and manufacturing scale-up, this architecture must continue to deepen - bringing together patient public funding, venture capital, specialised debt, working capital, catalytic finance, as well as domestic and international institutional capital to support every stage of the deep tech journey.
Engaging with the exceptional winning cohort at Bharat Innovates reinforced our conviction that the next generation of Indian deeptech founders is building for international scale from day one - engineering technologies that can outperform foreign counterparts on performance, efficiency, reliability, and cost. Their ambition must be met by equally supportive institutional scaffolding built on interdisciplinary collaboration across policy, academia, industry, and capital. With world class scientific talent and a unified ecosystem, India is well positioned to lead the world in deep tech, placing growth, resilience and global technology leadership at the heart of the nation’s growth story.
(Anjali Bansal is the Founding Partner of Avaana Capital, an early-stage venture capital firm)

articles.title: Android TV : nettoyez votre expérience TV lente et bourrée de pubs avec ce prompt
articles.text:
Android TV : nettoyez votre expérience TV lente et bourrée de pubs avec ce prompt
Grâce à quelques manipulations simples et un prompt, vous pouvez retrouver un téléviseur Android TV ou Google TV fluide et débarrassé du superflu.
LG 55G6
Il y a quelques semaines, nous vous disions tout le bien que nous pensions de solutions logicielles comme Projectivy Launcher pour se débarrasser des pires travers de Google TV et Android TV. En cette fin août, une autre solution propose d'arriver au même résultat, possiblement de manière encore plus efficace. Il s'agit d'un prompt créé par un développeur pour faire le grand ménage dans son téléviseur et profiter d'une interface plus réactive.
Désencombrer Google TV et Android TV : l'astuce du prompt IA
Pour parvenir à ce résultat, le prompt exécuté depuis un PC ordonne à l'agent IA de désactiver les bandeaux de pub et de recommandations, de bloquer les services et applications d'usine inutiles (bloatwares) et d'accélérer le téléviseur là où c'est possible. Le terme “désactiver” a ici toute son importance : la consigne impose d'opérer par étapes et de ne rien désinstaller, évitant ainsi tout risque de panne irréversible et permettant un retour en arrière à tout moment.
Garde-fous et précautions : désactiver sans tout casser
Il reste néanmoins recommandé de surveiller quels modules sont mis en veille afin d’éviter les mauvaises surprises, comme la désactivation d'un bouton de télécommande. Le déverrouillage du bootloader demeure quant à lui fortement déconseillé. Notons qu’à la fin du scénario, l’installation du lanceur d’applications open source FLauncher est proposée, bien qu’il soit tout à fait possible d’en choisir un autre par la suite.
Pour utiliser ce prompt (disponible ici), voici la marche à suivre :
- Activez les options pour les développeurs sur le téléviseur en appuyant sept fois sur la ligne Build (dans Paramètres > Système > À propos)
- Activez le débogage via Paramètres > Système > Options pour les développeurs > Débogage USB (ou sans fil si l'option est présente)
- Notez l'adresse IP du téléviseur affichée dans Paramètres > Réseau et Internet > État. Le téléviseur et le PC doivent impérativement être connectés au même réseau local
- Ouvrez Claude Code ou Codex sur son ordinateur, puis coller le prompt en remplaçant les mentions FILL THIS IN par la marque de la TV et son adresse IP
- Lancez le prompt : l'agent IA va installer automatiquement les outils nécessaires, procéder au nettoyage et solliciter la validation de l'utilisateur si besoin
Comme toujours avec les prompts issus d'Internet, la prudence reste de mise. Néanmoins, des retours d'expérience s'avèrent très positifs et la démarche suivie par le script apparaît parfaitement légitime.
