articles.title: File servers are here to stay. Here’s how to manage them securely
articles.text:
From soaring cloud costs to risk ownership, data sovereignty and legacy compatibility, there are many reasons why organizations continue to rely on file servers for inexpensive and abundant local storage. Yet no matter where your data lives, access governance is essential to keeping it in the right hands.
Even firmly into the cloud era, countless organizations continue to maintain on-premises file servers alongside their various SaaS subscriptions. These kinds of hybrid setups help businesses preserve large volumes of data while maintaining full control over cost, risk, retention, backups and access.
While the convenience of cloud services is still a big draw that drives many ongoing migration efforts, concerns like spiking subscription costs, data ownership and regulatory demands have caused others to pause or even rethink their cloud strategy.
So despite predictions of a gleaming, cloud-only future, it appears that the humble file server will stick around as an IT mainstay for years to come. No matter the reason your organization continues to rely on file servers, the important part is that you administer them securely and efficiently.
With the level of control and risk ownership that on-premises infrastructure affords you, effective access governance is essential to protecting your data.
Here are five best practices that every file server administrator needs to know.
#1: Never assign permissions directly to users
In order to grant a user access to a directory, you should always use a dedicated, single-purpose security group that follows a consistent naming scheme such as fs_finance_read.
Even though most admins are aware of this, sticking to the rule can be tricky in practice when some higher-up is shouting about how a team member needs access RIGHT NOW.
The problem with assigning access directly to users is that there is no way to track these one-off permissions. When you inspect a user object, you can see every group they are a member of. By naming groups after the permission they grant, this effectively doubles as a list of everything a user has access to.
However, when a user is privileged on a folder directly, the only place that permission shows up is in the properties of the folder itself. Even in a relatively small environment with only a few hundred directories, this makes one-off permissions effectively invisible.
Best Practice Guide to Active Directory & File Server Governance
A must-read for sysadmins: Our best practice guide lays out essential tips and tricks for governing access in Microsoft environments.
Clean up group structures, improve visibility and lower your workload – Dive in today!
Download Free White Paper
#2: Nest permission groups using the AGDLP model
As we’ve established, dedicated security groups are the best way to grant users access to file server directories. However, that does not mean you should add users directly to these security groups. File server administration becomes even more efficient when you add another layer of abstraction.
First, create global groups that map to the different roles in your organization: sales, customer support, human resources and so on. Next, make these global groups a member of the individual permission groups for each resource a user in that role needs access to.
By layering groups this way, you can now provide new users with all the access they need simply by adding them to the global role group that matches their job.
This approach is known as the AGDLP model, short for the nested structure of accounts, global groups, domain local groups and finally permissions. Following AGDLP or similar models allows you to implement a form of role-based access control for file server and Active Directory resources, streamlining access governance significantly.
#3: Set share permissions leniently, use NTFS to control access
Share permissions control access to network resources such as file shares. However, since NTFS permissions apply to both network and local access while also giving you more granular control over permission levels, most admins prefer to use NTFS permissions for governing access.
When NTFS and share permissions interact, the more restrictive permission level wins out. This makes it easiest to set share permissions to a high level – such as Change for users and Full Control for admins – while relying on NTFS permissions to restrict access from there.
#4: Avoid breaking inheritance
To streamline file server governance, focus on managing the top levels of your directory tree and let permissions propagate down from there. This works best with a clean folder structure that allows you to make full use of permission inheritance.
Ideally, you never want to set explicit permissions deeper than two or three levels down your directory tree.
Of course, admins rarely get to work under ideal conditions. Years of clutter plus leadership demands may force you to find workaround solutions in order to give users access to a specific project folder buried deep in a department share.
Even then, however, it can be easier to create new folders or move it up the directory tree rather than to overwrite inherited permission and deal with the knock-on effects on subfolders and files.
#5: Adhere to the Principle of Least Privilege
Users should only have access that is strictly necessary for their job and, even then, must hold the most restrictive permission level that still allows them to accomplish their task. The Principle of Least Privilege is a foundational concept of IT security that should inform all your decisions about access on file servers and beyond.
Importantly, the Principle of Least Privilege is more than just a one-time check the moment you grant a user access. Roles and responsibilities change over time, and so too can whether someone still needs access to a resource.
This permission may have fit their job duties when you assigned it, but is it still relevant after a month? A quarter? A year?
The only way to ensure that users privileges align with their day-to-day responsibilities is to review them periodically and revoke any that no longer serve a purpose. However, these kinds of privilege audits are challenging to implement without a centralized governance platform to track user permissions and manage access review policies.
Unfortunately, manual oversight simply is not up to the task when it comes to enforcing least privilege access.
Automated, best practice governance with tenfold
From nested permission groups to a clean folder structure, the right approach to file server administration will lower your workload while bringing order to the chaos.
Yet even if you follow every best practice in the book, managing file servers remains a very demanding and time-consuming task – especially as just one piece of your entire IT infrastructure.
There is only one way to deliver a truly seamless file server experience: A dedicated governance solution like tenfold. As a fully automated platform, tenfold can not only take over provisioning tasks, approval workflows and group management.
It also provides in-depth visibility into every level of your directory tree, showing you exactly who has access and why. Not just for your file server, but all local and cloud privileges.
With comprehensive Identity Governance from role-based access to lifecycle management, an in-depth Data Access Governance toolset and ever growing Event Auditing feature, tenfold combines three solutions in just one convenient platform. articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro : pourquoi vous ne pourrez sans doute pas le précommander comme les autres années
articles.text:
Alors que la conférence Apple du 9 septembre 2026 est désormais officialisée, c’est surtout le reste du calendrier de lancement de l’iPhone 18 et de l’iPhone 18 Pro qui attire l’attention cette année. Entre un décalage des précommandes pour respecter une date sensible, une sortie générale prévue le 18 septembre et des rumeurs sur un modèle pliable, l’iPhone Ultra, qui pourrait arriver plus tard, voici ce que l’on sait des prochaines étapes avant l’arrivée des nouveaux iPhone… et de l’iPhone 18, attendu pour 2027.
Apple tiendra bien son événement spécial le mercredi 9 septembre 2026 à 10 h (heure de la côte Ouest des États-Unis), soit 19 h en France, au Steve Jobs Theater de Cupertino. C’est lors de cette keynote que devraient être dévoilés l’iPhone 18 Pro, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max, ainsi que, potentiellement, le premier iPhone pliable d’Apple, parfois évoqué sous le nom d’« iPhone Ultra ». Les nouvelles Apple Watch (Ultra 4 et Série 12) sont également attendues.
Mais si la date de l’annonce ne fait plus débat, c’est bien la suite du calendrier qui devrait amener le plus de de changements.
Précommandes décalées au samedi 12 septembre à minuit (heure pacifique)
Contrairement aux années précédentes, où les précommandes ouvraient traditionnellement le vendredi suivant la keynote à 5 h du matin (heure pacifique), Apple aurait décidé de déplacer cette étape cruciale. En 2026, le vendredi 11 septembre correspond au 25e anniversaire des attentats du 11-Septembre. Par respect, la marque californienne choisirait donc de repousser l’ouverture des réservations au samedi 12 septembre.
Autre nouveauté : l’horaire. Selon plusieurs sources, dont MacRumors, les précommandes débuteraient à minuit pile (heure pacifique), soit 3 h du matin à New York et 9 h en France métropolitaine. Ce créneau s’appliquerait aux iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max et aux nouvelles Apple Watch.
Il s’agirait d’une première depuis 2019. Depuis l’iPhone 11, Apple a en effet pour habitude de démarrer ses précommandes à 14 h le vendredi.
iOS 27 disponible le 14 septembre, deux jours avant la vente
Comme à son habitude, Apple devrait rendre sa nouvelle version d’iOS disponible quelques jours avant la mise en vente effective des iPhone. Cette année, iOS 27 serait ainsi accessible à partir du lundi 14 septembre à 8 h (heure locale). Cette mise à jour logicielle devrait rester compatible avec tous les iPhone sortis depuis 2019 (iPhone 11 et modèles ultérieurs), mais certaines fonctionnalités, notamment celles liées à Apple Intelligence, seraient réservées aux modèles les plus récents (iPhone 15 Pro et suivants).
Mise en vente officielle : vendredi 18 septembre à 8 h locale
La date de commercialisation des nouveaux iPhone devrait, elle, respecter la tradition : le vendredi suivant la keynote, soit le 18 septembre 2026. À partir de 8 h, heure locale, les iPhone 18 Pro et Pro Max seraient disponibles en boutique et en ligne.
Rappelons que l’iPhone 18 « standard », celui qui équipe chaque année le plus grand nombre d’utilisateurs, ne serait, d’après les rumeurs, pas attendu avant 2027. Apple suivrait en effet un cycle de renouvellement annuel plus étalé qu’à son habitude.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra review - sets the bar for flagship foldable smartphones - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra continues to set the benchmark for premium foldable smartphones. It's flagship features, stunning design, excellent cameras, longer battery life and Galaxy AI puts unlimited possibilities at your fingertips.
- RATING
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra remains the pinnacle of the company’s foldable portfolio delivering pro level performance and stunning design.
While the new Galaxy Z Fold8 with its passport shape has stolen most of the headlines, the Fold8 Ultra has also seen an impressive improvement.
The Fold8 Ultra remains the device aimed at pro-level high end users, content creators and multitaskers.
Tech Guide has been using the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra for three weeks.
DESIGN
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra hasn’t had a massive change design-wise but Samsung has still managed to make it thinner.
It’s not much thinner but you can see they barely had room to fit the USB-C charging port.
Not that the previous model, the Fold7 was overly bulky. It was the first Samsung foldable that looked just like a regular phone in size and thickness and thankfully they’ve carried that forward with the Fold8 Ultra.
It is just 4.1mm thick when unfolded and weighs just 215g.
And despite the fact it’s a foldable device that happens to be thin and light, it doesn’t compromise its durability.
The device is made from armour aluminium and fitted with Corning Gorilla glass.
It has an IP48 rating, which offers water resistance against accidental spills and splashes.
DISPLAYS
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra has a 6.5-inch front screen and an 8-inch internal screen with up to 3000 nits peak brightness.
They are sharp and clear for you to view in any conditions at any time of the day or night.
The size of the front screen has increased over the years and the bezels have also shrunk.
It has now reached a point where it can be used for your day-to-day and immediate activities like answering calls and responding to messages.
One complaint we’ve had in years gone by with previous models is that the front screen didn’t offer us enough room with our fat thumbs to complete those everyday tasks and we were forced to open the device to complete them.
But since the Fold7 last year and this year’s Fold8 Ultra, that is no longer an issue.
Of course you’ve got the larger 8-inch display when you unfold the device, which is the ideal venue for viewing your content and multitasking.
The difference here between the Fold8 Ultra and the new Fold8 is the shape of that larger inside screen.
The Fold8 Ultra screen is square and while it gives you more room to move than the Fold8, the result is the same no matter how you hold the device.
The Fold8 7.6-inch display has a 4:3 shape, which means it has a landscape and portrait viewing mode.
That’s not the case with the Fold8 Ultra but your content still looks rather impressive.
And the crease is now virtually invisible when you open the Fold8 Ultra.
The hinge technology has improved remarkably over the year.
What helps here is the new Flex Titanium technology not only adds strength, virtually eliminates the crease and improves the viewing experience.
PERFORMANCE
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy it offers slick performance when switching between apps and multi-tasking and running up to three apps at a time on the larger screen.
Whether you are watching content or playing the latest games the Fold8 Ultra has more than enough juice to keep things flowing smoothly and seamlessly.
The device is running the One UI 9 – a minimal and easy-to-navigate interface above Android 17.
Also on board is Galaxy AI, which can keep you on top of things and boost your efficiency and creativity.
Whether it’s editing your photos or bringing your calendar to your fingertips when discussing your plans, the onboard Galaxy AI we’ll provide the nudges that you need to take action and get things done.
CAMERAS
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra offers a slight improvement to the triple camera system.
It includes 200MP main wide camera with improved high dynamic range, a new 50MP ultra-wide to offer added detail and clarity for wider shots, and a 10MP telephoto camera.
The big change here is the move to a 50MP ultra-wide camera – up from the 12MP on the Z Fold7. This improved resolution means sharper wider shots.
Optical zoom is limited to 3x and 30x digital zoom – not in the same league as the S26 Ultra, which has 5x and 100x Space Zoom – but it’s still respectable.
Both selfie cameras – the one on the front screen and on the main screen – are 10MP.
On the video side the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra can shoot up to 8K video at 30 frames a second and 4K at 60 frames a second.
What continues to impress with the Samsung Galaxy cameras is its Nightography, which can produce remarkable results in near darkness.
We took a shot of our astrophotography set up and the amount of light it somehow added it was amazing.
BATTERY
Another area which has been boosted is the battery capacity.
Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra has a 5000 mAh battery, which is a decent jump from the Fold7’s 4,400 mAh battery.
And the great thing is that despite powering two screens, three cameras, and multi-tasking, the battery easily got us through an entire day and well into the next before we even had to think about charging.
And when it was time to recharge, we got back to 100 per cent quickly, either through the 45W wired charging or the 20W wireless charging.
We went from 20 per cent to 100 per cent with a 45W charger in 48 minutes.
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra is available now and is priced from $2,999.
VERDICT
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra continues to set the benchmark for premium foldable smartphones. It’s flagship features, stunning design, excellent cameras, longer battery life and Galaxy AI puts unlimited possibilities at your fingertips.

articles.title: Une caméra dans votre brosse à dents : Dyson dévoile la CameraJet pour viser l'espace entre les dents
articles.text:
C’est à Paris que Dyson a décidé de présenter son tout nouvel appareil : une brosse à dents connectée. Son nom ? Dyson CameraJet. Une appellation qui peut surprendre puisqu’elle ne contient aucune référence à l’hygiène bucco-dentaire. Toutefois, ce nom permet de comprendre rapidement le principe : une micro-caméra logée près de la tête de brosse repère les interstices entre les dents et y envoie un jet de bain de bouche pendant le brossage.
Un produit high-tech et un sujet de santé
La marque insiste beaucoup sur l’aspect high-tech. En effet, la Dyson CameraJet a nécessité six ans de développement, 38 brevets, 661 ingénieurs, 470 000 images dentaires collectées et 16 millions de lignes de code pour le bon fonctionnement de la caméra. Tout cela pour aboutir à l’expérience de brossage de dents la plus complète selon le constructeur.
Dyson part d’un constat que les dentistes répètent depuis des années. Neuf personnes sur dix n’utilisent pas le fil dentaire aussi souvent qu’elles le devraient, et on passe en moyenne 45 secondes à se brosser les dents, loin des deux minutes conseillées. Or c’est justement entre les dents que la plaque s’installe en premier, avant d’engendrer mauvaise haleine, tartre et caries. Selon l’Organisation mondiale de la santé, près de 3,7 milliards de personnes dans le monde sont touchées par une maladie bucco-dentaire.
Votre production solaire dépasse votre consommation ? Le SolarFlow 2400 AC+ stocke automatiquement votre surplus dans vos batteries. 100 % compatible avec la grande majorité des installations solaires en toiture, il permet de faire évoluer votre système simplement et à moindre coût.
Gap Optical Targeting : une caméra qui vise entre les dents
Le cœur du produit, c’est la technologie que Dyson appelle Gap Optical Targeting. Une caméra macro de 100 000 pixels filme l’intérieur de la bouche à 28 images par seconde. Un algorithme maison, entraîné par apprentissage automatique, identifie les espaces entre les dents, les suit et anticipe leur position. Dès qu’un interstice est repéré, l’appareil y projette en moins de 100 millisecondes un jet conique de bain de bouche. La brosse voit ce qu’on ne voit pas et arrose la zone au bon moment.
Le jet lui-même a demandé des années de mise au point. Les hydropulseurs classiques envoient un filet d’eau fin, un peu comme une aiguille, qui traverse la plaque sans toujours la décoller. Dyson a préféré une pulvérisation en éventail composée de centaines de milliers de microgouttelettes, censée couvrir une plus grande surface tout en travaillant à basse pression pour rester douce sur les gencives et l’émail. Pour tester tout ça sans multiplier les essais cliniques, la marque a carrément mis au point une plaque dentaire artificielle avec la faculté de médecine dentaire de l’Université nationale de Singapour.
Le reste de l’ingénierie suit la même logique du détail poussé loin. Un réservoir dit « anti-gravité » de 12,5 ml délivre le bain de bouche de façon régulière, que la brosse soit tenue droite, inclinée ou à l’horizontale, ce qui est pratique pour l’arrière des dents. La station d’accueil remplit la brosse en cinq secondes et la recharge, et un étui de voyage est fourni. La tête de brosse combine deux types de poils, embarque une puce RFID qui prévient quand il faut la changer, et existe en version pour dents sensibles.
Dyson vend aussi son propre dentifrice et son bain de bouche, pensés pour aller avec la brosse. Le dentifrice ne mousse pas, ce qui aide la caméra à garder une vue nette, et les deux contiennent du fluor et du xylitol. Côté connexion, la CameraJet passe par le Wi-Fi 2,4 GHz et le Bluetooth, et l’application MyDyson affiche en direct l’image de la caméra, comme un petit endoscope qui montre ce que voit le dentiste. Bon point pour la vie privée : d’après Dyson, la caméra ne s’active qu’en visualisation ou en mode jet automatique, et aucune image n’est enregistrée.
Un prix conséquent : 479 euros
Dyson met en avant un essai clinique de quatre semaines mené en Italie sur 60 personnes. La marque annonce jusqu’à 58 % de plaque en moins et une nette réduction de l’inflammation des gencives face au brossage manuel.
La brosse à dents connectée n’a rien d’une idée neuve. C’est pourquoi Dyson tente de se démarquer avec sa caméra qui vise le jet entre les dents en temps réel.
La CameraJet est affichée au prix officiel de 479 euros et elle est disponible dès aujourd’hui dans les Dyson Demo Stores et chez les revendeurs partenaires. On est donc sur un positionnement très haut de gamme dans la lignée des aspirateurs ou des sèche-cheveux de la marque.
À titre de comparaison, une des grosses références du marché, l’Oral-B iO Series 6, est au prix officiel de 210 euros (et se trouve moins cher chez certains revendeurs). Rappelons aussi que la tête de brosse de la Dyson CameraJet est à changer régulièrement tandis que le dentifrice qui ne mousse pas comme le bain de bouche pensés pour la caméra sont vendus à part par Dyson. Autant d’achats récurrents à ajouter au budget si l’on veut profiter de l’appareil comme prévu.

articles.title: “Echaré de menos este trabajo”: Tim Cook se despide como CEO de Apple con una emotiva carta a sus empleados
articles.text:
En Apple, un cambio de CEO no se lee como un simple movimiento de organigrama. Quienes seguimos de cerca a la compañía sabemos que su historia reciente se ha contado, sobre todo, a través de etapas muy reconocibles: la Apple moldeada por Steve Jobs y la Apple que bajo Tim Cook se hizo mucho más amplia, más global y más apoyada en servicios. Hubo otros directores ejecutivos en la historia de la compañía, pero su memoria pública se ordena alrededor de esos dos nombres. Por eso la despedida de Cook como CEO no es solo el final de un cargo: es el cierre de una era.
El relevo ya estaba anunciado desde abril y llega ahora a su fecha efectiva. Apple comunicó entonces que Cook dejaría el puesto de consejero delegado el 1 de septiembre de 2026 para convertirse en presidente ejecutivo del consejo, mientras John Ternus, hasta ahora responsable de Ingeniería de Hardware, asumiría el cargo de CEO y se incorporaría también al consejo de administración.
La carta de Tim Cook en su último día como CEO
El cierre de etapa tuvo una parte pública y otra interna. En X, Cook agradeció el apoyo de la comunidad de Apple en su último día como CEO y recordó que su cargo cambiaría al día siguiente, aunque no su vínculo con quienes han acompañado a la compañía durante estos años. Puertas adentro, según publicó Bloomberg, el mensaje fue más largo y personal: un memorando enviado a todos los empleados en el que habló de gratitud, cultura y confianza en John Ternus. Este es el texto completo, traducido al español.
Equipo,
Hoy es mi último día como CEO de Apple. Este es un momento que siempre supe que llegaría algún día y, aun así, todavía cuesta creer que haya llegado y que esté escribiendo estas palabras. Amo esta compañía y al equipo que hay detrás de ella, y no podía dejar pasar este día sin enviaros una nota para deciros lo agradecido que estoy por todas las muestras de afecto que me habéis enviado, por la forma en que habéis dado lo mejor de vosotros cada día y, sobre todo, por el privilegio de toda una vida que ha sido serviros como vuestro líder.
La verdad es que, diga lo que se diga sobre mi éxito, sé que todo se debe a vosotros. Habéis sacado lo mejor de mí. En toda mi vida, nunca he visto ni he estado con un equipo de personas tan extraordinario, y cada día veo nuevos ejemplos de ello.
Hay algo verdaderamente especial en Apple. De lo que más orgulloso estoy es de aquello que un informe anual jamás podría capturar. Este lugar es la prueba de que la cultura triunfa sobre todo. Compartimos la convicción de que lo que construimos importa y de que tenemos tanto la oportunidad como la responsabilidad de dejar el mundo mejor de lo que lo encontramos. Ese propósito es parte de lo que hace que este lugar sea extraordinario. Apple ayuda a alimentarlo, pero creo que vivía dentro de cada uno de vosotros mucho antes de que llegarais aquí. Es lo que os trajo a esta compañía y lo que sigue impulsando el trabajo que hacéis cada día.
Juntos hemos creado algo mucho mayor de lo que cualquiera de nosotros podría haber imaginado o conseguido solo. Y ese es el secreto de nuestro éxito. Sacamos lo mejor los unos de los otros. Nos impulsamos unos a otros. Hemos hecho posible dejar nuestra “marca en el universo”, como Steve lo describió una vez, por quienes somos y por lo que creemos, por lo que valoramos y por cómo vemos el mundo. Qué afortunados somos. Qué afortunado soy yo.
Como sabéis, no me voy de Apple. Pero me aparto de un papel que he amado profundamente. Echaré de menos este trabajo de formas que apenas puedo empezar a imaginar, aunque sigo completamente en paz con mi decisión. Echaré de menos lideraros y estar con vosotros en cada paso, aunque siento un enorme consuelo al entregar el timón a alguien tan brillante, maravilloso y capaz como John. Pocas personas entienden lo que hace falta para construir productos que cambian el mundo como lo entiende John, y no podría estar más entusiasmado por su liderazgo.
Espero que sepáis cuánto os aprecio y qué honor ha sido ser vuestro CEO. Sobre todo, espero que sigáis sintiéndoos orgullosos de formar parte de este lugar extraordinario que llamamos Apple y que siempre le deis lo mejor de vosotros. Cuando ponemos todo lo que somos en este trabajo, cuidándonos los unos a los otros y cuidando a las personas a las que servimos, no hay límite para la profunda diferencia que podemos marcar.
Espero veros en mi nuevo papel en Apple Park y alrededor del mundo.
Con todo lo que tengo y todo lo que soy, siempre vuestro,
Tim
La próxima escena pública llegará muy pronto. Apple tiene fijado para el 9 de septiembre su evento “Un rayo de wow”, una keynote que, por calendario, ya pertenecerá a la etapa de John Ternus como CEO. Sobre la mesa está la nueva familia iPhone y también la posibilidad de que la compañía muestre su primer modelo plegable. La despedida de Cook, por tanto, no cierra solo una etapa interna: deja a Apple a las puertas de enseñar cómo quiere presentar su siguiente capítulo.

articles.title: AWS recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: AI Infrastructure Solutions, Q4 2025 | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
AWS recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: AI Infrastructure Solutions, Q4 2025
We’re excited to share that AWS has been recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: AI Infrastructure Solutions, Q4 2025. In this evaluation of 13 providers, AWS received the highest score in the Strategy category.
We believe this recognition reflects our commitment to delivering flexible, cost-efficient AI infrastructure that helps you move from experimentation to production-ready AI at scale.
The growing importance of AI infrastructure
As AI adoption accelerates, you need infrastructure that supports the full lifecycle of AI workloads—from training and fine-tuning to inference at scale.
According to Forrester’s evaluation, successful AI infrastructure requires three elements:
- Workload-specific architecture tailored for training, fine-tuning, and inference rather than generic computational needs.
- Engineering efficiency with coordinated design across compute, network, storage, and orchestration to maximize utilization.
- Sustainability and flexibility addressing power, cooling, and avoiding vendor lock-in.
What Forrester evaluated
The Forrester Wave: AI Infrastructure Solutions, Q4 2025 assessed 13 providers across detailed criteria spanning current offering, strategy, and customer feedback. AWS received the highest score possible (5.00) in 16 criteria, including:
Current offering category
- Architecture
- Ecosystem
- Data management
- Training
- Development
- Management and operations
- Fault tolerance
- Efficiency
- Security
- Scalability
Strategy category
- Vision
- Innovation
- Roadmap
- Partner ecosystem
- Pricing flexibility and transparency
 
How AWS approaches AI infrastructure
Our approach to AI infrastructure centers on customer choice and cost efficiency. We offer both proprietary AI chips, AWS Inferentia and AWS Trainium, alongside NVIDIA GPU instances. With both options, you can match the right compute to each workload without lock-in.
As Forrester noted in the report: “AWS’ vision is to offer both proprietary accelerators and NVIDIA GPUs, giving customers cost-efficient options for inference workloads without hardware lock-in. Its custom silicon delivers strong performance for mainstream tasks, while NVIDIA supports high-end needs. The compelling roadmap signals continued investment in silicon development and closer integration with AWS services such as Amazon SageMaker. AWS partners closely with leading model developers, giving customers direct access to a diverse set of foundation models.”
Forrester also observed: “AWS is best for companies with high-volume or elastic inference workloads that prioritize cost efficiency but still need access to GPUs for peak performance scenarios.”
Getting started
Whether you’re scaling inference workloads or building foundation models, AWS provides the AI infrastructure to support your journey:
- Explore AWS AI infrastructure to learn about our purpose-built chips and accelerated compute options.
- Get started with Amazon Bedrock to build, customize, and deploy generative AI applications faster with fully managed foundation models (FMs).
- Read the full report to see how Forrester evaluated all 13 providers across detailed criteria.

articles.title: Un seul chargeur pour tout recharger : l'Anker Nano II 65W à 22€ chez Amazon
articles.text:
La rentrée s'accompagne souvent d'un chargeur qui manque à l'appel, égaré dans un tiroir ou resté au fond d'un sac de voyage. Amazon propose actuellement le chargeur Anker Nano II 65W à 22,00 € au lieu de 39,99 €, une occasion de vérifier si ce format tout en un mérite sa place dans votre trousse à câbles.
Le marché des chargeurs multiports n'a cessé de se densifier ces dernières saisons, et l'Anker Nano II 65W compte parmi les références qui reviennent régulièrement dans les rayons high tech. Pour cette rentrée, cette offre disponible chez Amazon permet de s'équiper sans bousculer son budget.
Ce chargeur vise en priorité les personnes qui jonglent au quotidien entre un smartphone, une tablette et un ordinateur portable, sans vouloir multiplier les blocs secteur dans leurs bagages ou sur leur bureau. Reste à déterminer si cette baisse de prix suffit à en faire un achat pertinent, au delà du simple argument tarifaire, ce que les sections suivantes permettent d'éclaircir.
Voici le Anker Nano II 65W à 22,00 € au lieu de 39,99 € chez Amazon !
Pourquoi choisir le Anker Nano II 65W ?
- Un tarif de rentrée : 22,00 € au lieu de 39,99 €, soit environ 45 % de remise sur le prix conseillé.
- Trois ports en un seul boîtier : deux ports USB-C et un port USB-A pour recharger plusieurs appareils à la fois.
- Un format pensé pour voyager léger : la technologie GaN II permet un gabarit nettement réduit par rapport à un chargeur classique équivalent.
Un seul boîtier pour remplacer plusieurs chargeurs au quotidien
Branché seul sur son port USB-C principal, le Nano II 65W délivre sa pleine puissance, de quoi alimenter un ordinateur portable compact comme un MacBook Air ou un Dell XPS 13. Lorsque plusieurs appareils sont connectés en même temps, la puissance de 65 W se répartit automatiquement entre les trois ports, avec une priorité maintenue sur le port principal pour l'appareil le plus gourmand. Sa compatibilité PPS ajoute une charge rapide adaptée aux smartphones Samsung Galaxy et Google Pixel les plus récents, sans nécessiter d'accessoire supplémentaire pour en profiter. Dans ses analyses consacrées à la gamme Anker Nano, la rédaction de Clubic relève une stabilité thermique appréciable sur cette ligne de chargeurs, un point rassurant pour un usage quotidien prolongé, y compris en charge simultanée sur les trois ports.
Une bonne base, sans être la solution universelle
Ce chargeur ne remplace pas un modèle plus puissant pour les ordinateurs portables gourmands dont les besoins dépassent 65 W en charge complète. Il s'adresse avant tout à qui souhaite limiter le nombre de blocs secteur à transporter au quotidien, plutôt qu'à qui recherche la charge la plus rapide possible sur chaque appareil pris isolément.
✅ Les points forts
- Trois ports pour recharger plusieurs appareils en simultané, sans multiplier les blocs secteur.
- Format compact grâce à la technologie GaN II, facile à glisser dans une trousse ou un sac à dos.
- Compatible avec la majorité des smartphones, tablettes et ordinateurs portables équipés d'un port USB-C.
- Charge rapide PPS pour les appareils Samsung Galaxy et Google Pixel les plus récents.
- Un tarif particulièrement accessible à 22,00 € pendant cette opération de rentrée.
❌ Les limites
- Les câbles de charge ne sont pas fournis et doivent être prévus séparément si besoin.
- La puissance maximale de 65 W peut s'avérer insuffisante pour certains ordinateurs portables gourmands.
- La répartition de la puissance entre les trois ports peut ralentir la charge lorsque plusieurs appareils sont branchés en même temps.
- Ce modèle a déjà fait l'objet de plusieurs offres similaires ces derniers mois, sans garantie sur la durée de celle-ci.
Le Anker Nano II 65W reste disponible à 22,00 € chez Amazon, sous réserve de stock !
Au final, l'Anker Nano II 65W tient sa promesse : un format compact, trois ports polyvalents et un tarif de 22,00 € cohérent avec les précédentes offres déjà constatées sur ce produit. Cette version sous les 25 € s'adresse particulièrement aux étudiants, aux télétravailleurs et à toute personne qui souhaite réduire le nombre de chargeurs à emporter pour la rentrée.
Les utilisateurs équipés d'un ordinateur portable très gourmand en puissance pourront en revanche passer leur chemin et se tourner vers un modèle dépassant les 65 W. Pour tous les autres profils, ce bon plan mérite d'être examiné avant qu'il ne disparaisse des rayons, comme les précédentes offres similaires observées sur ce même chargeur.

articles.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops ‘HardBreacher’ Kaspersky Product Exploit
articles.text:
The researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse has dropped another zero-day — this time a privilege escalation exploit targeting a Kaspersky endpoint security product.
Nightmare Eclipse, also known as Chaotic Eclipse, has released PoC exploits for many vulnerabilities in recent months, mainly Windows and Microsoft Defender flaws.
The researcher started dropping zero-days after growing frustrated with Microsoft’s handling of vulnerability reports. While many of the exploits remained at the PoC stage, a few ended up being exploited in the wild by malicious actors.
Over the weekend, Nightmare Eclipse released an exploit targeting a privilege escalation vulnerability in Kaspersky Endpoint Security. The exploit has been dubbed HardBreacher.
“The PoC is not in the best shape at all, it is basically duct tapped, I just managed to make it work and that’s all,” the researcher noted.
“The interesting part about this is the Kaspersky completely loses it when you take control over the UI process, you can cause it to stop functioning, grant/block access to files its not supposed to, if the PoC succeeds, the entire operating system becomes a hot mess,” the researcher added.
Contacted by SecurityWeek, Kaspersky said the underlying issue has been resolved.
“The corresponding fix is delivered via an automatic update, or users can trigger a database update manually,” Kaspersky stated.
Other exploits made public recently by Nightmare Eclipse include ShieldBreak, which allows an attacker to spawn a shell with System privileges, and LegacyHive, which enables privilege escalation.

articles.title: Sony rebate acusação e diz que PS Store não engana consumidores • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Sony rebate acusação e diz que PS Store não engana consumidores
Dona do PlayStation afirma à Justiça dos EUA que consumidores “razoáveis” entendem que jogos digitais são licenciados e não vendidos.
A Sony afirmou que consumidores “razoáveis” não são induzidos a acreditar que são proprietários dos jogos em suas bibliotecas digitais. A resposta foi apresentada à Justiça em meio à ação coletiva que a empresa enfrenta na Califórnia (EUA) por supostas práticas enganosas na PlayStation Store.
O processo se iniciou em junho e acusa a Sony de induzir consumidores ao erro ao sugerir que eles compram jogos digitais, quando, na prática, recebem apenas uma licença de uso. A empresa, por sua vez, afirma que os usuários sabem que o conteúdo adquirido na PlayStation Store é licenciado, e não vendido de forma definitiva.
Em um documento obtido pelo portal Game File, os representantes da fabricante apresentaram a primeira resposta formal ao caso. A estratégia de defesa sustenta que as informações divulgadas na loja são suficientes e claras para garantir que consumidores “não sejam induzidos a erro”.
A empresa ressalta que tanto o Contrato de Licenciamento de Produto de Software (SPLA) quanto os Termos de Serviço alertam explicitamente que “o software é licenciado, não vendido”.
Para fortalecer o argumento, a equipe jurídica da companhia traçou um paralelo com a aquisição de objetos materiais. A Sony alega que qualquer indivíduo que paga por um jogo digital compreende a impossibilidade de possuí-lo nos mesmos moldes de um bem físico.
A ação coletiva foi movida por quatro clientes da PlayStation. A base da argumentação deles está na interface de transações da PlayStation Store. Segundo a denúncia original, a terminologia usada induz o usuário a acreditar que está comprando a posse definitiva do produto. O que é entregue, contudo, é apenas o direito de acessar o jogo.
Os advogados de acusação afirmam que essa conduta pode violar leis estaduais de defesa do consumidor na Califórnia. A legislação local proíbe que empresas comercializem bens digitais usando palavras como “comprar” ou “adquirir” sem uma declaração clara e visível de que o cliente recebe apenas uma licença. A lei exige ainda que esse alerta seja feito em linguagem simples e direta.
Atualmente, a plataforma da Sony até exibe as informações sobre licenciamento no carrinho de compras. No entanto, os jogadores destacam que os avisos são apresentados em letras miúdas, exigindo cliques em links que direcionam para documentos longos e complexos.
A disputa legal ocorre em um momento delicado para a empresa, que vem enfrentando críticas após confirmar os planos de interromper a produção de jogos físicos a partir de 2028. Mesmo diante da resposta negativa de parte da comunidade, a liderança da Sony manteve a decisão.
O debate sobre licenciamento de jogos digitais também levou a Sony a esclarecer como o PlayStation gerencia o acesso offline de títulos comprados na PlayStation Store, após questionamentos sobre a verificação de licenças.

articles.title: The three forces reshaping the future of enterprise SaaS
articles.text:
The three forces reshaping the future of enterprise SaaS
How Agentic AI is changing the future of SaaS
For years, enterprise Software as a Service (Saas) has enjoyed a comfortable position at the center of organizational processes. Users who wanted to raise a ticket, process an invoice or manage a workflow would log into their employer’s cloud application. The user interface was the gateway to the work, and the provider’s business model followed naturally: charge for seats, expand adoption, and grow revenue as more users spend more time inside the platform.
Global Head of AI for Government, and Head of AI Delivery at NTT DATA.
Agentic AI is beginning to change that. As users increasingly deploy AI agents, either to carry out tasks within SaaS platforms or to deliver functionality outside them, organizations require fewer seats – hitting providers’ subscription revenues.
At the same time, AI is making bespoke software faster and cheaper to build, giving organizations a credible alternative to buying another SaaS platform. Why accept subscription costs and vendor lock-in, when cheaper alternatives may achieve the same outcome?
None of this means SaaS is about to disappear, but its position at the center of enterprise software is under threat. SaaS vendors are facing three structural challenges that will reshape the economics of enterprise software.
Agents become the user
The first threat is simple: users may have AI agents carry out tasks within the SaaS platform, reducing the need for human users, or build agentic capabilities outside those platforms altogether.
That is a serious problem for any SaaS vendor whose business depends on people living in the interface. If an agent can resolve a support query, update a record or complete a routine transaction, the user never has to touch the application.
We’re already seeing this in practice. In some IT service management projects, agents now resolve such a high proportion of tickets that organizations need far fewer users interacting with the SaaS platform. As buyers begin questioning whether they still need premium software for the shrinking proportion of manual work, the economics start to shift.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Bespoke is back
The second threat is the one SaaS vendors dislike most: buyers may once again be willing to build new capabilities from scratch.
For the last decade or so, ‘build versus buy’ was often a non-debate. Custom software was too slow, too expensive and too risky, so SaaS usually won.
AI is starting to shift those calculations. As software development becomes faster, cheaper and more adaptive, some solutions that previously defaulted to SaaS start to look buildable – especially when the organization needs a narrow set of capabilities wrapped around its own processes and data. The more customization a SaaS platform requires, the weaker its cost-efficiency and automated-upgrade advantages become.
This does not mean large enterprises will abandon mature SaaS platforms overnight. Their resilience, integrations and compliance capabilities remain valuable. But once customers believe they have a credible alternative, vendors lose pricing power and the assumption that renewal is the obvious decision
Business model redundancy
The third threat is that even when the product survives, the commercial model may not.
Traditional SaaS pricing was built for a world in which value correlated reasonably well with the number of people sitting in the application. That logic gets shaky when agents perform work that would once have required more licensed users, and more operational dependency on the interface.
Vendors can see this. Many are shifting towards consumption-based pricing, exposing services directly to agents or redesigning products for an agentic world. The common thread is clear: once software starts working for people rather than being operated by them, seat-based economics begin to look outdated.
From the customer’s perspective, that could be a good thing. Paying for usage is often cheaper than buying licenses. The challenge for vendors will be proving they’re genuinely adapting to an agentic future, rather than simply repackaging existing products to protect margins.
SaaS is not dead
To be clear, this is not a “SaaS is over” argument. Many enterprise platforms will remain valuable, providing governance, resilience, compliance, and years of accumulated functionality that are difficult and expensive to recreate.
What will change is where value sits. In an agentic world, SaaS will be less the primary interface through which work gets done; more a component in a broader ecosystem of agents, orchestration and systems of record. Some platforms will adapt and become stronger; others will discover that the value they once captured has shifted elsewhere.
As for the corporate users of SaaS, the best advice we can give is not to wait for perfect conditions before acting. No business ever reaches a point where its data, processes or architecture are “finished”, and SaaS providers will continue to adapt their offers.
Meanwhile, experiment, learn and adapt in your delivery of administrative and corporate functions: in some functions you may find that agents drive down SaaS costs; in others, greenfield development may now be viable. In still other cases, adding new functionality using agents that leverage SaaS solutions but sit outside those ecosystems keep future options open.
So do something that works for you now – but keep the option of moving again in a year or two.

articles.title: Kyle Lowry, Cohere and Reddit leaders, and more to headline Elevate Festival 2026 | BetaKit
articles.text:
This year’s Elevate Festival will feature a star-studded lineup of guest speakers, including Kyle Lowry, who is not only widely considered to be the greatest Toronto Raptor of all time, but is the CEO of his own tech-focused venture firm.
The news: Returning to Toronto on Sept. 22, Elevate Festival announced a stacked lineup of guest speakers Monday morning, including former Toronto Raptors’ point guard and investor in the Toronto Tempo, Kyle Lowry, Cohere’s Michael Pelosi, Reddit’s Adam Collins, Clio founder and CEO Jack Newton, and Bumble’s Vivek Sagi, among others. The tech conference, which is celebrating its ninth anniversary, is also introducing new programming focused on sovereignty, dual-use tech, and cybersecurity, which was created in collaboration with DMZ and BDC.
From the source: “This year marks an important chapter for the festival, and we’re bringing together the people and ideas that can help shape what comes next,” said Lisa Zarzeczny, the CEO and co-founder of Elevate, in a press release. “The stakes only continue to get higher, which is why conversations around AI and sovereignty are at the forefront of this year’s programming.”
The context: Across this year’s three days of programming, Elevate Festival is looking to leverage its high-profile roster of speakers to discuss what it calls some of “the most pressing conversations facing Canada’s innovation economy.” Those conversations include discussions with Collins, Reddit’s chief communications officer, on the role human perspectives play amid a rash of AI-generated internet content. There will also be conversations with Build Canada, Dominion Dynamics, Sentinel R&D, and Coveo on how Canada can own the dual-use technologies of the future; panels with Coinbase Canada on the role stablecoins are playing in the Canadian financial system; and Elevate’s Fast Forward track, which will spotlight “emerging ideas poised to become tomorrow’s competitive advantage.”
Final thought: Like others in the Canadian innovation space, Elevate Festival is putting sovereignty front and centre this year. The festival, which over its tenure has drawn upwards of 87,000 attendees, is attuning itself to the topic at a moment when the national mood is preoccupied with Canada’s security, both physical and economic.
Image courtesy Elevate. Photo by Brandon Ferguson Media.

articles.title: Why it matters that President Trump just dialed in to a NASA news conference
articles.text: As is standard procedure for major NASA missions, the US space agency held a post-launch news conference on Sunday morning at Kennedy Space Center in Florida to provide information about how the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope was faring during its initial maneuvers. What was not standard, however, is what happened in the middle of the news conference. A little less than half an hour in, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman looked down at his mobile phone, and then stood up and walked away from the dais where he had been seated behind a table along with other NASA officials. He briefly left the room. Isaacman returned about a minute later, phone in hand, apologizing for interrupting NASA's chief of science, Nicky Fox, as she was speaking about the mission. "The President of the United States of America would like to address and congratulate everyone on this mission," Isaacman said, returning to his seat. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Graphics Card Prices Are Rising Fast (Again), and GeForce Is Taking the Biggest Hit
articles.text:
GPU pricing has taken an uglier turn. In technical terms, things are 'ultra stinky' right now. We published our last GPU pricing update only about six weeks ago, and in the short time since, graphics card prices have risen sharply. We warned this was likely to happen, and unfortunately, those increases have now worked their way through to retail.
But just how badly are gamers getting stung? We're looking beyond retailers in the United States to see how this is playing out on a global scale. Are GPU prices surging everywhere, or are certain regions and models being hit much harder than others? We have plenty of data to dig through, and the picture isn't pretty.
As we've been doing for some time now, we're tracking pricing across 10 countries. Our previous update captured prices just before this latest climb began, giving us a particularly useful, if painful, snapshot of what GPUs cost immediately before the market turned upward.
We're also including data from February. That's important because GPU prices were actually trending slightly downward during the first half of 2026 for some models. July-to-August pricing shows the immediate impact of the latest hikes, while comparisons with February tell us whether cards are simply returning to earlier levels or pushing into new highs.
Before getting into the numbers, it's worth clarifying how we collect this pricing data, because we've seen some confusion in the comments on previous updates. The prices shown here are not averages for a specific GPU. They represent the single lowest price for an available, in-stock model within each region. We use price comparison websites for each country, find the cheapest model, verify that it is actually available to purchase at that price, and then include it in our data.
Often, that means we're looking at base models from any given graphics card maker rather than something like an Asus ROG Strix, Gigabyte Windforce, or PNY OC. If you want a premium model, you'll almost certainly pay more than the prices shown here.
Also keep in mind that these prices were collected several days before this article went live, so individual listings may have changed slightly. At the time of writing, however, these figures represented the minimum amount you would have needed to spend to buy each GPU brand new.
Entry-Level GeForce Pricing Takes a Sharp Turn
GeForce RTX 5050 + RTX 5060
The news isn't great if you're interested in purchasing an entry-level GeForce GPU. The RTX 5050's price remained relatively stable for several months, but has recently increased in most regions, especially India, where gamers are getting absolutely rolled.
The card is no longer available at MSRP in the US, where you're now looking at spending around $50 more, despite that being one of the regions with the smallest month-over-month increase. Across all 10 regions, the RTX 5050 is now 14% more expensive than it was in July and 19% more expensive than in February.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5050
|  | USA | Australia | Germany | UK | Canada | India | Philippines | Brazil | Poland | Netherlands | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Feb 2026 | $260 | $365 | 280 € | £230 | $380 | ₹30,700 | ₱16,700 | R$1,660 | 1,150 zł | €270 | 
| Jul 2026 | $290 | $360 | 270 € | £240 | $420 | ₹28,800 | ₱19,000 | R$1,900 | 1,135 zł | €285 | 
| Aug 2026 | $300 | $430 | 300 € | £270 | $460 | ₹44,000 | ₱19,250 | R$2,000 | 1,350 zł | €305 | 
| Change | 3% | 19% | 11% | 13% | 10% | 53% | 1% | 5% | 19% | 7% | 
It's even worse for the RTX 5060. This model is supposed to cost $300, but pricing has drastically increased in the US, where the cheapest cards now sit around $450. That's pretty outrageous for an RTX 5060.
That sort of money should be getting you an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, and absolutely did late last year, but those days are unfortunately gone. It's not just the US, either. Pricing there has jumped 32% month over month, with similarly large increases in India, Poland, and the Netherlands.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060
|  | USA | Australia | Germany | UK | Canada | India | Philippines | Brazil | Poland | Netherlands | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Feb 2026 | $300 | $520 | 310 € | £290 | $450 | ₹38,700 | ₱19,600 | R$2,300 | 1,350 zł | €320 | 
| Jul 2026 | $340 | $450 | 305 € | £275 | $450 | ₹33,500 | ₱20,000 | R$2,100 | 1,240 zł | €310 | 
| Aug 2026 | $450 | $500 | 370 € | £330 | $520 | ₹48,000 | ₱22,900 | R$2,300 | 1,650 zł | €390 | 
| Change | 32% | 11% | 21% | 20% | 16% | 43% | 14% | 10% | 33% | 26% | 
Some regions haven't been affected quite as badly. In Australia, for example, the RTX 5060 is 11% more expensive than it was in July, but it's still cheaper than it was in February. That's an outlier, though, and not something we're seeing in many other countries. Overall, the RTX 5060 is now 23% more expensive than it was in July and 18% more expensive than in February.
The RTX 5060 Ti Split Has Become Ridiculous
GeForce RTX 5060 Ti: 8GB + 16GB
It's no surprise to see a similar impact on the RTX 5060 Ti 8GB. This model stuck closest to MSRP for quite some time, but in August it could no longer resist the upward pressure. Prices have jumped massively in regions such as the US, Australia, and India. The card is now sitting around $500 in the US, which is getting dangerously close to RTX 5070 MSRP territory.
In other countries, including Germany and the UK, prices have risen compared with July but aren't substantially higher than they were in February. That's because the RTX 5060 Ti 8GB is a horrible GPU that simply hasn't been particularly desirable or in demand. During the first half of 2026, it actually fell in price and frequently sold below MSRP.
Recent increases have pushed it back toward normal pricing, or above it. Overall, the 8GB version is now 24% more expensive than it was last month and 13% more expensive than in February.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 8GB

| Change | 39% | 40% | 22% | 16% | 22% | 37% | -4% | 10% | 31% | 23% | 
The 8GB card hasn't received nearly as much attention recently as the 16GB model, because the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB is now sitting above $700, almost the MSRP of an RTX 5070 Ti. That's insane.
This model is up 22% compared with last month, which is already a very significant increase, but it's also 27% more expensive than in February. That's particularly shocking given that the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB wasn't even an MSRP-priced card in some regions back then.
Pricing for this model has continued to rise throughout 2026. In the US, it's now 70% above MSRP. Globally, it's the second most overpriced card behind the RTX 5090, sitting an average of 53% above its $430 MSRP after accounting for local currency conversions.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Feb 2026 | $500 | $750 | 540 € | £450 | $700 | ₹65,500 | ₱28,800 | R$3,700 | 2,300 zł | €600 |

The 8GB version, meanwhile, is just 14% above MSRP across the 10 regions we're examining. That illustrates the enormous discrepancy between the unpopular 8GB card and the much more desirable 16GB version.
Right now, you have to spend roughly 50% more to get 16GB of VRAM instead of 8GB at this tier, and in some regions the premium reaches 62%. That's the reality of current memory pricing.
RTX 5070 Pricing Is Bad, but the Ti Is Worse
GeForce RTX 5070 + RTX 5070 Ti
Next we have the RTX 5070. This model has risen by 20% on average over the past month and now costs 19% more than it did in February. The RTX 5070 is currently sitting 31% above its global MSRP. That's not as bad as the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, but it's still pretty bad, and these increases have significantly narrowed the gap between the two cards.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070

| Feb 2026 | $550 | $930 | 640 € | £510 | $900 | ₹70,900 | ₱39,300 | R$4,200 | 2,650 zł | €640 | 
| Jul 2026 | $600 | $860 | 580 € | £530 | $850 | ₹66,800 | ₱43,300 | R$4,200 | 2,640 zł | €620 | 
| Aug 2026 | $800 | $1,040 | 720 € | £600 | $1,080 | ₹90,000 | ₱44,500 | R$4,700 | 3,200 zł | €700 | 
| Change | 33% | 21% | 24% | 13% | 27% | 35% | 3% | 12% | 21% | 13% | 
At MSRP, the RTX 5070 should cost 28% more than the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, a difference of $120. Right now, that gap has shrunk to just 10% worldwide because both models have become more expensive, but the 5060 Ti has risen by more. In the US, the raw price gap has fallen from $120 to just $70, likely a byproduct of the RTX 5070 having a lower 12GB VRAM capacity.
The RTX 5070 Ti is an interesting one. This model is up 17% month over month and is 14% more expensive than it was in February, but many of its price increases were heavily front-loaded.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti

| Feb 2026 | $1,000 | $1,400 | 1,000 € | £800 | $1,280 | ₹109,000 | ₱61,000 | R$7,100 | 4,100 zł | €980 |

In other words, the card became dramatically more expensive at the beginning of the year and has been treading water to some degree since then. So while pricing is "only" up 17% since July, a smaller increase than we're seeing for many other models, the RTX 5070 Ti is still 44% above MSRP on average. That makes it the third most overpriced GPU on the market.
High-End GeForce Pricing Goes From Bad to Absurd
GeForce RTX 5080 + RTX 5090
The RTX 5080 tells a similar story to the RTX 5070 Ti. Prices are up 15% on average compared with July, with the US getting stung especially hard. The 24% increase there is roughly double what we're seeing in European markets such as Germany and Poland.
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080

Surprisingly, the RTX 5080 is only 8% more expensive than it was in February. This is another model where prices fell slightly during the first half of the year after rising sharply earlier on. Even so, the RTX 5080 is currently sitting 38% above MSRP on average. In the US, it's 55% above MSRP, which is a significant outlier.
Then there's the RTX 5090, which just keeps getting more ridiculous. Prices increased another 20% over the past month and are now 41% higher than in February, by far the largest six-month increase of any card we're tracking. At nearly $5,000 in the US, the RTX 5090 is 145% above MSRP there and 136% above MSRP across the 10 regions we're examining.

At this point, it's difficult to consider the RTX 5090 a gaming card. This is workstation-level pricing, and the card continues to command such ridiculous prices largely because of its AI performance and 32GB of memory.
Radeon Prices Are Rising Too, Just Not as Quickly
Radeon RX 9060 XT: 8GB + 16GB
For a slight change of pace, let's move over to Radeon, starting with the RX 9060 XT series. The 8GB model is actually the Radeon card that has been hit hardest between August and July. While this GPU saw no price increase in the US, it rose by 16% on average across the 10 regions, with particularly large increases in India, Poland, the Netherlands, and the UK.
It's now 20% more expensive than it was in February and sits 26% above its global MSRP on average.

The 16GB version hasn't seen as dramatic a recent increase, but that doesn't mean it's well priced. On average, the RX 9060 XT 16GB rose by 8% over the past month. That sounds relatively good because it's only a single-digit increase, and the card is also just 11% more expensive than it was in February.

However, the overall price is now 28% above MSRP, making it the most overpriced Radeon model relative to where it should sit in a normal market. That's a similar level of overall inflation to the RX 9060 XT 8GB, but it has occurred at different times. The 8GB model has risen more sharply recently, while the 16GB card has gradually crept upward throughout the memory crisis.
That's probably because the 16GB card is far more desirable, so stock sitting on store shelves is constantly being replaced with more expensive inventory.
The RX 9070 Series Is Holding Up Surprisingly Well
Radeon RX 9070 + RX 9070 XT
The RX 9070 has been one of the most resilient cards on the market, with relatively small price increases in several regions. On average, pricing is up 8%, largely because of significant increases in India, Brazil, and Poland. Here in Australia, for example, it's only around 5% more expensive.
The RX 9070 is also just 5% more expensive than it was in February, the smallest six-month increase of any model we're tracking, and it currently sits only 13% above MSRP.

This is supposed to be a $550 GPU and it has 16GB of VRAM, making it just as susceptible to memory pricing pressures as other 16GB cards. Given those conditions, we'd say the RX 9070 currently has one of the best prices on the market at a little over $600.
The RX 9070 XT is holding up reasonably well, too. Pricing has risen by 12% across the 10 regions, with Australia and Brazil getting hit the hardest, but we're still looking at a card that's only 8% more expensive than it was in February. Unfortunately, the RX 9070 XT is now 21% above MSRP and 16% more expensive than the RX 9070. We recently found the 9070 XT to be about 12% faster than the 9070 across a 52-game sample, so that currently makes the RX 9070 slightly better value.
That calculation does vary by region. In the Philippines, for example, the XT model makes more sense because the price gap is smaller.
Intel Battlemage Supply Keeps Getting Worse
Intel Arc B570 + B580
Lastly, we have Intel's Arc GPUs. The B570 is becoming increasingly difficult to find and doesn't appear to be in particularly good supply. Even in regions where we could find pricing, there were often only one or two listings available.
Pricing is up around 12% compared with July and 22% compared with February, although the B570 remains one of the cheapest GPUs you can buy. It's even cheaper than AMD's new RX 9050, which is diabolically bad.

The Arc B580 is in better supply, though availability still isn't great compared with GeForce or Radeon. This model has risen by 7% on average since July and 14% since February, and it now sits 25% above MSRP.
In the US, for example, it's priced similarly to the RTX 5050 while remaining comfortably below the RTX 5060. So even after these increases, the B580 remains competitive at the lower end of the market.
GPU Prices Jumped 15% in a Single Month
As expected, the current state of GPU pricing isn't pretty. After prices remained stagnant or slightly improved over the months leading into July, we've now seen a sudden and sharp increase across the market. If you didn't pick up the graphics card you wanted in June, for example, you're now getting absolutely rolled, and there's no indication that prices will return to those levels anytime soon.
Looking across every graphics card model in all 10 regions, we recorded a 15% average price increase compared with this time last month. That's the simplest number for quantifying just how quickly things have deteriorated. But it doesn't tell the full story, because these increases haven't been distributed evenly across every model or manufacturer.

Some GPU models are now 40 to 50% more expensive than they should be, which is just bloody fantastic.
GeForce GPUs have risen by 19% month over month, while Radeon GPUs are up by 11%, excluding the recently released RX 9070 GRE. That's broadly in line with what we heard would happen at the end of July, when much larger increases were expected for Nvidia cards than AMD models.
Unlike in previous GPU pricing updates, the impact across the GeForce lineup has actually been quite similar from one model to another. Previously, we saw much larger increases for 16GB GPUs compared with 8GB models. Between July and August, however, most GeForce cards simply rose by around 20%. In fact, some of the largest percentage increases have affected 8GB cards, which had previously been more resistant to rising prices.
There are a couple of ways to frame all this, depending on how positive you want to be. The positive interpretation is that GPU prices are "only" 17% higher on average than they were in February, and in some cases the latest round of increases has simply returned cards to pricing levels seen earlier in the year.
The negative interpretation is that the overall GPU market is now priced 28% above launch MSRP on average, excluding the ridiculously overpriced RTX 5090, which isn't really a gaming GPU anymore. Some models are now 40 to 50% more expensive than they should be, which is just bloody fantastic.
Memory Pricing Is Now Written All Over GeForce Prices
How Much Are Nvidia GPUs Above MSRP?
If we focus on actual dollar increases in the US market, much of the GeForce lineup has risen by an amount that broadly tracks the VRAM capacity of each card.
The RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5060 Ti 16GB are now around $300 more expensive than at launch. The RTX 5070, with 12GB of VRAM, is up $250, while the RTX 5060 and RTX 5060 Ti 8GB are roughly $120 to $150 more expensive. It's not a perfect explanation, of course. The RTX 5080 has the same 16GB of VRAM as the RTX 5070 Ti yet is now $550 above MSRP. Still, it certainly appears that Nvidia pricing is being heavily affected by increased memory costs.
A while ago, we published an article modelling what rising GDDR7 prices could do to graphics card pricing. We estimated that if memory became three times more expensive, 16GB Nvidia GPUs would become at least $250 more expensive, while 12GB models would rise by roughly $200.
We're very much living in that reality now.
Radeon Has Escaped the Worst of It, for Now
AMD GPUs haven't been affected nearly as badly, although its 16GB Radeon models are still around $100 to $150 more expensive than MSRP. There are a couple of reasons AMD's offerings have been more resistant to memory-related price increases. AMD uses GDDR6 instead of GDDR7, and its margins are different from Nvidia's. Ultimately, though, Radeon cards are still facing many of the same pricing pressures.
We suspect Radeon GPUs will become more expensive throughout the remainder of 2026, especially if you look at what's happening on the console side. The PlayStation 5, for example, is a lower-margin product than a discrete Radeon GPU and has increased in price by $150 since the middle of 2025. Of course, the PS5 also contains NAND flash, which has become significantly more expensive, but a decent portion of that increase is likely tied to its 16GB of GDDR6 becoming more costly as well.
Right now, though, the difference between GeForce and Radeon price increases has created some very interesting matchups. The RTX 5060 should be directly competing with the RX 9060 XT 8GB, but it's currently priced at roughly the same level as the RX 9060 XT 16GB. The RTX 5060 Ti 16GB and RTX 5070 are both sitting around the same price as the RX 9070 XT, which is pretty crazy considering the performance difference between those cards.
And across the 10 regions we're examining, the RTX 5070 Ti is now 50% more expensive than the RX 9070 XT. That makes it extremely difficult to recommend a GeForce GPU right now. Radeon cards are simply much better value. That value gap may not last, given the rumors of incoming Radeon price increases, but at the moment it just doesn't make much sense to buy most of Nvidia's lineup.
You could argue that it doesn't make sense to buy any GPU right now, and that's fair.
But if you're going to buy one anyway, Radeon is clearly the way to go.

articles.title: Dyson made a camera-equipped toothbrush that flosses for you
articles.text:
Dyson is once again expanding its line of personal care products with a device that focuses on your teeth instead of your hair. As the name implies, the $499 CameraJet is the first electric toothbrush to incorporate a camera into the brush head. Available starting today in ceramic blue or ceramic pink color options, it can let you inspect the inside of your mouth by livestreaming video over Wi-Fi to your phone. But the camera also works alongside an AI algorithm to detect and blast the gaps between your teeth with mouthwash. So while you’re brushing, the CameraJet simultaneously takes care of flossing.
Dyson made a camera-equipped toothbrush that flosses for you
A tiny camera triggers a blast of mouthwash that flosses between your teeth when a gap is detected.
That price isn’t cheap, but it’s also only slightly more expensive than other premium smart toothbrushes that don’t have its camera-plus-spray setup. It could be worth the splurge for those of us who are bad at regularly flossing and don’t like dealing with a disappointed dentist.
Just below the brush head is a tiny camera with a 100,000-pixel resolution and a strobing light. The toothbrush’s AI analyzes 28 live images from the camera every second as part of a feature Dyson calls Gap Optical Targeting, without storing them on the device or sending them to the cloud. Within 100 milliseconds of a gap between your teeth being detected, the CameraJet emits a cone-shaped blast of mouthwash to clean out the space. Dyson uses a wider blast than what water flossers typically employ so it can effectively remove plaque with less pressure, making the CameraJet’s flossing mechanism gentler on enamel and gums
The replaceable brush heads use a combination of softer outer bristles that safely clean along the gumline and stiffer inner bristles that are better at scrubbing away tooth stains. The brush head oscillates nearly 1,000 times each second while the angle of oscillation is constantly changing to improve the effectiveness of your brushing. Pricing on replacement brush heads isn’t known, but each one features an RFID tag so the CameraJet can track usage and alert you when a replacement is needed every three months.
To ensure its mouthwash reservoir can effectively pump no matter how the CameraJet is held — even upside down — instead of sticking a tube into the reservoir, there’s an air bladder inside the tank that slowly inflates to fill empty space, minimize air pockets, and maintain a constant pressure. An elaborate docking station recharges the toothbrush and can automatically fill its built-in 12.5ml mouthwash reservoir in just three seconds.
While the CameraJet will work with your regular toothpaste and mouthwash, Dyson also plans to sell its own non-foaming toothpaste and a low-foaming mouthwash so the toothbrush’s camera can more effectively see inside your mouth.

articles.title: Gemini Notebook agora pode puxar informações de livros que você comprou • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Gemini Notebook agora pode puxar informações de livros que você comprou
Antigo NotebookLM agora pode extrair trechos diretamente de obras compradas via Google Play Livros.
O Gemini Notebook, antigo NotebookLM, pode levantar dados diretamente dos livros disponíveis em sua biblioteca do Google Play Livros. A ferramenta, chamada Expert Intelligence, é compatível com mais de 100 mil livros oferecidos no app, e o usuário pode não só extrair trechos como também acessá-los por inteiro diretamente pela IA.
A inteligência artificial “acadêmica” do Google pode, então, realizar fichamentos, organizar gráficos e até gerar podcasts a partir de conteúdos originais, diminuindo os riscos de informações incorretas e alucinações. Isso não acaba com as chances de erro, mas é uma maneira bem interessante de evitá-los.
Segundo o The Verge, alguns usos foram demonstrados pelo diretor editorial Steve Johnson, do Google Labs. Entre os exemplos estão a criação de um livro de receitas e até sugestões de como ter uma conversa difícil com um funcionário a partir de um livro de gerenciamento de empresas.
Ao permitir a consulta diretamente via Google Play Livros, o Gemini Notebook facilita a vida do usuário, que não precisa inserir links e trechos completos na IA para receber uma resposta mais direcionada. Essa é uma das principais recomendações de especialistas para diminuir riscos de erros e alucinações, o que aumenta consideravelmente a confiança na inteligência artificial na hora de montar apresentações, planos de estudos, entre outros materiais.
O Google afirma ter trabalhado junto a autores para desenvolver controles específicos. Entre os exemplos dados, entretanto, a empresa citou apenas a limitação da consulta a livros adquiridos pelo próprio usuário, excluindo a possibilidade de acessar obras compartilhadas por algum amigo.
Recentemente, diversos vendedores de livros impressos alegaram um aumento nas compras em larga escala de títulos publicados antes de 2022 por desenvolvedoras de IA. O movimento aponta para uma confiabilidade maior em conteúdos escritos antes da presença massiva da inteligência artificial entre as produções, evitando o chamado AI Slop.
A novidade anunciada pelo Google reforça essa lógica, “limpando” a base de dados a ser analisada pela IA na hora de gerar uma resposta. Pensando no modelo voltado para usos acadêmicos, é essencial que o conteúdo gerado seja o mais assertivo possível. Mas, vale reforçar: isso não elimina totalmente a possibilidade erros e alucinações, sendo necessário sempre checar as informações e utilizar os materiais junto aos livros em questão.
